### D-WS7-062 — Scheduled draft sweep wants job infrastructure (lazy fallback shipped)

- **Tags:** `[INFRA]` `[WIZARD-DRAFT]` `[WS7-5a]` `[SWEEP]`
- **Source:** WS7-5a build, May 28, 2026. Hans preferred a scheduled sweep for abandoned wizard drafts; the prompt told CC to verify job infra first and fall back to lazy-sweep.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN. Lazy fallback is shipped and correct for WS7-5a product intent; the scheduled upgrade is the open decision.
- **Finding (VERIFIED by code read):** the api-server has **no scheduler / job-runner / cron infrastructure** — no queue or cron dependency, only comments about a future cron. Single Express app, no worker process.
- **What shipped (lazy sweep):** a per-user delete of drafts older than 30 days, as a side-effect of the wizard-drafts read; per-user scope keeps it bounded, failures swallowed so the read still proceeds.
- **The gap it leaves:** it only reclaims for users who *re-open the wizard* — a user who abandons and never returns leaves the row indefinitely. Harmless pre-launch, unbounded accumulation at scale.
- **Options (Hans to rule):** BullMQ + Redis (heaviest, most capable), in-process `node-cron` (lightest, dies with the process / no horizontal scale), or pg_cron (DB-side, no app infra). Each is a real infra commitment beyond the sweep logic — hence deferred rather than built unprompted.
- **Owner:** post-WS7 infra decision (one scheduler choice also solves the "permanent-deletion cron is post-MVP" gap). Not WS7-5b.

### D-WS7-064 — Per-day-intake macro model (long-term divisor refactor) [post-WS9]

- **Tags:** `[MACROS]` `[PLAN-REVIEW]` `[PRODUCT]` `[WS7-5]` `[POST-WS9]`
- **Source:** WS7-5a close, May 28, 2026, spun out of D-WS7-060.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN, deferred to **post-WS9.** Not in WS7 scope.
- **Current (kept) behavior:** daily average = sum of assigned-meal macros ÷ distinct assigned days; unassigned meals excluded; a mobile subtext ("Macros are calculated based on meals that have assigned days") discloses this. Ratification in D-WS7-060.
- **The long-term model Hans described:** a true per-day-intake view — each assigned day shows that day's *summed* macros (breakfast + lunch + dinner ≈1800 kcal, not one meal's ~600), plus a weekly-average-per-day rollup, plus the unassigned-meal bucket shown separately. Requires a Plan Review UI refactor, not just a divisor change.
- **Why deferred:** it changes the whole macros surface, not one number; the audience is planning dinners, not tracking diet-adherence, so the precision is lower-value pre-launch. Hans: "log a deferral for after WS9 to determine the long term plan."
- **Owner:** post-WS9 product/UX. Revisit with real data on how many users assign multiple meals per day.

### D-WS7-065 — Wizard-activation ingredient category inference is a deterministic first-pass

- **Tags:** `[MACROS]` `[GROCERY]` `[DATA-QUALITY]` `[WIZARD]` `[WS7-5b-server]`
- **Source:** WS7-5b-server build, May 28, 2026 — recording the known coarseness of the deterministic-inference-at-activation ruling.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN, deferred to a future master-data reconciliation pass. Not a bug; the acknowledged tradeoff.
- **The mechanism:** a keyword matcher maps ingredient names to the **seeded** vocabulary — `Produce | Protein | Dairy | Pantry | Bakery | Frozen` (matched exactly to the seed; no invented strings), fallback `"Pantry"`.
- **The coarseness:** no "Spices" / "Condiments" / "Oils" category exists in the seeded vocab, so **all spices, condiments, oils, vinegars and uncommon ingredients land in `"Pantry"`** — correct (it's the catch-all) but coarse; proteins all collapse to `Protein`. Acceptable pre-launch; grocery lists are still usefully grouped.
- **Why deterministic, not AI:** activation must not block on or pay for an AI call.
- **The forward-compatible fix (build-it-right, §5):** the rules array is structured so a future master-data reconciliation pass — analogous to the WS6 6c-4 `purchaseUnit` AI writeback — can re-categorize after the fact without touching the activation transaction (add keywords or invert the lookup; no call-site changes). Pairs with the nullable-until-reconciled purchase-pack fields.
- **Owner:** future data-quality / master-data reconciliation pass (post-WS7). Not 5b-mobile.

### D-WS7-067 — Wizard-activate `$transaction` write volume wants batching (timeout raised as interim insurance)

- **Tags:** `[PERF]` `[WIZARD]` `[ACTIVATION]` `[WS7-5b-server]` `[WS9]`
- **Source:** WS7-5b-server smoke-fix, May 29, 2026. The first end-to-end real-Prisma run threw P2028; root cause **verified by measurement** (§27).
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — interim timeout fix shipped; durable batching fix deferred to WS9.
- **What happened:** activate materializes the draft into a whole meal graph inside one interactive `$transaction`. **The unit tests stub Prisma, so they proved orchestration only — never real transaction behavior.** First live smoke hit **P2028**: the tx ran **5034ms against the default 5000ms** budget. Timeout confirmed by Prisma's own clock; the "missing await" hypothesis **ruled out** by a full await-audit — do not re-investigate.
- **Interim fix:** (1) **hoisted ingredient upserts OUT of the transaction** — ingredient rows are write-once reference content, so orphans on a later rollback are harmless and reused next activation; trims ~25–40 RTTs from the critical section. (2) **raised the budget** to 60s (maxWait 20s) — the post-hoist run measured the real un-clamped tx at **17,063ms** on 17 dishes, and the initial 30s pick gave only ~1.76× headroom because the first measurement was clamped at 5034ms and under-counted true work. 60s ≈ 3.5× over observed, absorbing dish-count variance.
- **The durable fix (WS9):** most remaining round-trips are per-row ingredient creates (~135) and per-step creates (~84). **Convert both loops to `createMany`** — collapses ~219 RTTs into 2 batched writes, cutting tx duration far more than any timeout number can. **The 60s budget is the band-aid until it lands.**
- **Why the timeout shipped anyway:** the smoke gate needed a genuinely-green end-to-end run; batching is a perf-durability improvement, not a correctness gate.
- **Residual UNVERIFIED (§27):** only 14- and 17-dish shapes measured; a 20+-dish tail case could approach 60s. Batching removes this risk class entirely.
- **Owner:** **WS9.** Not 5b-mobile.

### D-WS7-072 — Stale wizard-draft cleanup (resume interstitial offers un-saved drafts from prior sessions)

- **Tags:** `[UX]` `[WIZARD]` `[WS7-5b-mobile]` `[WS9]`
- **Source:** WS7-5b-mobile FIX BLOCK Phase 1, May 30, 2026 (device-test finding 4). After "Save for Later," the resume interstitial offered "pick up where you left off" with what looked like the just-saved plan. **Verified by DB inspection (§27): NOT a save-path bug** — save + activate correctly flip `isWizardDraft → false`; the offer was a *different*, stale draft row from an earlier "View Plan Details" tap that was never saved.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — diagnosed, no code change in the fix block.

- **Fix candidates (WS9):** (a) shorter TTL for never-touched drafts, (b) auto-discard a session's other drafts when one is saved/activated, (c) better interstitial disambiguation (timestamp / "1 of 3 from your last attempt"). **NOT a `decideWizardResumeUi` change** — it correctly trusts the server list.

### D-WS7-073 — Server expands the client-submitted wizard candidate with no server-side candidate registry

- **Tags:** `[SECURITY]` `[WIZARD]` `[WS7-5c]` `[WS9]`
- **Source:** WS7-5c Block A addendum, May 31, 2026 — surfaced while VERIFYING input-chaining (Hans's concern that the AI might "rebuild" a different plan than the user previewed). **Chaining is correct and identity is server-stitched**; the trace also confirmed the route trusts the client-echoed candidate.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — VERIFIED, accepted non-issue for MVP, no fix in 5c.
- **Mechanism:** the expand route takes the candidate from the request body. Candidates are stateless by design — no re-validation against a "candidate I actually generated" registry — so a tampered client could post `mealTitles` no build call returned and the server would expand them. The WS7-5a stateless-candidate trust-boundary ruling restated: "Call #2 expands the plan the user saw" holds only as far as "the client didn't tamper."
- **Why non-issue for MVP:** no incentive to tamper against your own plan generation; no multi-tenant exposure. Relevant only if candidates ever carry server-trusted state (pricing, entitlements) or abuse/cost-control needs a "real candidate" gate.
- **Fix candidates (WS9):** (a) sign the candidate on issue and verify on expand; (b) short-lived server-side registry keyed by candidateId; (c) re-derive mealTitles from the candidate's generation inputs.
- **Owner:** **WS9** (hardening).

### D-WS7-075 — Defer wizard step-generation off the blocking Save path (background/lazy materialize)

- **Tags:** `[LATENCY]` `[WIZARD]` `[SAVE]` `[SCHEMA]` `[WS7-5c]` `[WS9]`
- **Source:** WS7-5c-tail finalize fix, June 1, 2026 — two options for the ~51s finalize-steps call at Save: (A) parallelize finalize per-meal (**shipped**), or (B) defer steps off the blocking path. A read-only confirmation pass (§27) established B is materially larger.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — A shipped instead (tidy, lower-risk); B logged as the deeper future win.
- **Why B is bigger (EVIDENCED):** the expanded-plan schema requires `steps` `.min(1)`; the materializer re-parses against it and writes one step row per step inside the `$transaction`. Naive deferral hits that gate — B requires EITHER loosening to `.min(0)` + skipping the step-write loop + a backfill at first cook-view, OR splitting materialize to persist the graph with placeholder steps and write real steps via a background worker. Both land a new **"plan exists but isn't cookable yet"** data-model state. Plus an UNVERIFIED secondary question: whether the cook-view tolerates a dish with zero step rows.
- **Payoff:** Save drops further (no finalize call on the blocking path), beyond the per-meal-parallel win that took finalize ~51s → ~17s wall-clock.
- **Owner:** **WS9** (or a dedicated WS7 sub-phase if Hans wants the deeper Save win before WS7-CLOSE). Not MVP-blocking — A made Save acceptable.

### D-WS7-079 — Grocery list should refresh/reconcile when the plan changes after generation

- **Tags:** `[GROCERY]` `[PLAN-MUTATION]` `[RECONCILIATION]` `[WS7-5d]` `[WS7-7]`
- **Source:** WS7-5d Block 3 device test, June 2, 2026 — Hans generated a list, swapped a meal in the plan, reopened Groceries, list was STALE. A fresh generate rebuilds the list, but an existing list does not auto-refresh when the plan mutates.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — design resolved and foundation landed; the reconcile consumer (read-side delta computation) is **Block 4**, which closes this entry.
- **The right shape (Hans's framing):** the list should refresh and re-validate **incrementally** (reconcile only the delta), NOT regenerate from scratch. Ties to `bumpPlanRevision` — a list can track the plan `revisionId` it was generated against and reconcile when stale.
- **Why WS7-7:** that's grocery list mutations + Find Similar swap, where the incremental-update plumbing lives. **Arguably bigger than the rest of 5d combined; does not belong in a 5d bug-fix block.**
- **DESIGN RESOLVED + FOUNDATION LANDED (June 11, 2026 — WS7-7-A B1):** **Trigger:** on-read (mirrors PrepWeek's drift-detect), with a user-visible "updating your list to match plan changes" message on stale-detect (Block 5). **Result shape:** the complete consolidated plan-derived set for the meals CURRENTLY in the plan, minus extras, PLUS user-added + recurring items (**always preserved**). **Work shape:** delta-scoped — re-resolve only changed/added/removed meals; carry unchanged meals' resolved rows forward **WITHOUT re-calling AI gap-fill** (efficiency requirement). **Foundation:** an `isUserAdded` flag discriminates user-added Extras (never touched) from plan-derived rows, and a per-row multi-source provenance table means a shared ingredient (garlic from 3 meals) carries forward only if ALL its source meals are unchanged and re-resolves if ANY changed; AI-renamed/merged tail rows get zero sources → "always re-resolve" (conservative). **Check-state-through-edit preservation explicitly descoped → D-WS7-124 (WS9).** **§12.3.2 redline queued** (auto-reconcile-on-read + manual regenerate escape hatch replaces the "regenerate or use existing?" prompt).
- **Owner:** **WS7-7.**

### D-WS7-082 — `saveWizardDraft` has the same long-AI-call timeout exposure as activate (+ Android timeout asymmetry context)

- **Tags:** `[WIZARD]` `[MOBILE]` `[TIMEOUT]` `[RELIABILITY]` `[WS9]`
- **Source:** WS7-5b-followup D-WS7-080 mobile fix, June 3, 2026. Two out-of-scope findings:
  1. **`saveWizardDraft` same exposure:** save runs the same finalize-steps fan-out as activate, so it carries the same ~35s-call-with-no-client-timeout exposure. NOT fixed in the activate block because save doesn't activate — it lacks the "perceives failure → re-runs wizard → displaces own active plan" consequence, so the blast radius is lower. A "save silently appeared to fail" report would be the same root cause and the same fix.
  2. **Android-vs-iOS timeout asymmetry (diagnostic context):** **Android OkHttp's ~10s default read timeout makes a client-side abort near-certain on a ~35s call; iOS NSURLSession's 60s default only catches the long tail.** This explains the "intermittent" framing and means **any long-AI-call mobile path is far more failure-prone on Android** — relevant when triaging future long-call reports and setting defaults for new AI-backed mobile calls.
- **Proposed fix:** apply the D-WS7-080 pattern (AbortSignal + client timeout longer than the server budget) to `saveWizardDraft`, and audit any other mobile call fronting a >~10s server AI call.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — logged proactively; no save-failure symptom reported yet.
- **Owner:** **WS9.** Promote if a save-appeared-to-fail report surfaces.

### D-WS7-103 — Read-time UTC-day-granular coverage (resolver + SQL pre-filter)

- **Tags:** `[RESOLVED]` `[THIS-WEEK]` `[WS7-6-E]` `[BUG]`
- **Source:** WS7-6 (E) Block 1 rework, device-reproduced June 7, 2026.
- **Status:** ✅ RESOLVED (logic-only fix, no migration).
- **Root cause (VERIFIED):** the coverage helper compared raw instants. Mobile sends `YYYY-MM-DD`, which parses to UTC-midnight, so a plan whose `endDate` is "today" read as expired the moment `now` passed 00:00 UTC. This broke (a) the seam-B gate → no `activatedAt` stamp on a This-Week PATCH on the last day of the week, and (b) the resolver read path. ⚠️ The existing test passed only because it sent full ISO timestamps 5 days out, **never hitting the boundary mobile actually sends** (§27 scope-too-narrow test gap).
- **Resolution:** day-granular UTC comparison in **three** consumers — the shared helper, the in-memory resolver filter, and the resolver's **SQL pre-filter** (so SQL and in-memory stay aligned). CC's audit caught that third consumer; fixing the helper alone would have left 5 route sites broken. Pinned by bug-revealing tests proven fail-against-old / pass-against-new, with symmetric guards proving no over-widening.
- **Owner:** none (resolved).

Pick one semantic and rename across the stack, or split into two concepts.
- **Interim (Hans-ruled June 9):** the two options are **greyed/disabled** in dish contexts — NOT silent no-ops. (The silent-no-op pattern is how D-WS7-048 happened.)
- **Unblock path:** decide semantics → add the write path → add the sort values server-side; the keyset cursor is already sort-aware.

### D-WS7-134 — Servings-change propagation: in-place `servingsOverride` edits don't reconcile

- **Tags:** `[OPEN]` `[GROCERY]` `[RECONCILE]` `[COUPLED:D-WS7-136]`
- **Source:** WS7-7-A B4 Phase 0 + commissioning, June 12, 2026.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN → dedicated later block (WS7-7 extension or WS9; decide at scoping).
- **What it is:** a servings-override edit on a plan item whose meal stays in the plan is undetectable by B4 reconcile: the meal id is unchanged (so the id-set diff sees no add/remove) and the grocery item's source record carries no quantity, so there is no persisted baseline to diff a meal's prior contribution against. Reconcile carries the row forward and stamps the revision current; the new servings never reach the list. A fresh generate DOES reflect it.
- **Why deferred (Option A, Hans's ruling at B4 commissioning):** closing it needs a per-meal grocery-contribution signature (a per-meal content hash on the list, or quantity on the source record) + first-reconcile backfill for legacy lists. Out of B4 scope; honors the locked "reconcile via the source record" mechanism.
- **Interim mitigation:** B5's manual regenerate hatch + a visible "list may not reflect recent meal edits — regenerate" hint (same hint covers D-WS7-136).
- ⚠️ **Coupling:** the signature mechanism this needs is the SAME machinery D-WS7-136 needs. Scope and close the two together.

### D-WS7-135 — New recurring-pref items don't appear via reconcile

- **Tags:** `[OPEN]` `[WS9]` `[GROCERY]` `[RECONCILE]`

- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN → WS9 (low priority).

Narrow case, no data loss. Related family ("list state reacts to edits made after generation"): D-WS7-124, D-WS7-127/130.

### D-WS7-136 — Global meal/dish edits don't propagate to already-generated grocery lists

- **Tags:** `[OPEN]` `[GROCERY]` `[RECONCILE]` `[COUPLED:D-WS7-134]` `[PRIORITY-PATH]`
- **Source:** WS7-7-A B4, June 12, 2026 — Hans's device test (ingredient edit didn't reach the list); the initial "consolidator ignores overrides" hypothesis was corrected with code evidence per §27.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN → dedicated later block. ⚠️ Real fix NOT planned inside the remaining WS7-7-A blocks (B5 UX / B6 library buttons).
- **What it is:** "Apply always" wipes-and-recreates the dish ingredients on the same meal row but does NOT bump the revision on any plan containing it (meal edits are global / plan-agnostic; grep-confirmed). So B4 reconcile-on-read never fires and existing lists stay stale. A fresh generate DOES reflect the edit.
- **Two coupled layers to close it:** (a) bump the revision on every plan whose items reference the edited meal (cross-plan); AND (b) in-place change detection for an unchanged meal id — the SAME signature mechanism reserved for D-WS7-134, since meal-id-granularity provenance can't otherwise detect a same-meal content change.
- **Latent override dependency (conditional, not an independent ticket):** if D-WS7-090 later wires the "just this time" ingredient-override write path (an unwired stub today), the consolidator must ALSO be taught to read the override records — it ignores them entirely, so even a fresh generate wouldn't reflect a plan-scoped override.
- **Interim mitigation (B5):** visible "list may not reflect recent meal edits — regenerate" hint. Converts silent staleness to visible staleness; cheap, no mechanism needed. Chosen because this affects the highest-priority path (signup → plan → grocery list).

### D-WS7-142 — Just-this-time override model is ingredient + title only; step edits don't persist — ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 11, 2026): a step-duration edit must persist on either save choice**

- **Tags:** `[OPEN]` `[MEAL-EDITOR]` `[OVERRIDE]` `[COUPLED:D-WS7-141]`
- **Source:** WS7-7-A B5 follow-on, June 15, 2026 — surfaced in the steps round-trip trace for the D-WS7-141 fix.
- **Status:** ✅ **RULED September 11, 2026 — FALLBACK BUILDING (mobile, BUG-252), TARGET OWED.** Hans, verbatim: *"if a user adds or changes an ingredient they would know if that changes a step. I don't know why a user would have the need to change a recipe step duration once, so I don't know if that's a valid use case. but if they decide things cook better at a higher temperature for shorter or a lower temp for longer, or whatever else makes the meal better the user should be able to save the step duration. and the edit mode is the same regardless of an ingredient or step or duration. on save, the user gets prompted for 'this time, always, cancel.' the 'this time' save use case is aimed at someone subbing an allergen ingredient or other preference one week, or cooking 6 servings instead of 4 because they have guests one day. if it's easier to write to the template meal for step duration edits I am ok with doing that every time, but if we can just have them save in the meal editor and apply always or just this meal that's the target"* — **Fallback (building now):** on "Just this time" with step edits, the ingredient/title override saves as today and the step changes are written to the recipe through the "Apply always" path, with copy saying so. **Target (owed, its own block):** the override carries steps and EVERY reader of a plan item's steps merges them — Cook Mode, prep week, the plan's shown time (D-WS9-235: re-derive from the overridden steps). Surfaced again as BUG-252 on September 11. ✅ **Fallback BUILT `0a1d8d8` (September 11 evening; device-unproven).** ⚠️ **Still lost on either path: a dish ADDED in the editor and saved "Just this time" has no canonical dish to write to, so its steps go nowhere — pre-existing, part of the target.**
- **What it is (VERIFIED, §27):** the override builder emits ingredients + title only, the view-parser ignores steps, and the override read re-merges canonical steps. So **a step edit saved under "Just this time" does NOT persist**; "Apply always" DOES, via the template write. True before and after the D-WS7-141 fix. ⚠️ The ingredient-removal bug is addressed independently; this is a distinct axis.
- **Decision needed:** are per-instance step overrides in scope (extend the override schema, builder and parser to carry steps), or are step edits intentionally apply-always-only?
- **Disposition:** deferred at surfacing — folding it into the B5 follow-on would expand the override schema mid-fix.

### D-WS7-152 — Single-dish meal: suppress per-step "for {meal_name}" attribution in Cook Mode

- **Tags:** `[COOK-MODE]` `[MOBILE-RENDER]` `[ATTRIBUTION]`
- **Source:** WS7-8a Block 2b commissioning, June 17, 2026 (Hans product direction; logged early for 8b).
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN. Owner: **WS7-8b** (mobile-render only — no server change).
- **What it is:** steps carry meal attribution so the UI can show which meal a step serves ("chop 3 carrots **for the chicken noodle soup**"). **Prep the Week:** KEEP everywhere — even single-meal items — because a combined prep group can feed multiple meals. **Multi-dish meal, Cook Mode:** KEEP — several sub-recipes in flight. **Single-dish meal, Cook Mode:** SUPPRESS — every step belongs to the one dish; repeating the name is noise.
- **The rule:** suppress the suffix **only when (context = Cook Mode) AND (meal is single-dish)**. Keep it everywhere else.
- **Where it lives:** purely a **mobile rendering** decision. The server keeps attribution on every step; no server/schema change, nothing for 8a.

### D-WS7-153 — Prep-week per-step checkbox persistence + per-meal prep state + plan-level rollup

- **Tags:** `[PREP-WEEK]` `[COOK-MODE]` `[SCHEMA]` `[PERSISTENCE]`
- **Source:** WS7-8a Block 3 commissioning + build, June 18, 2026 (Hans product direction; Phase 0 audit grounded the design).
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN (in build at logging time). Owner: **WS7-8a Block 3** (server); the per-item `isPrepped` response-shape change is consumed by **8b**.
- **The problem:** prep-week steps live in a structure blob **overwritten wholesale** on regenerate, so checkbox/resume state can't live there — and steps had **no stable identity** (only a positional number, which shifts when meals are added or reordered).
- **The stable key (load-bearing Phase 0 finding):** `(phase, ingredientId)` — the engine groups by ingredient and phase-assignment is a pure function of the ingredient, so ingredient→phase is 1:1 and the key is unique-per-step and stable across regenerate. A single **`seasonings_dry#blend`** sentinel covers the collapsed dry-blend step (plan-singular per D-WS7-151).
- **Storage (build-it-right, §5):** side table `PrepStepCompletion { planId, stepKey, checkedAt }`, unique on (planId, stepKey), cascade-delete; row-presence = checked, uncheck = delete. **Chosen over a JSON column** for queryability (per-step checked-at analytics), concurrency-safety (no read-modify-write race), and declarative lifecycle. Plus a manual-override flag on the plan.
- **Per-meal prep state (derived, NOT stored):** a meal is prepped ⟺ every prep step attributed to it has a completion row. **Vacuous-prep ruling (Hans):** a meal with **zero** contributing prep steps rolls up as **prepped** — a no-prep meal is ready to cook, and zero-prep meals are NOT excluded from the denominator (a plan of all-easy meals must reach `prepped`).
- **Plan rollup + manual override:** `prepStatus` (`not_prepped`/`partial`/`prepped`) is **derived** while the manual flag is false — all prepped → `prepped`, some → `partial` ("Prepped (mostly) ✓"), none → `not_prepped`. **Manual override wins + pins:** a PATCH setting `prepStatus` (incl. end-of-session "Done") also sets the manual flag; an explicit un-mark/reset clears it, returning control to the derived rollup. The forward-only transition guard and prep-started event still gate manual transitions. ⚠️ **`partial` re-defined: per-meal mixed, NOT per-step** (PRD redline queued WS7-CLOSE).
- **Endpoints (new):** check / uncheck / read, auth + ownership-as-404, with **no** subscription check — checkbox/resume is free; the prep-week entitlement stays only on the AI-generation route.
- **Orphan-prune on regenerate:** delete completion rows whose step key isn't in the freshly assembled set — prune to the new set, NOT merge-forward blindly.
- **Cook-Mode surfacing (seam):** the cooking-sequence route is plan-agnostic (a meal lives in multiple plans) — ⚠️ threading a plan id in would be the wrong seam. Per-meal prepped state is surfaced on the **plan-scoped reads** Cook Mode launches from instead.
- **8b consumes (flag for 8a-CLOSE handoff):** (a) per-item `isPrepped` defaults the "did you prep this?" prompt; (b) the **mise-en-place recap** is built 8b-side from existing prep-step text filtered by meal attribution — NO new AI, NO new server field; (c) ⚠️ cook-step quantity/qualifier text ("2 cups diced") must NOT be stripped — it's the recovery path when a user marked prepped but missed a step; (d) prep-prompt copy is 8b UI copy.

### D-WS7-154 — Pre-existing: prep-week result validator throws on sub-4-phase input instead of returning `success:false`

- **Tags:** `[PREP-WEEK]` `[VALIDATION]` `[PRE-EXISTING]` `[TEST-RED]`
- **Source:** WS7-8a Block 3 Sub-block A, June 18, 2026 (CC surfaced during the B3 test run).
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN. Owner: **TBD** (out of B3 scope). Candidate for a WS7-CLOSE validation sweep.
- **What it is:** the refinement loops the first four phases with no bound guard, so a result with fewer than 4 phases throws a TypeError instead of returning a clean `success:false`; the negative test is therefore red. ⚠️ **Pre-existing, VERIFIED — not introduced by B3:** CC stashed its B3 changes and re-ran; the test crashes identically on the pre-B3 HEAD.
- **Why deferred:** harmless in production — the assembly path only ever produces exactly 4 phases (empty phases still emitted), so sub-4-phase input never occurs at runtime. Purely validator robustness + the red negative test.
- **Fix when picked up:** add a length/bound guard before the phase loop. Re-greens the negative test.

### D-WS7-155 — `prepStatus` PATCH bumps the plan revision → extra prep-week regenerate (benign under stable keys)

- **Tags:** `[PREP-WEEK]` `[CACHE]` `[OBSERVATION]` `[PRE-EXISTING-BEHAVIOR]`
- **Source:** WS7-8a Block 3 build, June 18, 2026 (CC surfaced at audit; not a B3-introduced defect).
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN. Owner: **TBD** — logged for tracking, not action; revisit only if regenerate cost becomes a concern.
- **What it is:** `prepStatus` counts as a changed field on the plan PATCH (pre-existing), so any write to it bumps the plan revision and stales the prep-week structure cache. B3 makes this fire more often because end-of-session "Done" is a `prepStatus` write.
- **Why benign under B3:** the stable-key design means completions survive a regenerate — orphan-prune keeps every step key still in the assembled set, and keys are position-independent. No data loss; cost is one extra (cheap) regenerate.
- **Why not fixed in B3:** narrowing the changed-field set changes shared plan-mutation semantics — out of B3's blast radius and riskier than the symptom (other consumers rely on revision drift detection). Benign-under-stable-keys means there is no functional bug; a note for future cost-tuning only.

### D-WS7-183 — Mixed blend step (make-ahead spice mix + at-cook dredge in one `isBlend` step) can't be cleanly demoted from prep

- **Tags:** `[WEEK-PREP]` `[ASSEMBLY]` `[NARRATION]` `[AT-COOK-RULE]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b Block 4 prep-week aggregation fixes, CC Phase 0, July 1, 2026 (confirmed against the live tree; Hans ruled defer).
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN → owner WS9 (promote to WS7 if fresh-data device-testing shows it actually occurring). Low.
- The engine collapses all `seasonings_dry` components on a dish into ONE `isBlend` step and `skipSuggested` is all-or-nothing per step. FIX 3's at-cook rule demotes a dredge/breading blend out of prep when a recipe step applies it <~20 min before cooking — reachable for a **single-dish** dredge. But when a blend collapses a genuine make-ahead spice mix and an at-cook dredge into one step, that step is half-prep / half-cook and can't be demoted as a unit without hiding the legitimate make-ahead prep.
- **Accepted behavior (Hans-ruled): leave the mixed blend in prep** — it may tell the user to dredge during prep. Judged rare: needs a spice-blend dish and a dredge dish sharing the collapse in the same plan-week.
- **Fix (if ever wanted):** an assembly carve-out (don't fold a demotable at-cook dredge into a shared blend step) OR per-component skip granularity. Deliberately NOT built — narration defaults **loud** (keep-in-prep when uncertain), so the mixed case lands on the accepted outcome without a carve-out. If FIX 3's wording can't keep single-dish demotion working without mis-demoting a mixed blend, CC stops and surfaces rather than silently under- or over-fixing.
- **Cross-ref:** the single-dish dredge case (the FIX-3 headline for items 1.3/1.5/1.7) is handled in wording, in scope this block.

### D-WS7-184 — Demoted prep steps: "omit + server-exclude" REVERSES the WS7-8a B3 "flag-don't-drop" ruling

- **Tags:** `[WEEK-PREP]` `[SERVER]` `[ROLLUP]` `[REVERSAL]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b Block 1 commissioning, July 2, 2026. Device-testing showed demoted steps rendering muted; Hans ruled omit-entirely, forcing the server-side reversal.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN → owner **WS7-8b Block 2** (server rollup threading, not yet commissioned). The render-omit half + the narration demotion rule are Block 1.
- **What it reverses:** WS7-8a B3 ruled **"flag-don't-drop"** — demoted/skip-suggested steps stay in the required-set, flagged not removed. Now **REVERSED**: the AI-free server `isPrepped` derivation must **EXCLUDE** `skipSuggested` steps from the required-set entirely. **Reason (VERIFIED at CC Phase 0):** render-hiding demoted steps in the VM alone means their keys never get written (the "Done with phase" batch pulls keys from the VM), so any meal with a demoted step can never reach `isPrepped` and the Cook gate nags forever. **Omit-on-render REQUIRES server-exclude to be correct; the two are coupled.** The threading mechanism (persist `skipSuggested` per stepKey, read from cached structure, or reuse Block 1's demotion signal) is scoped in Block 2's Phase 0 hard-STOP.
- **⚠️ Guard:** a mixed blend (D-WS7-183, ruled keep-in-prep) must NOT be excluded from the required-set — it stays required because it stays prep. Block 2 Phase 0 confirms this.
- **Cross-ref:** BUG-013, BUG-015; D-WS7-183; D-WS7-185 (defines what "demoted" means).

### D-WS7-185 — Canonical demotion rule: combines-into-a-mix = KEEP; standalone-into-nothing = DEMOTE

- **Tags:** `[WEEK-PREP]` `[NARRATION]` `[ASSEMBLY]` `[CANONICAL-RULE]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b Block 1 commissioning, July 2, 2026. Cross-ref BUG-014.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN → owner **WS7-8b Block 1**. Becomes a locked behavioral rule at Block 1 close.
- **The rule (Hans-ruled):** a single-ingredient measure that combines **INTO** a marinade / sauce / dressing / seasoning blend = **KEEP** (stays prep); a **standalone** single measure combining into nothing (oil → pan) = **DEMOTE**. Hans's hard constraint: do not ask the user to pre-measure 2 tbsp oil days ahead of cooking.
- **Mechanism:** reads the new **`dishRole`** structural signal, threaded from the meal-dish link's role label through to the prep contribution (zero query change). `dishRole ∈ {sauce, topping, base}` → KEEP; a lone cooking-fat in a `main`/`side` dish that `relevantSteps` shows poured into a pan → DEMOTE; `relevantSteps` is the fallback when role is ambiguous. `dishRole` is the shared assembly-membership signal (serves this rule AND D-WS7-186's grouping); **NOT** `SAUCE_NAME_HINTS`.
- **⚠️ 183 guard:** `isBlend` steps are explicitly EXCLUDED from demotion — the "do not demote a mixed blend" carve-out stays dominant. Safe by construction (Phase 0 + dry-run verified).
- **Sub-mechanism (audit-surfaced, §3):** the **`blendSpiceDish?` code-owned field** is stamped on a grouped sauce step only when that dish's dry spices truly survive into the collapsed blend (3+ per-dish survivors); the mandatory linkage wording ("combine … with the [Special Sauce] spices from your seasoning blend") emits ONLY when the field is present, so it never points at spices that aren't there.
- **Cross-ref:** BUG-014; D-WS7-186 (shared signal + grouping); D-WS7-183 (mixed-blend guard).

### D-WS7-186 — Full-sauce single step (5b) deferred; Option-A grouping shipped instead

- **Tags:** `[WEEK-PREP]` `[ASSEMBLY]` `[PRD-CANDIDATE]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b Block 1 commissioning, July 2, 2026. Cross-ref BUG-015.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN → owner **TBD** (PRD-candidate). Low, TBD-pending-usage.
- The stranded-vinegar fix shipped as **Option A (5a)** — group `sauces_marinades` by `dishId` so a sauce's wet parts land in one step, dry spices stay in the collapsed seasoning blend, bridged by the `blendSpiceDish` linkage wording (D-WS7-185). **5b** — pulling ALL of a sauce dish's ingredients cross-phase into one "make the whole sauce" step — was **NOT built**: it breaks the fixed 4-phase model (which phase would it live in? violates seasonings-first/proteins-last ordering) and re-opens the D-WS7-183 blend guard. Hans: 5b may be better UX "but that's still TBD based on actual usage."
- **Ruling (Hans):** ship 5a now; defer 5b as a PRD-candidate. If device-testing shows the blend-then-sauce two-step reconstruction confuses users, promote 5b to a workstream — it's a phase-model change + PRD redline, not a fix-block change.
- **Cross-ref:** BUG-015; D-WS7-183 (4-phase + blend integrity); D-WS7-185 (the linkage that makes 5a's two-step reconstruction clear).

### D-WS7-189 — Chunked prep narration (residual truncation headroom past 16384 tokens)

- **Tags:** `[WEEK-PREP]` `[AI]` `[DEFERRED]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b BUG-022, July 4, 2026. Prep narration runs the whole week in one call and passed no `maxTokens`, so it ran on the 4096 default and truncated mid-steps on a heavy plan → parsed to `{}` → 502. Fixed by passing a named 16384 max-tokens constant, with a regression test asserting the raised ceiling.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — owner **TBD** (WS7-CLOSE triage or later). P3.

Not scheduled — 16384 covers realistic heavy plans (~30–50 steps) with headroom, and Sonnet 4.6 supports 64K output if the constant needs another bump first.

### D-WS7-190 — `wantsLeftovers` deprecate-or-reuse (removed from UI, backend retained)

- **Tags:** `[PREFERENCES]` `[WIZARD]` `[UX]` `[SCHEMA-LATER]`
- **Source:** Hans ruling July 6, 2026 — an early-idea preference that doesn't meaningfully shape generation; pull it from the screen now, decide deprecate-vs-reuse later.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — **UI removal + neutralization DONE** (Cookbook Phase B, July 10, 2026). The field is **inert** and the reuse design is RULED; only the deprecate-vs-reuse call remains. Owner: post-launch / catalog-workstream commissioning. Not blocking.
- **Current state:** field kept in schema but **neutralized** — control removed from onboarding, Preferences and both wizard screens and dropped from their inputs and payloads, **schema default flipped `@default(true)` → `@default(false)`**. Servings math is exactly `householdSize` for every user. The prompt-body servings line was left **untouched** — it already produces the correct result when false, so no reseed was needed.
- **⚠️ Why the default had to flip:** with no UI control, leaving `@default(true)` would have **silently turned leftover-inflation ON for every new user** — the opposite of pulling the feature. Removing a toggle is not the same as neutralizing a field; both were required.
- **⚠️ Behavior note (unresolved, low-stakes):** PRD §5.7 says `servings = householdSize + (1-2 if leftovers)`, i.e. the published NUMBER inflates — but a device test with `wantsLeftovers: true` showed **4 servings for a household of 4**. Either the per-run value (D-WS7-035) defaulted it off at generation, or the servings line wasn't taking effect. **Not chased** — the field is inert, so it's moot for shipping. Flagged rather than asserted (§27).
- **Reuse design RULED (Hans, July 10, 2026) — if ever revived:** published **servings stays = `householdSize`** and **per-serving macros/math are unchanged**; the leftover intent is expressed by **scaling ingredient quantities up by 1-2 servings behind the scenes**. Hans: *"you're making 4 servings, the macros and math per serving doesn't change because it knows behind the scenes the user wants another serving or two left over, and the user just cooks more food than they need for 4."* **This REPLACES the PRD §5.7 contract**; redline queued if/when revived, not applied now. Better because it keeps the servings label honest and per-serving macros stable — inflating the number makes both lie.

### D-WS7-191 — USDA backfill CSV doesn't round-trip `foodCategory` → `--apply` writes `foodCategory: null` on matched rows

- **Tags:** `[USDA]` `[BACKFILL]` `[METADATA]` `[MINOR]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b USDA arc Block 2, July 5–6, 2026. The dry-run CSV has no `foodCategory` column, so `--apply` writes the match shape with `foodCategory: null`; reactively-enriched rows DO carry it.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — low priority.

### D-WS7-192 — USDA backfill whole-file abort on transient failure has no resume-from-offset

- **Tags:** `[USDA]` `[BACKFILL]` `[RESILIENCE]` `[SCALE-LATER]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b USDA arc Block 2, July 5–6, 2026; refined at BUG-028 close.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — low priority.
- On a *transient* USDA failure (429/5xx/network/timeout) the backfill aborts, keeps the partial CSV, and is re-runnable from the top — but with no resume-from-offset a failure at row 300 of 383 re-processes rows 1–299. BUG-028 removed the *deterministic-400* abort (now a per-row MISS), so one un-searchable name no longer kills the run; the transient abort stands and is the correct conservative choice — **don't record a transient blip as a false MISS.** Fine at 383 rows; only matters if the catalog grows large. **Fix if ever wanted:** resume-from-offset or checkpoint the last-processed ingredient.

### D-WS7-193 — Unit-normalization data-quality (`defaultUnit` + `DishIngredient.unit` free-text)

- **Tags:** `[DATA-QUALITY]` `[UNITS]` `[POST-LAUNCH]` `[PREREQ-FOR-DETERMINISTIC-MACROS]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b USDA arc; Hans ruling July 6, 2026.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — **post-launch, low-priority. NOT MVP, NOT go-live.** Revisit ~10K users.
- `DishIngredient.unit` is free-text with ~33 distinct values including junk (`to_taste`, `large`, `"6 oz"`, ~24 empty-string units); `defaultUnit` is similarly un-normalized. This blocks any future *deterministic* (non-AI) gram-conversion layer, which needs clean units.
- **Why it's safe to defer (Hans ruling, VERIFIED-mechanism / device-confirmation-pending):** USDA grounding is **gram-bounded** — the AI still does the quantity→grams conversion and the per-100g value scales against *that*. So a per-100g outlier (cooking spray at 792 cal/100g) does **NOT** inflate a meal total unless the AI assigns a crazy gram weight, which is pre-existing behavior grounding didn't change — a can of PAM does not add 870 cal unless the AI thinks you're eating a can of PAM. **⚠️ Device-confirmation pending:** spot-check a spray/spice-heavy meal for a sane (single-digit-ish cal) contribution to move this from verified-mechanism to verified-in-practice (§27).
- **Fix if ever done:** normalize both fields to a canonical unit vocabulary + build the quantity→grams table. Prerequisite for D-WS7-194.

### D-WS7-194 — Deterministic ingredient-level macro computation (scale-phase cost optimization)

- **Tags:** `[USDA]` `[MACROS]` `[COST]` `[SCALE-LATER]` `[OPTIONAL]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b USDA arc, Ruling 1's deferred half, July 5, 2026. Hans verbatim: *"be sure this is a logged future phase at scale cost cutting optional item."*
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — **scale-phase, optional. Acceptable as-is until ~10K users** (Hans, July 6: *"$130/month at 1k users is entirely acceptable... probably not worth revisiting until more like 10k users"*).
- Dish macros are AI-estimated (Haiku), now USDA-*grounded* per-ingredient but still summed by the model. A fully *deterministic* computation (USDA per-100g × normalized grams, no AI call for the sum) would save ~$130–150/mo at 1K users — an accepted cost, only material at ~10K scale.
- **Prereq:** unit normalization + a quantity→grams layer (D-WS7-193). Can't go deterministic without clean units.

### D-WS7-196 — Grocery cross-sourcing: derive a listed ingredient from another already on the list (e.g. lemon juice from lemons)

- **Tags:** `[GROCERY]` `[NET-NEW]` `[BUG-025-4]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b grocery cluster Phase 0, July 8, 2026. Split out of **BUG-025** as sub-item **25-4** — a device test showed "1 bottle (15 oz) lemon juice · 5 tablespoon" as its own buy-item while the list already carried whole lemons.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — **deferred (net-new logic, not an MVP bug-fix).** The other four BUG-025 sub-items (25-1 purchase-size math, 25-2 fractional-ceil, 25-3 recurring-unit, 25-5 staples-variant) ARE in-scope Block B fixes; only cross-sourcing defers. Owner: post-MVP, when the grocery-quality surface is next opened.
- **Why it's not a fix:** verified at Phase 0 (grep, not hypothesis) — consolidation buckets on `(canonical, unit)` only, and there is **no ingredient→derived-form graph, no ratio/equivalence table, and no post-AI substitution/merge layer** anywhere in the code. Fixing it means building a derivation engine — which derivables map to which source produce, at what ratios, plus the "use N lemons instead of a bottle?" decision UX. A feature, not a bug patch; pulling it into the cluster would be a "while we're in there" scope violation (§3).

### D-WS7-198 — Expand-stage preference resolution: server resolves `client ?? stored` once, used at BOTH generate and expand (AMENDS the Block-2 stored-overwrite design)

- **Tags:** `[WIZARD]` `[AI]` `[PREFERENCES]` `[COOKBOOK-PHASE-B]` `[AMENDMENT]`
- **Source:** Cookbook Phase B Blocks 2 → 4, July 9-10, 2026. Block 2 wired the four Phase-B prefs (`discoveryMealsPerWeek`, `saucePreference`, `maxCookTimeMinutes`, `maxCookTimeCoverage`) into generation via a server-loaded preferences bag; because the expand-candidate context is 100% client-supplied and passed through verbatim, Block 2 ruled that expand must **overwrite** sauce + cook-time from stored `UserPreferences` rather than trust a client echo — correct then, since the client had no legitimate reason to send those values.
- **The conflict (Block 4 Phase 0, §27 catch by CC):** Block 4 built the per-run override layer (D-WS7-035), giving the client a **legitimate** per-run value. The unconditional overwrite would **silently revert** a per-run cook-cap/sauce override, so it would shape candidate *titles* but not the *expanded recipe* — where times and ingredients are actually authored. The feature would have been mostly cosmetic.
- **Decision (Hans, July 10, 2026):** **AMEND the Block-2 design.** The server **resolves the effective preference once** (`client per-run ?? stored`, per field) and uses **that same resolved bag at both generate and expand** — preserving the server-authoritative intent while accounting for a legitimate per-run override.
- **Status:** ✅ RESOLVED — built in Block 4 as a shared pure resolver folded into the existing preferences bag, so **prompt bodies were unchanged and no reseed was needed**; expand calls the resolver instead of overwriting. Discovery is generate-only, not carried to expand.
- **⚠️ Presence-check, not `??`:** the resolver uses `!== undefined`, NOT nullish coalescing. `null ?? stored` would wrongly discard an explicit `null` cap ("No limit **this plan**") and silently inherit the stored cap; the presence check makes null-the-value distinguishable from omitted-the-field. **Load-bearing — do not "simplify" it to `??`.**
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS7-035 (the per-run override layer this amendment serves).

### D-WS7-199 — Brand names in `store_bought` sauce, gated on retailer-ordering

- **Tags:** `[AI]` `[PREFERENCES]` `[GROCERY]` `[RETAILER-PHASE]` `[COOKBOOK-PHASE-B]`
- **Source:** Cookbook Phase B Block 2 ruling, July 8, 2026.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — not MVP. Tied to the deferred retailer phase (§9: retailer integrations deferred until Instacart developer-program access). Owner: retailer phase, at Instacart adapter commissioning.

### D-WS7-200 — Kiwi Community Cookbook: require the meal's Edit button to have been pressed before a URL-imported recipe can be shared publicly

- **Tags:** `[COOKBOOK]` `[IP-RISK]` `[SHARING]` `[v1-STOPGAP]`
- **Source:** Hans, July 10, 2026 (WS7-8b Block B1 close session).
- **The decision (two parts):** (1) **Naming ratified: "Kiwi Community Cookbook"** — "Community" signals **user-generated** content, setting the expectation that these recipes are not Kiwi-authored and reinforcing the legal posture: a community *sharing space*, not Kiwi *republishing* third-party content. (2) **The gate:** before publishing a **URL-imported** meal, the meal's **Edit button must have been pressed at least once**. **Track only that the button was pressed** — do NOT require or verify that an ingredient or step actually *changed*; a single boolean per meal, set on first press, unlocks sharing. Hans's reasoning: content diffs are expensive to build and police, while the button-press is cheap, adds friction and creates a paper trail — *"a little protection to say I tried to protect IP if the app scales rapidly while someone complains."*
- **⚠️ HONESTY NOTE — this is a FRICTION/PAPER-TRAIL gate, NOT meaningful IP protection. Logged explicitly so no future reader mistakes it for a solved problem.** A user can press Edit, change nothing, and publish a byte-identical copy of a copyrighted recipe. "We required an edit-button press" is **not** a defense that would withstand a serious content-creator complaint. **Both parties acknowledged it as thin at logging time.**
- **Status:** 🟢 **RULED as the v1 stopgap — knowingly accepted as weak.** Hans: ship the thin gate now as partial cover during early scaling, **then design a robust plan while evaluating the feature overall.** A conscious risk-acceptance, not a misunderstanding.
- **🔴 COMPANION OPEN ITEM (the real work, NOT resolved here):** a genuine IP posture still needs designing. Candidates, none decided: a **DMCA-style takedown process** (the industry-standard protection); **attribution / source-URL retention** surfaced on the shared recipe; **ToS** language placing publishing responsibility on the user; possibly **disallowing public sharing of URL-imported meals entirely**; real **change-detection** (diff vs. the imported original) if the button-press proves insufficient. **Owner:** Cookbook workstream — a **definition-track ruling**, no code commissioned here. The v1 gate implements whenever public sharing is built; the companion item wants its own decision session **before** the Cookbook opens to real users at any scale.
- **Cross-ref:** URL Import best-effort posture (WS6 6c-1, D-WS6-041, PRD §10.3.1 / §10.3.4 / §10.9) — this entry covers what happens to imported content *downstream* when a user republishes it.

### D-WS7-202 — WS7-11 (Favorites, Saves, Ratings): the post-cook feedback loop gets its own workstream, built on the WS9 design system

- **Owner:** **WS7-11** (new workstream). **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — RULED (scope + sequencing); definition work pending.** **Date:** July 13, 2026 (WS7-8b close).
- **Origin:** Hans — *"at the end of cooking a meal, there's no 'done' or real end to it. the user has to back out of cook mode."* Cook Mode's step list simply **ends**, so cooking a meal through and abandoning it halfway are, to the app, **the identical gesture**.
- **THE SEQUENCING RULING (Hans):** **pulled OUT of WS7-8b; deferred until AFTER the WS9 restyle** — the completion screen is **net-new** and WS9 restyles every screen, so building it now means **designing it twice**. **WS9 → WS7-11 → sharing-lite.**
- **THE SCOPE (four things that are really one — "what happens after you cook, and what the product learns from it"):** (1) **cook completion screen** (PRD §13.5.7 + §13.10.1); (2) **star rating (1–5)**, **needs a schema field**, mounted on the completion screen *and* **Meal Detail** (Hans: *"meal detail should have the rating option for a user to rate a meal at a later time… 'oh, I cooked this last week and it was great'"*); (3) **favorites**, **needs a surfacing decision**; (4) the **`timesCooked` / `lastCookedAt` write path**, adopting **D-WS7-111**'s dead columns.
- **RULING — Done is the only button.** §13.5.7 and §13.10.1 each specify *"two buttons"* and name **different pairs** ("Back to Plan" | "Done" vs. "Save updates" | "Skip"), so built verbatim the screen has **four buttons and two competing exits**. Hans ruled **one button, "Done," → routes to Meal Detail.** Stars save on tap; time/difficulty edits stage locally and commit on exit. **Touch nothing, tap Done → nothing is written — that *is* "Skip,"** so no Skip button. "Back to Plan" is dropped: Meal Detail already has a nav stack under it, and Cook Mode also launches from the **Library** with no `planId`, so it would be dead half the time. **⚠️ The back arrow must behave identically to Done** — otherwise a user sets 50 minutes, hits back, and it silently evaporates.
- **RULING — `timesCooked` increments on DONE, not on Cook-tap.** Tapping **Cook Now** only means *"I'm going to attempt this"* — the intent abandoned when the kid melts down at step 3. Counting on **launch** inflates the number with meals nobody ate and **corrupts the one thing you'd want it for** (*"show me my staples"*): a meal you started and bailed on is the **opposite** of a staple. **The completion screen is the write point.**
- **THE FAVORITES DISTINCTION (Hans's catch — the load-bearing insight):** three concepts, only two controls today. **Saved** = *"this is in my library"* — the **heart** (PRD §9.5: on a public card it is the **save-to-my-library** control), an **acquisition** gesture, **not a rating**. **Rated** = *"it was good"* — net-new stars, retrospective quality. **Favorite** = *"this is a staple; put it in front of me when I'm planning"* — **forward-looking intent**, neither of the other two.
  **Why stars CANNOT subsume favorites:** a **5-star** meal can be a once-a-year showpiece — great, not a staple; a **3-star** meal the kids will actually eat on a Tuesday is **exactly** a favorite. **Quality and reach-for-it-ness are uncorrelated.** Hans verbatim: *"this is a 4 star meal, but it's easy and my kids love it, save it as a favorite if I want to add to a plan because it's a staple meal."*
  **⚠️ Two chat-Claude errors corrected here, both by Hans (§3/§27 — recorded so they don't recur):** (a) framing heart-vs-stars as *"two rating mechanisms that collide"* and leaning toward **stars subsuming the heart** — **that would have deleted the save button**; the codebase disagreed with the framing. (b) then leaning toward stars subsuming **favorites** — wrong for the reason above (treating a rating as a proxy for intent).
  **⚠️ The PRD contradicts itself on the heart:** one section says *"No separate UserFavorite table needed"*, another refers to *"removes the favorite (UserFavorite record)."* One is stale. **Verify against running code, not the PRD, at WS7-11 Phase 0.**
- **THE OPEN QUESTION (definition work — NOT yet ruled):** **favorites must *do* something or they are decoration** — the value is in the planning loop. Candidates: a **Favorites filter/sort on My Meals**; **wizard bias** (seed/weight generation toward favorites — a **prompt-contract change**, not a UI change); **add-to-plan pickers** with favorites pinned to top. *A favorite toggle that visibly does nothing is worse than no toggle.* **Rule this before commissioning.**
- **PRD redline REQUIRED (§13.10.2 `[SCHEMA]` note is WRONG):** it claims *"No new fields required"* because it only contemplated `estimatedTimeMinutes` and `difficulty`, which already exist on `Meal`. **It forgot the stars** — there is nowhere on `Meal` to store a 1–5 rating. WS7-11 needs a **migration** (rating + favorite + cook-tracking, likely one).
- **⚠️ Fork-on-calibrate (do NOT miss this):** §13.10.2 requires that editing time/difficulty on a **curated/public** meal *"creates a user-owned copy if one doesn't exist"* and that *"the post-cook prompt also creates the user copy."* So **rating/calibrating an unsaved curated meal must FORK it.** The machinery **already exists** (**D-WS7-139** fork-on-acquire, gated on not-already-owned, wired at add-to-plan / use-template / meal-swap) — **reuse it, don't reinvent it.** This is the one part of WS7-11 that can **corrupt shared catalog data** if done wrong: never write a personal rating to a `userId: null` row.
- **Cross-ref:** **D-WS7-203** (thumbs ruling), **D-WS7-204** (D-WS7-111 dead columns), D-WS7-139, BUG-018, PRD §13.5.7 / §13.7 / §13.10. Named by Hans: **"Favorites, Saves, Ratings."**

### D-WS7-203 — Rule the sharing-lite thumbs (like/dislike) against the WS7-11 star rating BEFORE sharing ships
- **Owner:** WS7-11 (rule it) → sharing-lite / Cookbook Phase D (consumes it). **Status:** ⚠️ **SUPERSEDED by D-WS7-211** (stars only; thumbs retired). **Date:** July 13, 2026.
- **The collision is not heart-vs-stars — it is stars-vs-thumbs:** sharing-lite specs *"Dislike: thumbs-down, label 'Not for me.'"*; WS7-11 introduces 1–5 stars. Two quality signals on **different scales**, meeting on the Cookbook browse surface. Free to reconcile before sharing ships; after, it is a data migration on public content. **§27:** the thumbs were specced **before stars existed** — reconcilable, not a locked ruling.
- **chat-Claude's lean (NOT a ruling):** stars subsume the public thumbs. **BUT the dislike may have a second job** — feeding *"Not for me"* into recommendation suppression. **Check what the dislike actually feeds before ruling;** if it drives suppression it isn't redundant and can't simply be deleted.
- **Why WS7-11 sequences BEFORE sharing:** WS7-11 is the private half of the feedback loop (what a rating, a favorite and "I cooked this" mean against your own library); sharing exposes those primitives publicly. Build sharing first and you ship thumbs, then reconcile.
- **Notes:** naming LOCKED ("the Kiwi Cookbook," Hans, July 6, 2026); Phase D slotted **"with or after the WS9 restyle so it's built once in the new visual language."**
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS7-211 (supersedes) · D-WS7-202 · D-WS7-200 · roadmap row 7 · PRD §9.5.

### D-WS7-206 — `saveMutationLimiter` is a module-global IP-keyed bucket: any new test file adding `POST /me/meals` cases will 429
- **Owner:** Test infra / any block touching `POST /me/meals`. **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN (mitigated).** **Date:** July 13, 2026 (BUG-018 B1). **CC-flagged.**
- **The sharp edge:** a **module-global bucket keyed by IP + method + path** (no `keyFn`), **capacity 12**. The canonical save test was already at the ceiling; added POST cases pushed a downstream case into a 429. **Any future test file adding these cases hits the same shared bucket, and the failure surfaces as an unrelated-looking 429 in a different test.** Mitigated by a test-only store reset (`__clearRateLimitStoreForTests()` + `beforeEach`), zero runtime change.
- **⚠️ The instructive part (§27 working):** CC's first fix — isolating on a separate `userId` — was **WRONG** (the key is IP), and CC caught and reverted it itself. Recorded because **the wrong fix is the intuitive one.**

### D-WS9-043 — Catalog SPINE: the harness generates against a curated target-dish LIST (top ~600 most-popular US non-breakfast meals), not a preference-profile spread — supersedes D-WS9-041's profile-as-variety-engine

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[ARC]` `[WS-GEN]` `[STORE]` `[BLOCK-3]` `[HARNESS]` `[CATALOG]`
- **Source:** Block 3 1B pilot dry-run (July 18, 2026) — 12 attempted / 10 produced. **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN** — ruled, unbuilt. **⚠️ ID note:** minted as -042, **renumbered to -043** on reconcile — the parallel definition track consumed -042 in the same window (live §29.2 collision).
- **The finding that forced it:** the dry-run produced **4 distinct dinners presented as 8** — every omnivore profile converged on **chicken thighs** across four cuisines. **The dedup key did not fail;** normalized-title worked, and the model regenerated the same dish under a cosmetically different name that legitimately passed. **"Different titles mean variety" does not hold** — convergence is the model reaching for the most-probable dish per cuisine when nothing tells it what to make. At that rate 600 calls buy ~60 real meals and 540 near-clones, and **no structural checklist catches it** (every duplicate passes protein-completeness, timings, ordering, the BUG-040 gate).
- **The reframe (Hans's — it dissolves rather than patches):** the harness is **not doing discovery**; the catalog should hold **the most-cooked dinners in the US.** With a target dish name as input **convergence is structurally impossible** — each call has a distinct target and **the dish-name list IS the variety mechanism.** Accepted as **brute-force over logic-creating.**
- **⚠️ GRANULARITY RULE (load-bearing — Hans's burger point):** the list is **dishes at variant granularity, not categories.** "Burger" is NOT one entry — **smash, pub/fancy and standard** are different meals with different ingredients, techniques and audiences; same for tacos, mac and cheese, chicken sandwiches, pizza. **Granularity decides whether 600 entries yields 600 real meals or ~300 plus ~300 collisions.**
- **Popularity-ranked, not taste-curated:** Saag Paneer isn't a bad meal, just not what most US households cook on a Tuesday; ranking handles that automatically. **Geography is a phase axis:** a future market seeds **its own list** — the harness is list-driven, so a new market is a new list, not new code.
- **THE RULING — LIST SOURCING = OPTION 3 (hybrid) WITH HANS'S EDITORIAL PASS.** AI-generate the ranked list in a one-time chunked pass with the granularity rule in the prompt, **spot-check the top slice against a real public source** (free recall drifts toward what food media *writes about* rather than what is *cooked*, plus tail duplicates like "Spaghetti Bolognese" / "Spaghetti with Meat Sauce"), **then Hans reviews and edits before freeze.** Rejected: pure AI-generate + review (thinner grounding); fully external-data-sourced (sourcing cost, paywall/scrape shape). The list becomes a **checked-in constant. Anti-padding rule: better ~450 genuinely distinct dishes, stated as such, than 600 padded with near-duplicates.**
- **What it supersedes in D-WS9-041:** the preference-profile spread as the **variety engine**, plus the two dry-run variety fixes (exclusion-list of generated titles; profile-axis widening) — **both unnecessary. STANDING:** direct meal-gen (not plan-harvest), the finalize-steps quality stage, dish-owned steps, BUG-040 pre-validation, the protein/entrée check, allergen stamping, cache discipline. **Preference profiles do not disappear** — they still parameterize *how* a dish is generated (servings, difficulty); they stop being the variety mechanism. **Cache impact: none** — the target dish name goes in the **volatile** block.
- **Also carried:** ⚠️ **`promptVersion: null` on every harness call** (keys live in the in-memory registry, not seeded per §7) — a **real telemetry gap at 600**; seed before the scale run. ⚠️ **Allergen false-positive:** a *vegan* bowl stamped `egg` — not blocking, we stamp rather than filter. ⚠️ **Near-duplicate dedup stays a backstop** — loosening it to fuzzy matching was rejected as the primary mechanism (**paying for generations you throw away is the expensive way to get variety**).
- **Pilot economics:** 10 meals / 22 AI calls, **73.2% cache hit, $0.0616/meal**; both prefixes cleared the Sonnet 4.6 2048-token floor as measured.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-041 (the harness shape this amends) · D-WS9-040 (this defect class is what its checklist *cannot* catch) · D-WS9-037 · arc scope §4 Block 3.

### D-WS9-044 — The catalog list names the MAIN, not the meal: target dish = centerpiece, harness composes the complete dinner around it + a structural "main-only" reject

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[ARC]` `[WS-GEN]` `[STORE]` `[BLOCK-3]` `[HARNESS]` `[CATALOG]` `[QUALITY-GATE]`
- **Source:** Hans's editorial review of the 548-row list, July 18, 2026. **Status:** ✅ **BUILT** (Block 3).
- **The finding:** rows like "Grilled Salmon" and "Chicken Tenders" are *dishes*, not meals. Hans: *"I just don't want the AI plan generation to snag only grilled salmon and suggest eating a piece of salmon for Tuesday's dinner."* **Structural, not stray rows: 40+ bare-main entries in the top 100 alone.**
- **The ruling: the LIST is fine; the generation contract was under-specified.** The cached prefix states the target dish is the **centerpiece** and the harness **composes a complete dinner around it**, PLUS a structural **`main_only_no_accompaniment` reject** so a lone protein cannot be written to the store.
- **Rejected:** rewriting entries into meal-shaped names ("Grilled Salmon with Rice Pilaf and Asparagus") — hardcodes sides, kills accompaniment variety, and blocks D-WS9-045, which depends on accompaniments being free to vary.
- **⚠️ Why it belongs in the CHECK, not only the prompt — same class as the chicken-thigh convergence:** a lone salmon fillet passes **every** structural gate while being **wrong as a dinner. Prompt-only fixes are hope; the reject is enforcement.**
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-043 · D-WS9-041 (the protein/entrée check this extends) · D-WS9-040 · D-WS9-045.

### D-WS9-045 — Multi-version catalog so one plan never contains two versions of the same dish (mechanism REVERSED — D-WS9-059; generation model SUPERSEDED — D-WS9-062)

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[ARC]` `[WS-GEN]` `[STORE]` `[CATALOG]` `[SCALE-RUN]` `[RETENTION]`
- **Source:** Hans, July 18, 2026, at the list review. **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN** — the retention ruling stands; both mechanisms superseded.
- **The ruling:** generate a **primary version of the full list**, then **additional unique versions weighted by rank.** Hans's rationale is a **retention motion**: *"I liked the last one, I'm excited to try another Kiwi version"* / *"the last one was OK, maybe this one is better"* — and standouts are what people **share socially** (D-WS7-212).
- **⚠️ READ TIER BOUNDARIES FROM D-WS9-057, NOT HERE.** The original flat-3 (~$51) and first tiered tables are history; operative is 25 / 50 / 133 / 350 dishes at 6 / 5 / 3 / 1 versions with tier 3 widened to **76–208**. **Tiering is not in code, so a stale table is a live foot-gun.**
- **⚠️⚠️ THE RUNTIME-GENERATION MECHANISM IS SUPERSEDED — D-WS9-062.** Versions are no longer generated N-per-entry at run time (never built, and inert — the harness makes one blind call per dish). The list is **expanded into pre-named meal rows**, one meal per row; the 6/5/3/1 counts survive only as **how many rows each concept gets.**
- **⚠️ THE HARD CONSTRAINT (Hans's, load-bearing, STILL STANDS):** the AI **must never put two versions of the same dish in the same plan** — *"smash burgers and pub burgers"* in one week is exactly the near-clone experience D-WS9-043 exists to eliminate. **⚠️ MECHANISM REVERSED (D-WS9-059):** the structural `dishFamilyKey` exclusion ruled here is **withdrawn** after three failed key attempts — same-dish detection is a **semantic judgment, not a rule**, and plan composition is already **single-shot**; enforcement is a **prompt instruction** in the `wizard.candidate.generate` body. **⚠️ Mutual exclusion was NEVER shipped**, so that instruction is the **FIRST** enforcement, not a replacement for a broken one.
- **Economics (hold):** at ~**$0.06/meal** the catalog is trivial against the per-user live-generation cost it displaces. Hans: *"$0.06 per meal… 500 meals = $30. not bad."*
- **✅ Rank-tier dependency RESOLVED:** the restored appliance entries (D-WS9-046) would have received 1 version while less-common dishes received 5–6; resolved by **widening the tier rather than displacing incumbents** (D-WS9-057).
- **Sequencing:** meal-shape fix (D-WS9-044) → re-run dry-run → clean → `--apply` pilot → report → **then** the scale run. **Do NOT expand versions before the pilot passes.** *(Pilot passed July 19, 2026.)*
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-044 · D-WS9-043 · D-WS9-046 · D-WS9-057 (operative tiers) · D-WS9-059 (mechanism) · D-WS9-062 (operative generation model) · D-WS9-039 (distinct: -039 is about *letting loved meals recur*, this is about *not stacking near-clones in one plan*) · D-WS7-212.

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[ARC]` `[CATALOG]` `[BLOCK-3]` `[AMENDMENT]`
- **Source:** Hans, July 18, 2026 — **overrides chat-Claude's endorsement of CC's removal.** **Status:** ✅ **RESTORED + RE-RANKED. Operative: all 10 restored, N = 558.** (Earlier "8 restored / 2 dropped / ~556" figures are HISTORY.)
- **What happened:** CC removed **10 appliance entries** (6 slow-cooker, 2 Instant-Pot, Baked Salmon in Foil, BBQ Pork Ribs (Oven)) on the rationale *"the appliance is how, not what"*. **chat-Claude endorsed this. Both were wrong.**
- **⚠️ The ruling (Hans):** a slow-cooker meal **is** a distinct meal. *"Some people LOVE slow cooker meals and they're super appealing if you can just toss stuff in the morning and dinner's ready later. Same idea with Instant Pot — throw it in, cook hard, done and easy."* **The appliance changes the user's DAY, not just the cooking method** — categorically unlike grilled-vs-pan-seared.
- **Amendment to D-WS9-043's granularity rule:** *"the appliance is how, not what"* is **WRONG as stated and must not be reapplied.** The correct test remains: *would a cook shopping and cooking these two produce materially different food **or a materially different cooking experience**?*
- **⚠️ AMENDMENT (July 20, Gate 2) — A DROP WAS RULED BUT NEVER EXECUTED, AND IS NOW REVERSED.** Two entries were ruled dropped as oven/foil *method*; Gate 2's Phase 0 found **all 10 still present in the file** — the log recorded a drop the CSV never received. Hans ruled the **entries STAY (N = 558)**: the drop rested on a **misreading** (he had understood it as removing the word *"foil"* from a name, not removing the entry). The two sit at ranks **557–558**, deliberately untouched by the re-rank.
  - **⚠️ Durable lesson (third instance):** *a ruling recorded in canon is not a change made on disk.* **Verify canon against the artifact before building on it** — Gate 2's prompt asserted the 2 were absent **because chat-Claude read it in this entry**, and CC was right to stop rather than work around the contradiction (§3, §27).
- **✅ Carried consequence RESOLVED:** the 8 appliance entries moved into the **3-version band at ranks 76–83**, ⚠️ **without displacing any incumbent** — the boundary was widened to **76–208** instead (**D-WS9-057**).
