### D-WS9-072 — Draft recovery is a VISIBLE link, not invisible resurfacing: "See Previous Options" + drafts cleared only by an explicit regenerate act — SUPERSEDES D-WS9-035

- **Owner:** WS9 / Plan-Gen Arc **Block 4.** **Status:** ✅ **SHIPPED July 28, 2026 (Block 4b-3, pushed). Supersedes D-WS9-035**, which deferred "same-session supersede scope" to Block 4.
- **⚠️ THE RULE, in Hans's words (the July 27 refinement, and what shipped):** *"user generates plans, sees results. Next time the user goes to generate plans, let them see the prior plan options that were generated. If they click Generate Plans again, clear the prior results and write the new ones."* **Generation clears. Nothing else does** — saving, activating, previewing, backing out and navigating away clear nothing. ⚠️ **"Build My Plan" and "Get New Results" are NOT two separate clearing controls — they are the SAME ACT on two screens.**
- **⚠️ CHAT-CLAUDE PROPOSED SPLITTING "DISMISS" FROM "DISCARD" — HANS OVERRULED IT, AND HE WAS RIGHT.** The proposal was that the dismissed-set gate the *interstitial* but not the *link*; **that distinction does not exist in the build** — the interstitial's only non-resume option **is** "Get New Results," which *is* the regenerate act. Hans: *"we assume the user is thinking 'I know what those are, and I don't want them, so give me new ones' — they don't need or want to see them again."*
- **⚠️ THIS RETROACTIVELY EXPLAINS WHY THE NO-SESSION-ID RULING WORKS.** If generation always clears prior drafts and writes the new batch, **"all unconsumed drafts" IS the last run, by construction** — nothing to disambiguate. **Do not reintroduce session-id plumbing.** **⚠️ The D-WS9-035 deferral was DISSOLVED, not answered** — it asked whether supersede should narrow to same-session drafts, needing a session id threaded through generation and consume; **Hans reframed: drafts are scoped by an EXPLICIT USER ACT, not by session identity.**
- **SCOPE IS GLOBAL, NOT ROUTE-SCOPED (July 27).** All three generate paths show the same last run: **"I think just showing them what was generated the last run is good for now though." NO HOME-PAGE CTA:** *"my lean is not to do this because it's just more there to decide on and less easy click and get stuff."*
- **What the feature is for (Hans):** *"the user goes to the wizard, sees a plan they like, backs out accidentally, and then if they go back to the wizard it's gone."* **A recovery feature — and recovery problems want a visible way back, not invisible state that resurfaces later.** The gap it fixes: swiping back from plan-options left the drafts **existing but unreachable.**
- **RULED — the UX:** a visible **"See Previous Options"** link surfaces the pending batch; **drafts persist until an explicit regenerate act**; **drafts SURVIVE saving a plan.** **Why they survive saving — the deciding reason:** against *saving clears drafts* and *cleared only by "Use This Week"*, **this is the only option where the user can never lose something they wanted.** Its cost is **stale drafts behind a link — a mild tidiness problem**; the others' cost is an **unrecoverable "I picked wrong," the exact complaint that created this feature.** Hans: *"I think it's a better UX."* The two-save-button variant was also rejected as **too much subtlety for a link most users will never tap.**
- **✅ WHAT SHIPPED:** a `WizardLastBatch` table (`userId @unique`, `payload Json`, `source`; FK cascade) upserted **on success only** at the end of all three generate routes and deliberately **not** on Tell Kiwi's `unclear` short-circuit; a last-batch endpoint + the link, with a rehydrate mode on the results screen (mount-time generate/auto-expand effects early-return on rehydrate). The supersede call moved from all four consume sites to the three generate routes, idempotent branches getting a **scoped self-archive** rather than a blanket supersede (BUG-047's fix).
- **⚠️ Consequent behavior change, intended, not a regression:** expand A → expand B → activate A now leaves **B lingering** as a resumable draft until the next generation. Hans: *"it's ok if they see prior results and the prior results included the one they used."* **Marking the already-used option is WS9 3c polish; do not add a second clearing act to achieve it.**
- **⚠️ DRAFTS ARE NOW WRITTEN FOR THE WHOLE BATCH AT `build-plans` TIME — FORCED by the rule**, because the user must see the last run **even if they never opened a card. ✅ Cost is low — measured, correcting an earlier chat-Claude estimate** that ~20% of slots would still need live AI generation (arithmetic on an *assumed* meals-per-candidate — never measured): the device run was **100% catalog-bound. Not guaranteed** — a thin shelf against unusual preferences still needs live fills. Hash-reuse verified: a rehydrated candidate carries its titles verbatim, so the content hash matches and expand reuses the existing draft with **zero AI calls.**
- **⚠️ MOUNT-GATE MECHANISM (explains a confusing behavior Hans hit).** The resume interstitial fires on **screen mount**, so swiping back from a plan detail returns to an **already-mounted** screen and the gate doesn't re-run, while backing out to home and re-entering **remounts** and it does. **This is why the interstitial appeared inconsistently** — and it is the structural argument for the visible link: *a mount-time interruption can only ever catch the user at one moment.* Dismissals also persist to device storage and filter that draft out permanently on every future mount.
- **Two follow-ons:** **BUG-051** (generation doesn't invalidate the cached last-batch query, so the link serves a stale batch until a remount → WS9 3c) and **D-WS9-084** (a stale batch judged against changed preferences is explicitly **not** a defect).
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-035 (superseded) · D-WS9-032 · D-WS9-070 · BUG-030 / BUG-023 · BUG-047 · BUG-051 · D-WS9-083 · D-WS9-084.

### D-WS9-073 — Catalog exhaustion + repeat behavior: deterministic lineage via `sourceStoreMealId`, AI-judged soft nudge (NOT deterministic scoring, NOT hard exclusion) — ✅ SHIPPED July 27, 2026 — ⚠️ **EFFICACY REMAINS AN OPEN MEASUREMENT QUESTION**

- **Owner:** WS9 / Plan-Gen Arc **Block 4.** **Status:** ✅ **RULED** (July 23, 2026) **and SHIPPED** (Block 4b-2, July 27). **Implements the mechanism for D-WS9-039**, whose *direction* remains governing and unchanged.
- **⚠️ TWO OF THE THREE QUEUED SUB-QUESTIONS WERE ALREADY ANSWERED — no new work:** *"what happens when a household has seen most of the catalog?"* → per **D-WS9-037** the read path degrades on **actual coverage, not a flag**, so **exhaustion is not a cliff.** *"Where's the line between 'you loved this' and 'we're out of ideas'?"* → **D-WS9-039 already ruled it:** no aggressive never-repeat logic, bias toward **letting loved meals recur**, recurrence **preference-aware.**
- **What was ACTUALLY open:** the repeat mechanism was **id-based and lineage-blind** — the fork gives the user's copy a **new id**, so `excludeMealIds` cannot connect it to the store original and **the store can re-offer a meal the user already had, arbitrarily.** Such a repeat is **unlikely** per week — but **rare-and-arbitrary is the annoying kind:** unpredictable, and it reads as careless when it lands.
- **⚠️ Hans's reframe — the target is a PATTERN, not a repeat.** *"baked chicken 2 weeks in a row is fine, but I don't want a user to be like 'man, kiwi really loves suggesting those dang fajitas'… but I also recognize it's easier to cook something you've cooked before."* **A window cannot express this** — it only knows recent/not-recent, and cannot distinguish "twice" from "every week."
- **RULED — the split: DETERMINISTIC DATA, AI JUDGMENT.** **Deterministic: `sourceStoreMealId` on the user's forked copy**, pointing back at the catalog original — **a data fact, not a judgment, and without it there is nothing to pass in either direction.** **AI-judged (do NOT build deterministic scoring):** recently-served store ids go into the generation prompt with a soft nudge. **Rejected: hard exclusion** — it creates a cliff (banned, then abruptly fully available), *precisely* what produces the fajita clustering at the boundary, and it forbids the best-burger recurrence outright. **Rejected: deterministic weighted scoring** — it pushes **all versions of a family down together**, whereas the catalog's intentional multiplication of popular meals lets the model **vary WITHIN a family. Unit of recency: PLAN COUNT, not calendar time** (~3 plans) — a time window punishes heavy users and does nothing for someone planning every three weeks.
- **⚠️ The known cost of choosing AI judgment, accepted with eyes open:** a prompt instruction is **unverifiable** — not unit-testable, learnable only from weeks of real use, and **the arc's standing lesson is that prompt-level claims have failed when measured.** **Treat "does the nudge actually work" as an OPEN MEASUREMENT QUESTION, not a shipped feature.**
- **Prompt intent + STARTING DRAFT (⚠️ NOT frozen text):**

  > Meals recently served to this user are listed below. Prefer meals the user hasn't seen. A recently-served meal — or another version of it — may be chosen when the user's preferences point that way, but no meal or dish family should dominate the user's rotation.

  **Why this wording:** Hans's draft (*"avoid over-representing these. similar variations are ok if the user's preferences say so"*) had the right structure, but **"similar variations are ok" reads as permission and risks being taken as encouragement** — the failure mode where the model over-indexes on the most specific clause and returns *six* fajita variants. The revision makes **"prefer unseen" the explicit default**, renders the variant clause **permitted rather than invited**, and anchors "similar" to **`dishFamily`. ⚠️ Do NOT freeze this wording.**
- **Scope boundary: store meals only.** Live-generated meals have no store id and are unaffected.
- **✅ SHIPPED:** a recent-rotation builder walks the user's last **3** plans (a named constant, to be tuned) and resolves each served meal via the lineage hop `fork.sourceStoreMealId → original.dishFamilyKey → {dishFamily, familyRank}`, falling back to **title-only** for live-generated meals. **Best-effort: a failure yields an empty rotation and never sinks generation.** Threaded onto **build-plans** and **directed** only; **Surprise Me deliberately untouched.**
- ✅ **FIRST EFFICACY MEASUREMENT, September 12, 2026 (BUG-255): THE NUDGE FIRED AND LOST — a shelf meal was re-offered five minutes after the plan containing it was saved into the rotation.** **Cause measured and ruled: at a 30-minute cap the eligible shelf is SIX dinners, and all six appear in this user's generations. Prefer-unseen over six candidates has nowhere to go.** **The rule is unchanged; the fix is the catalog supplement. Revisit efficacy once the shelf is deep.** ⚠️ **AND OTHERWISE IT REMAINS UNVERIFIED — it must not be quietly treated as closed.** At ship time the account carried **24 lineage-bearing forks with `timesRecentlyServed` mostly 1** — almost nothing for "prefer-unseen / no domination" to push against. The device test confirmed the **mechanism**, **not the behavior. Revisit with real usage before assuming this works.**
- **⚠️ FUTURE GAP — the plan-walk misses cooked-but-never-planned meals.** The replaced helper carried a **cooked branch** (`cook_meal` activity events) the rotation walk does not; that branch is **inert today**, so nothing was lost. **But when the Cook Mode completion writer lands (WS7-11 / D-WS7-204), a meal cooked without being on a plan will be invisible to the rotation walk.** The fix is likely a union, not a replacement.
- **⚠️ TWO RULINGS APPLIED AT BUILD TIME (Hans).** (1) **REPLACE, not layer** (§10, the line-824 lesson): the pre-existing `# Recent history` instruction was *replaced*, accepting cache-prefix invalidation and a version bump as the cost of one coherent mechanism. (2) **Build-plans and directed only:** Surprise Me was excluded because its crowd-pleaser constraint (*"popular, mainstream… No obscure or experimental dishes"*) points at the catalog **head** — exactly where a returning user's already-seen meals concentrate — a soft-vs-soft collision with no tie-break.
- **⚠️ ONE CLAUSE CUT FROM THE DRAFT, and the reasoning generalizes:** an *"or genuine ingredient reuse across the plan"* permission was removed. The two surviving exceptions (a listed cuisine; an allergy/constraint that narrows the field) are **user preferences**, which is what this entry licensed; **ingredient reuse is a system objective in a different category**, already instructed elsewhere (D-WS7-167), and naming it a third time invites the model to use it as a general-purpose excuse to repeat.
- **⚠️ THE SHELF GUARD IS LOAD-BEARING — do not let future prompt edits erode it.** Both shipped sections state that prefer-unseen means *"reaching for a different shelf meal or a different dish family, never abandoning the shelf."* ⚠️ **Corrected September 10, measured: that is set_preferences' wording; the directed body says *"prefer-unseen means a different shelf meal or family, not abandoning the shelf."* A guard asserts each body's own phrase.** Without it, prefer-unseen reads as licence to invent over catalog meals, **silently undoing Block 4b-1's entire gain.** Verbatim text is in `kiwi_plan_generation_arc_scope.md` §Block 4b-2.
- **Measured lineage ground truth (corrects canon):** **24** forks carry `sourceStoreMealId` across **20 originals** (canon said ~20 forks); 19/20 carry `dishFamilyKey`. ⚠️ **Every fork's own `dishFamilyKey` is null** — forks never copy it — so **the hop to the original is the only path.** ⚠️ **Canon's "write-backs don't carry lineage" is FALSE.**
- 🔴 **THE GAP HANS FOUND September 11, 2026, AND IT IS IN THIS ENTRY'S OWN SHIPPED DESIGN: the rotation walks the user's last 3 PLANS, so a meal OFFERED in a generation that is never saved is never "recently served" and can be offered again indefinitely.** He has seen one flatbread *"a handful of times recently when generating plans."* **Minted as BUG-255, where the ruling (does offering count as seen?) and the measurement that must precede it live.** ⚠️ **Same shape as this entry's own cooked-but-never-planned gap — and the same likely fix, a union rather than a replacement.**
- 🔵 **TWO NEIGHBOURS ADDED September 10, 2026 — DIFFERENT RULES, KEEP THEM APART.** **BUG-249** (no meal repeated across the three plans of ONE generation) is within a response; this entry is across generations. The server block that builds BUG-249 was told to leave this entry's rotation text byte-identical and to guard each body's own shelf-guard phrase. **D-WS9-234** (the Playlist): a declared staple must not be pushed away by this nudge — confirm at the playlist spec.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-039 · D-WS9-037 · D-WS9-045 (`dishFamily` — the anchor for "similar") · D-WS9-061 · D-WS9-036 · D-WS9-070 / D-WS9-072 · D-WS7-204 · WS7-11 · BUG-249 · D-WS9-234.

### D-WS9-074 — Canonicalize `cuisines` to a single enforced enum (BUG-043 structural / Fix B) → WS10
- **Tags:** `[WS10]` `[DATA-MODEL]` `[PREFS]` `[TECH-DEBT]` · **Status:** 🟡 OPEN · **Owner:** WS10 (Hans, July 25)
- **Source:** BUG-043 diagnostic (July 19) + Fix A close (July 25). Fix A cleared the live pollution; this is the structural half that stops it recurring.

### D-WS9-079 — Two generators behind one endpoint, and a prompt body that contradicts one of them
- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[PLAN-GEN]` `[PROMPT]` `[DEBT]` · **Status:** 🟡 OPEN · **Owner:** WS9 prompt-hygiene pass · **Source:** latency block text-mode conversion (July 26–27)
- **Two coupled facts.** (1) `POST /wizard/build-plans` runs a **text-mode streaming primary** and a **tool-mode buffered fallback** — *different generators*, not merely different transports. Measured equivalent at ship time (10 runs/arm: identical field counts; `storeSlotsMarked` 14.50 text vs 13.80 tool), but **nothing detects drift** as the prompt body evolves. (2) The body (v6) says *"Return ONLY the tool_use call"*; the streaming path injects a code-side override — *"There is NO tool available; ignore any instruction to make a tool_use call."*
- ⚠️ **It works (10/10 first-try validity) but it is a layered contradiction rather than a replacement** — the pattern behind this arc's line-824 failure. Anyone editing that body later will not know the streaming path contradicts it.
- **The override is deliberately in code, not the body:** no version bump, `promptVersion` stays diagnostic, and the body **cannot simply drop** the tool_use language because the fallback still needs it.
- **Target:** make the body **mode-neutral** (accepts a bump) so neither path needs an override; then rule whether the fallback aligns to text mode or stays tool-mode as the constrained safety net.

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[UX]` `[COPY]` · **Status:** 🟡 OPEN · **Owner:** plan-options screen rebuild (4b UI / WS9 3c) · **Source:** Hans, device test of streamed generation (July 27)

### D-WS9-081 — Stream liveness: a server-side overall timeout is still missing as a backstop
- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[PLAN-GEN]` `[RELIABILITY]` · **Status:** 🟡 OPEN · **Owner:** WS9A / hardening before the hosted deploy · **Source:** latency block (July 27)
- Delta-driven **progress frames** keep the client's 20s stall watchdog from tripping during a slow generation, and because the signal derives from **real model output** rather than a timer, a genuine stall correctly stops the frames and the watchdog fires as intended. (A timer-based heartbeat was rejected precisely because it would mask a wedged-but-pinging server.)
- **Still missing:** a server-side overall timeout — a wedged upstream could hold a stream open indefinitely. Deliberately **not** built under the block's gate: a half-designed timeout is worse than none.

### D-WS9-085 — Marking the already-used option in a previous batch requires server-side lineage; no candidate→plan linkage exists today — 🟡 **DEFERRED (polish, not a gate)**
- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[PLAN-GEN]` `[DRAFT-LIFECYCLE]` `[POLISH]` · **Status:** 🟡 OPEN · **Owner:** WS9 post-3c, or post-go-live
- **Source:** Block 3c, from Hans's standing ruling that **activation does NOT clear the batch** — verbatim: *"it's ok if they see prior results and the prior results included the one they used."* One of the three options a returning user sees may already be in their library and should be **marked**. ⚠️ **A marking task, not a clearing task. Do not resolve it by adding a second clearing act.**
- **⚠️ THE FINDING — VERIFIED BY CODE READ AND SCHEMA GREP.** No linkage from a batch candidate to a created plan: no model carries a source-candidate or source-draft id; the candidate id is a **stub identifier** (`m1`/`c1` scaffolding), not a durable key; and the server's **content-hash dedup** (candidate title + sorted meal titles) is internal and **never exposed to the client**, so the one place a linkage effectively exists is unreachable from the surface that needs it.
- **⚠️ THE ONLY CLIENT-SIDE OPTION IS FUZZY TITLE-MATCHING AND IT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED.** It breaks on renames and on multiple plans built from one batch. **A wrong mark is worse than no mark** — it tells the user they already used something they didn't, on a screen whose whole purpose is helping them choose. Same reasoning as D-WS7-214's flag-don't-compute ruling: *a confidently wrong answer is a trust failure where an honest absence is not.*
- **Two viable shapes, neither built, not ruled between:** (1) **server-side** — record the activated candidate index/draft id alongside the stored batch and return it (durable, survives reinstall); (2) **client-persisted** candidate→plan map at activate time (no server change).
- **Why deferred:** polish on a surface that already works — blocks no tester, affects no correctness, and needed a design decision that would have expanded a block already carrying six parts.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-072 · D-WS9-084 · D-WS7-214.

### D-WS9-087 — `recentPlanNames` is overloaded to carry meal titles on the build-plans route — 🟡 **DEFERRED (correct today, mis-named)**
- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[PLAN-GEN]` `[PROMPT-INPUT]` `[NAMING]` · **Status:** 🟡 OPEN · **Owner:** WS9 or WS10 · **Source:** 3c follow-up Group 3, disclosed by CC as an unavoidable route asymmetry
- **The asymmetry:** the surprise route merges shown **plan titles → `recentPlanNames`** and shown **meal titles → `recentMeals`**. Build-plans **cannot use `recentMeals`** — D-WS9-073 strips it there in favour of `recentRotation` — so **both** fold into `recentPlanNames`. **A field named "plan names" carries meal titles on one of two routes.**
- **✅ Functionally correct today** (the widened instruction treats the whole list as things to steer away from). **The defect is legibility**; the risk is a future reader — human or model — trusting the field name.
- **⚠️ WHY `recentRotation` WAS NOT USED, and why that was right:** its consumers were unvetted, and it is a **distinct lineage signal** (`fork.sourceStoreMealId → dishFamilyKey`), not a title list. Threading session titles into it would have overloaded a *semantic* field rather than a *nominal* one — strictly worse. **The conservative choice was correct; the naming debt is the price.**
- **📝 Related device observation (BUG-053, not a defect):** post-fix, plans are distinct but individual meals still recur. This overload is **one** candidate explanation; **by-design soft-nudge behaviour (D-WS9-073) is the other**, and they have not been separated. Hans is observing rather than acting. **Do not tighten the nudge without separating them first.**
- **What to do:** rename to something honest (`avoidTitles`) or give build-plans its own session-exclusion field distinct from both. **Prefer the latter** — it stops overloading anything.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-073 · D-WS9-086 · BUG-053.

### D-WS9-089 — Server-owned fields leaking into client-echoed write payloads: a structural hazard, patched locally twice — 🟡 **DEFERRED (work item, not a symptom) → WS10 Zod bundle**
- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[WS10]` `[ZOD]` `[WIRE-SHAPE]` `[STRUCTURAL]` · **Status:** 🟡 OPEN · **Owner:** WS10, bundled with **D-WS9-074**
- **Origin — the 3d Part 3b P1.** Adding `dietaryUpdatedAt` to the mobile preferences payload (so the **client** could compute staleness) broke **every** preference save: the screen echoes the whole fetched object back, and the strict validator returned **400 `unrecognized_keys`**. Fixed by not declaring the field on the mobile schema, so it is stripped at parse and can never re-enter the edit buffer.
- **⚠️ SECOND OCCURRENCE, NOT THE FIRST.** The form-state builder **already** strips `weeklyPacingDefault` for exactly this reason — patched locally once, never fixed structurally, which is the whole argument for logging it as a work item rather than closing it with the P1.
- **✅ SIZED BY MEASUREMENT (probe A6 — the count is 1, and that is the useful part).** Sweeping every strict endpoint for *(validator rejecting unknown keys)* × *(save path building its body from a fetched object)*: **count = 1**, the preferences PATCH, currently guarded. All other strict endpoints assemble bodies by **explicit field selection**; other routes use non-strict objects that silently strip. The plan PATCH is **safe today** (callers field-scope) but carries the **identical latent risk** — strict validator, so one future screen spreading a fetched plan reproduces the bug.
- **⚠️ THE STRUCTURAL HAZARD IS UNCHANGED BY THE LOW COUNT.** Any **new server-owned column** on the preferences GET re-breaks the save path unless added to the strip list. Count 1 means the *cleanup* is small, not that the *trap* is closed. **A low incidence count is an argument about cost, not about safety** — the same reasoning that let this ship twice.
- **What to build (WS10):** a single declared `SERVER_ONLY_PREFERENCE_KEYS` boundary (or client-edge `.strip()`) so the strip is **declarative and one place**, not two hand-patched fields plus a schema omission.
- **📝 Architecture note worth keeping.** Root cause was **mobile being asked to compute a judgment**, against the standing invariant *server owns all math, attribution and structure; mobile renders and never recomputes.* The fix moved the staleness decision server-side. **The wire-shape bug was a symptom; the invariant violation was the cause.**
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-074 · D-WS9-086 (same bundle) · BUG-055 (a *different* defect on the same save path — do not conflate) · §27.

### D-WS9-090 — Archived (composted) plans and grocery lists remain reachable by direct navigation — ✅ **RULED July 30, 2026 (Hans): READ-ONLY WITH A "THIS PLAN WAS COMPOSTED" MESSAGE, not 404** · 🟡 **BUILD OPEN → Block 3e**
- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[PLAN-LIFECYCLE]` `[GROCERY]` `[UX]` · **Source:** 3d Part 3c probe A5; proposed by CC, **recommendation only, nothing built.** Hans: *"agreed with ws9-090: message it was composted."*
- ⚠️ **The reasoning is load-bearing against re-litigation: plan DELETE is a SOFT-delete** (sets `isArchived`/`compostedAt`/`status=past`; the row and its graph stay intact — CC corrected the prompt's "hard delete" framing). **A 404 would report a user's own intact, archived data as nonexistent** and break legitimate history browsing. **Archived is not gone.**
- **Three confirmed facts (verified, not inferred):** the plan by-id GET returns **archived** plans (ownership-only filter); the grocery-list by-id GET returns **archived** lists; the grocery screen's **"view plan"** link navigates **unconditionally**, with no archived check.
- **✅ NO LIVE ORPHAN EXISTS TODAY, and the absence is itself evidence.** All 10 of the dev user's grocery lists read `planArchived=false, status=active` — **consistent with the A3 crash**: the plan Hans "composted" **never archived**, so its list was never cascaded. **The orphan symptom was downstream of the crash, not a second defect.** Once the crash fix lands the cascade fires and the real question surfaces.
- **⚠️ WHAT REMAINS UNDECIDED IS THE DEGREE OF READ-ONLY, and 3e must settle it rather than assume.** The ruling fixes the *message*, not which affordances survive. **Open for 3e Phase 0:** does a composted plan still expose **Use again** (arguably its most useful action in that state)? Do **Prep & Cook** / **Grocery** CTAs hide, disable, or stay live? Is the composted grocery list read-only, or does it keep check-off state? **Decide deliberately — an ambiguous "read-only" invites CC to pick, and the wrong pick means a user losing access to a plan they wanted back.**
- **Scope as ruled:** an `isArchived`/`compostedAt` flag on the two GET payloads, a banner on both screens, and a **label** (not a block) on the grocery "view plan" link. ⚠️ **Do NOT add a 404 path, and do NOT filter archived records out of the by-id GETs** — the 3c-2 index filter is a *list* concern and is already correct; **by-id retrieval must keep working or the ruling cannot be implemented.**
- **⚠️ DELIBERATELY WALLED OUT OF 3c-2's SCOPE** so CC could not answer a pending product question by implementing one. **The ruling arrived from Hans, not from a build.**
- **Owner:** Block 3e. **Status:** ✅ RULED · 🟡 BUILD OPEN. **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-001 · the 3d A3 crash · R-3d-7.

### D-WS9-092 — Expand + activate latency: ~39s and ~$0.08 per GAP-FILLED meal — the code scales linearly, but coverage behaves as a STEP FUNCTION — 📦 **PACKAGED to roadmap row 8a**
- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[PLAN-GEN]` `[LATENCY]` `[COST]` `[MEASURED]` `[CATALOG-COVERAGE]` · **Status:** 📦 **PACKAGED** → `kiwi_latency_program.md` (the single pickup point; read it instead of this entry).
- **⚠️ THE ARCHITECTURE IS FINE. TWO CHAT-CLAUDE HYPOTHESES WERE FALSIFIED BY READING THE CALL SITES:** `expand` is called **per LIVE slot**, not per candidate; `finalize_steps` **per BUILD meal**, not per plan; **catalog-bound slots make ZERO AI calls and are NOT echoed back through the model.** The *"expand re-describes the whole plan"* hypothesis **is dead. There is no fix to make in the call structure.**
- **✅ MEASURED COST OF ONE GAP (device log, 3 catalog-bound + 1 live slot):**

  | Call | Latency | Cost |
  |---|---|---|
  | `expand` (1 live slot) | **13.5s** | $0.029 |
  | 3 × nutrition estimate (parallel) | ~2.8s | $0.010 |
  | `finalize_steps` (1 build meal) | **22.8s** | $0.039 |
  | **One gap-filled meal, total** | **~39s** | **~$0.08** |

  User-facing: **17.4s to open the plan**, then **32.4s on "Use this week."** **Whole plan $0.111.** A fully-catalog plan runs **~$0.046**, **~2s** expand, **no `finalize_steps` call at all**.
- **⚠️ THE REAL FINDING: COVERAGE IS A STEP FUNCTION, NOT A GRADIENT — which is why a percentage metric hid it.** 3/4 coverage *sounds* like a 75% win; **on the measured plan, 3/4 → 4/4 saves ~36s and ~$0.065, because one miss pays a full meal's generation while the three catalog meals contributed essentially nothing to the wait.** ⚠️ **Probe A7 measured 75–100% coverage and concluded the latency "is not primarily gap-fill" — wrong conclusion from a correct measurement.** **Hans's instinct that the catalog effort was not cashing out was right; the mechanism was not the one he or chat-Claude proposed.** ⚠️ **Standing lesson, third instance this arc: a coverage percentage is not a latency percentage when the residual is serial and pays full price.**
- ⚠️ **CATALOG COVERAGE IS NO LONGER THE FIRST LEVER.** Two cheaper mechanisms were split out — **D-WS9-094** and **D-WS9-095** — and ⚠️ **both are LOOKUP failures, not generation costs: fixable without touching the catalog, invisible until instrumentation shipped. Sequence 094 and 095 ahead of coverage work.** **The third lever is coverage BREADTH** — hit-rate on the meals users actually get offered, not total size — and ⚠️ D-WS9-077 / -078 **narrow the reachable pool for exactly the users most likely to miss**, so they price into it. **Secondary, unpriced:** `finalize_steps` is the largest call (22.8s / $0.039); whether its output volume can shrink without quality loss has never been tested. ⚠️ **The floor underneath all of it is D-WS9-093** — a **9.2s non-AI DB transaction** on every genuine activation, which **at full coverage becomes the largest single wait**, so plan the two together.
- 📦 **RE-OWNED July 31, 2026 (Hans): roadmap row 8a — post-MVP/UAT polish, AFTER row 8 (Instacart), before row 9 (Auth+Stripe).** ⚠️ **Supersedes the earlier "own block immediately after 3d Part 4" sequencing, which rested on a testing-throughput argument** (*"faster loading = faster testing"*) — the remaining WS9 blocks are **not plan-regeneration surfaces**, so the buy-back is small. **Packaged, not discarded.**
- ⚠️ **THE INVESTIGATION IS BLOCKED ON DATA WE ARE NOT KEEPING (3e Phase 0).** The expand/finalize summary events carry live-vs-store slot counts **to stdout ONLY — no log store, nothing queryable** — so **the coverage-vs-cost curve CANNOT be drawn after the fact**; ordinary generations produce it and throw it away. The **cost** side IS queryable (`LLMCallLog`): `expand` **334 calls, 8.0–21.0s (avg 13.1s), ~$0.029/call**; `finalize_steps` **228 calls, 12.5–28.1s (avg 18.9s), ~$0.035/call**. **Ship telemetry persistence FIRST at pickup — ~1 turn, unblocks this permanently.**
- ⚠️ **AN OPEN QUESTION THAT MUST BE SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT INFERENCE.** Timestamp clustering (expands in groups of 4 within ~3s) was read as **recent generations getting ZERO catalog binding**. ⚠️ **The 3e audit does NOT accept this:** clusters of four are equally consistent with the known adversarial-preferences test run in the same window, and the inference contradicts two prior *measurements* (this entry's 3-of-4, 4b-3's 12-of-12) — **the exact failure shape logged five times this arc: one signal, two stories, the cheaper one adopted.** ⚠️ **DO NOT carry "the catalog binds nothing" into canon.** Settle it with **one ordinary-preferences device generation with the terminal open** — 15 minutes — before ranking levers.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-093 (the floor) · D-WS9-083 (✅ tension RESOLVED: its 1.5–2.5s was a **4/4-bound** expand, this is **3/4** — different coverage, not contradictory) · D-WS9-082 · D-WS9-077 / -078.

### D-WS9-093 — The 9.2s activate transaction: sequential plan-graph inserts, no AI — 📦 **PACKAGED (structure verified; per-statement cost UNVERIFIED)**
- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[LATENCY]` `[DB]` `[PLAN-GEN]` `[NOT-AI]` · **Source:** probe A5, from a device log line in plain sight — `activate $transaction elapsed: 9203ms (ok)`: **9.2 seconds, no AI call**, sequential plan-graph inserts.
- ✅ **CURRENT TRUTH (3e Phase 0): the 284ms-vs-32,358ms activate split is idempotency HIT vs MISS**, not "all-store vs live." On a hit, the activate-side BUG-030 idempotency finds the content-hash already materialized, archives the orphan draft and returns the existing plan — **skipping `finalize_steps` AND materialization entirely.** Arithmetic corroborates (22.8s + 9.2s ≈ 32.0s) and it explains the awkward 25.3s expand three seconds earlier. **CC's "all-store" reading is FALSIFIED.**
- ⚠️ **CONSEQUENCE: the 9.2s IS paid on every *genuine* (non-idempotent) activation and does NOT shrink with catalog coverage** — store-bound slots route through a fork-for-user clone with its own pile of inserts. **The governing variable is TOTAL ROW COUNT, not slot count and not coverage.**
- ⚠️ **TWO DURABLE LESSONS.** (1) The original "paid on every activation" claim came from a **single log line** generalized without a second observation — *one measurement plus a plausible mechanism is not a finding*, and it reached a canonical doc stated as fact. (2) **A CORRECTION CAN ITSELF BE AN OVER-CORRECTION:** the July-30 retraction generalized a single 284ms observation into "the figure is conditional, it shrinks with coverage" by exactly the mechanism the original error used. **When falsifying a claim, retract to *unknown*, not to the opposite.**
- ✅ **STRUCTURE VERIFIED:** O(meals + dishes + ingredients + steps), every row a separate sequential create inside one interactive transaction. A 4-meal plan at ~3 dishes × ~8 ingredients × ~8 steps ≈ **200+ sequential round-trips** → ~9s warm, worse cold (**same P2028 transaction-budget risk the grocery route already hit**). **Batchable into `createMany` with pre-generated UUIDs — the grocery generate route already does exactly this.** ✅ **It does NOT touch the content-hash / supersede / BUG-030 logic — those live in the route AROUND it.**
- ⚠️ **PER-STATEMENT TIMING REMAINS UNOBTAINABLE** (no query-level instrumentation, stdout-only logs), so the projected 9.2s → 1–2s is **modelled, not measured**, and the obvious per-item-loop story is **plausible and unconfirmed.** ⚠️ **This project's history is a list of plausible stories failing on measurement; instrument before designing.**
- **⚠️ WHY THIS EARNS ITS OWN PHASE 0 RATHER THAN A TACK-ON FIX (Hans, Option A).** The materializer is **load-bearing**: content-hash idempotency, supersede and BUG-030's dupe-on-back-out fix all live around it, and two months of Blocks 1 and 4b-3 went into making it produce no orphans. **A batching change touches transaction semantics on the one path where a partial write creates exactly the garbage that work eliminated.**
- 📦 **RE-OWNED July 31, 2026 (Hans): roadmap row 8a, after Instacart.** ⚠️ **Read `kiwi_latency_program.md` at pickup, not this entry.** ⚠️ **RE-MEASURE BEFORE BUILDING:** the ~9.2s was measured against Neon **from Hans's local machine**, and **WS9A hosting lands first** — a co-located deploy may shrink it materially.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-092 (the AI half of the same wait) · BUG-030 + D-WS9-034/-035 · D-WS7-176/-177 (scale-at-render servings — the invariant the plan graph must preserve).

### D-WS9-094 — ⚠️ SUPERSEDE ARCHIVES THE VERY DRAFT THE CONTENT-HASH LOOKUP WOULD HAVE REUSED — two correctness systems cancelling each other — 📦 **PACKAGED (highest-value latency lever)**
- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[PLAN-GEN]` `[LATENCY]` `[COST]` `[IDEMPOTENCY]` `[SUPERSEDE]` `[MEASURED]`
- **✅ THE MECHANISM, VERIFIED.** `contentHash` is **input-derived and computed BEFORE the AI call**, and **the lookup does short-circuit cost** — the idempotency machinery works as designed. **The duplicate cost comes from supersede archiving the reusable draft**, so the next lookup misses and pays full generation again.
- **⚠️ THE SHAPE IS THE POINT: TWO SYSTEMS BUILT TO PROTECT THE SAME THING ARE CANCELLING EACH OTHER.** Supersede prevents orphan/duplicate drafts; the content-hash lookup prevents regenerating identical content. Neither is wrong alone. **The defect is in their interaction, which is why every audit of either one came back clean.**
- **✅ DEVICE EVIDENCE (three expands of one plan):** identical `contentHash` across three draft IDs, with **differing** expand output tokens (4758 vs 4627 — the model genuinely produced different text each run). **~$0.18 and ~19s per repeat, ~$0.54 for one plan in one test session.**
- ⚠️ **RETRACTED (3e Phase 0): the earlier "this may dissolve D-WS9-072" claim is FALSE. D-WS9-072 IS ALREADY SHIPPED, AND THE RE-TIMING DID NOT FIX THIS.** Supersede already fires **on generate only** — save/activate **skip** it and narrowly self-archive the consumed draft. **That IS "regenerate-only"; it shipped as BUG-047's fix on July 28**, verified three independent ways. ⚠️ **Canon asserted a state the artifact did not have — the fifth instance this arc.** **D-WS9-072 decided WHEN supersede fires. This entry is about WHAT IT SPARES. Different changes.**
- ⚠️ **THE REASON RE-TIMING DIDN'T HELP SIZES THE FIX: THERE ARE TWO BLOCKERS, NOT ONE.** Supersede sets `isArchived:true` **AND NULLs the draft payload**; the expand-side lookup filters on unarchived rows **and parses that payload**. **Even if the lookup stopped excluding archived rows, the row would still be unreusable — the payload is gone.** A retain-for-reuse fix must do both: **(a)** not exclude the retained draft **and (b)** not null its payload. **A fix addressing only one will appear to do nothing.**
- ✅ **THE ORPHAN ENUMERATION — the gate on any fix.** Supersede currently prevents: **(1) Resume-list pollution, its primary live purpose** — the resume interstitial filters unarchived wizard drafts, so without on-generate supersede every peeked candidate from every past run stays offered forever; **(2) Stale-payload mis-activation (BUG-052)**; **(3) Idempotent-return orphan (BUG-047)** — handled by the narrow self-archive, **not** by sibling supersede. **Verdict: retaining the same-hash draft (payload intact) while still archiving different-hash siblings appears SAFE against 1–3** — the retained draft becomes resumable, but it is the plan the user is re-generating, so offering it is arguably correct. ⚠️ **That is a behavior change and wants an explicit ruling before build.**
- ⚠️ **ONE GAP LEFT OPEN, CC-flagged rather than claimed complete: the stale-draft TTL sweep was NOT traced** — directly load-bearing, because the fix is literally "retain a draft longer" and an untraced sweep that deletes stale drafts is precisely what interacts with that. **One grep closes it; it must happen in Phase 0, not during the build.**
- **⚠️ WHAT THE FIX MUST NOT BREAK. Blocks 1 and 4b-3 spent two months eliminating exactly the garbage supersede guards against; any change to its timing must be shown not to re-open orphan creation** — the gate on this work, and why it belongs in a Phase-0-gated block. **Phase 0 also needs:** the precise supersede trigger and scope, what the lookup keys on, and whether a draft can be retained-but-inactive rather than archived.
- **⚠️ CHAT HYPOTHESIS FALSIFIED, recorded as precedent.** Chat-Claude proposed *"the identity is computed only after paying full generation cost — idempotency prevents duplicate ROWS without preventing duplicate COST."* **Wrong**; the prompt asked CC to falsify rather than confirm, and it did. **The correct instinct (something is defeating reuse) reached the wrong mechanism — the fourth time this arc a confident log-derived story failed on code inspection.**
- 📦 **RE-OWNED July 31 (Hans): roadmap row 8a; read `kiwi_latency_program.md` at pickup.** ⚠️ **Honest payoff note: this mostly helps Hans testing** — repeated regeneration of byte-identical content is a testing pattern more than a user pattern. **Do not oversell it as a user-facing win.**
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-072 · D-WS9-095 · D-WS9-092 · BUG-030 / BUG-047.

### D-WS9-095 — ⚠️ **RETRACTED AS ORIGINALLY FRAMED.** Store-compose never binds against the user's own PRIVATE library — 📦 **PACKAGED (the finding that survives, narrowed twice)**
- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[PLAN-GEN]` `[LATENCY]` `[COST]` `[RETRACTION]` · **Source:** probe A3 → ⚠️ **corrected July 30, 2026 by Hans, who tested the surface and knew what it does** → narrowed again at 3e Phase 0.
- **⚠️ WHAT WAS ORIGINALLY CLAIMED AND WHY IT WAS WRONG.** It said *"the wizard's prior-plans path carries no `sourcePlanId` and ALWAYS regenerates, while `copyPlan` — the cheap path — already exists,"* and proposed threading `sourcePlanId` through `copyPlan`. **False premise about what the surface is.**
- **✅ WHAT PRIOR-PLANS ACTUALLY IS (Hans, product authority, device-verified): it shows THE LAST WIZARD RUN'S RESULTS — the previous run's candidate cards. It is NOT a list of saved plans.** ⚠️ **So the "missing `sourcePlanId`" is CORRECT BY DESIGN, not a defect.** A **candidate is a spec** (title + meal titles), not a materialized plan; there is no source plan to point at, and `copyPlan` copies a plan *instance*. **Expanding a candidate is supposed to cost generation the first time. That is the architecture working.**
- **⚠️ ALL OF THE OBSERVED WASTE COLLAPSES INTO D-WS9-094:** the identical `contentHash` proves the system recognized the repeat; the second expand should have hit the cache and did not, **because supersede had archived the reusable draft. One mechanism, not two.**
- **✅ THE FINDING THAT SURVIVES:** store-compose binds candidate slots **only against the public pool — never against the user's own private meals.** ⚠️ **A user with a large personal library gets ZERO binding benefit; cost impact scales with library size, so it is invisible on a fresh account and worst for exactly the engaged users we most want to keep.**
- ⚠️ **"CATALOG-ONLY" WAS ITSELF IMPRECISE.** The shelf-pool predicate is `{ isPublic: true, isArchived: false }`, which **already spans both `userId:null` catalog/curated meals AND owned-but-public community meals.** **The real exclusion is the user's own PRIVATE (`isPublic:false`) library — same practical consequence, different mechanism, and the mechanism matters because it changes what the fix is.**
- **What binding to private meals would require (verified structurally):** user meals **do** share the `Meal → dishes → ingredients → steps` graph, and the composer already demotes structurally-unusable pool meals to live generation at runtime — **a partial safety net, not a gate.** A real fix needs **(a)** widening the pool to the user's own private meals scoped to `userId`, and **(b)** a **structural-completeness gate the catalog gets FREE from the freeze bar** (*"no row is malformed"*), because imports and manual entries can be shape-incomplete. ⚠️ **UNVERIFIED whether user meals *should* be bindable at all — establish that before designing.** ⚠️ **Relying on the runtime demote-if-unusable path alone for a large private library means MANY SILENT DEMOTIONS — retrieval cost with no binding benefit.**
- **⚠️ THE PROCESS LESSON, the more valuable half.** CC answered the *mechanism* question correctly and its answer was folded into a *product* framing chat-Claude invented; **Hans then had to correct a canonical entry from his own product knowledge.** ⚠️ **The prompt had ASKED for design intent, CC came back thin on it, the thinness was flagged in the audit and then written into canon anyway as if resolved. A flagged gap logged as a finding is worse than an unlogged one: it launders uncertainty into record.**
- 📦 **PACKAGED July 31 (Hans) to roadmap row 8a** → `kiwi_latency_program.md`. ⚠️ **Lowest priority of the four levers — payoff scales with library size, near-zero for Hans today. Defer unless re-measurement at pickup changes the ranking.**
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-094 (where the actual waste lives) · D-WS9-092 · D-WS9-008 / `copyPlan` (the **Use again** path — genuinely a plan-instance copy, genuinely unrelated).

### D-WS9-096 — Meal swap HARD-deletes the `MealPlanItem` where PRD §8.4.2 specifies a soft delete — ✅ **BLAST RADIUS VERIFIED: no data loss** · 🟡 **audit-trail decision open**
- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[PRD-DIVERGENCE]` `[SCHEMA]` `[AUDIT]` · **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — low urgency, needs a ruling not an investigation.** **Owner:** WS10 or PRD redline at WS9 close
- **The divergence:** PRD **§8.4.2** specifies replacement as **create-new + soft-delete-old**, preserving day assignment **and audit history**. The code does **create-new + HARD delete**, preserving the day assignment (test-verified) but not the history.
- **✅ THE OPEN QUESTION IS NOW ANSWERED: ZERO FKs POINT AT `MealPlanItem`.** Every candidate reference resolves elsewhere — prep structure and step completions key on the plan id, grocery lists on the plan-instance id, item sources on the list-item id, order sessions on the list id. **No cascade, no constraint throw; a user's cooking and prep progress survives a mid-week swap.**
- **What IS destroyed with the row:** `recipeOverrideJson`, `ingredientOverrides`, `componentSelections` — **columns on the item itself, which the swap intentionally resets.** Correct behavior, not loss.
- ⚠️ **So this is an AUDIT-TRAIL gap, not a data-loss path**, and the `plan_meal_changed` activity event already preserves a trail. **The earlier concern that a mid-week swap might cascade-delete cooking progress is retired.**
- **THE DECISION:** convert to soft-delete for conformance, or **redline §8.4.2 to match the code**. ⚠️ **Chat-Claude's lean: redline the PRD.** A soft-delete adds a filtered-everywhere column to a hot path for a trail that already exists elsewhere — **conformance for its own sake is not a reason.**
- **Cross-ref:** PRD §8.4.2 · D-WS7-216 · D-WS9-004.

### D-WS9-097 — The plan list sorts on `createdAt` (= draft-EXPAND time), so a re-saved plan sorts as though it were older — 🟡 **OPEN (product decision)**
- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[PLANS-TAB]` `[UX]` `[SORT]` · **Status:** 🟡 OPEN · **Owner:** WS9 **3g** or WS10 · **Source:** Hans's device observation + probe A6
- **Observation:** after using **Use This Week** more than once, only one version saved (supersede working), **but the earlier-saved plan sorted ABOVE the later one** in a list ordered by date added.
- **✅ VERIFIED MECHANISM:** the list sorts on **`createdAt`, set at DRAFT-EXPAND time**, not at save; **activate updates the row in place and never refreshes it.** A plan's position reflects **when you first looked at it**, not when you committed it.
- **⚠️ CHAT HYPOTHESIS PARTLY WRONG — right outcome, wrong mechanism.** Chat-Claude proposed *"supersede updates in place, so a re-saved plan keeps its first-save timestamp."* **It is `activate` that updates in place, not supersede, and the retained timestamp is draft-expand time, not first-save time.** Recorded because *"right answer, wrong mechanism"* is the failure mode that survives review — a correct-looking conclusion stops the reader checking the reasoning.
- **THE DECISION:** sort on **`committedAt`** (added this block; it means *when the user chose this plan*), or keep `createdAt` and rename the UI's "date added" to something honest. ⚠️ **Chat-Claude's lean: `committedAt`** — **a user's mental model of "when I added this plan" is when they committed it, not when they first previewed it**, and previewing is now cheap and casual precisely because 3c made card-tap a browse action.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-032 (card-tap-as-browse, which created this gap).

### D-WS9-101 — User-assigned tags in both builders — ⛔ **DECLINED August 4, 2026. Nothing was built.**
- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[MEAL-BUILDER]` `[DISH-BUILDER]` `[SEARCH]` `[UX]` `[3F]` · **Status:** ⛔ **DECLINED** — the design was superseded twice (predictive-search entry → Hans's August 3 CLOSED-CHIP ruling, D-WS9-107), then the feature itself declined. **Owner: closed.**
- **Source:** Hans, August 2, 2026, raised unprompted: *"I'm not sure we need something filterable... maybe a 'tag' but I don't think we have tags for dishes or meals that the user enters/assigns anyway."*
- **What was true and stays true:** **`Meal.tags` and `Dish.tags` columns already exist** (no migration), the server already accepts and persists tags on both, and PRD §10.5.4 specifies a Tags chip section that was never built. Wizard candidates and templates already emit AI tags; the field was simply never **user**-editable.
- **⚠️ A FALSE CLAIM THIS ENTRY CARRIED, RETRACTED IN PLACE.** It read *"Search ALREADY targets tags… the retrieval half is built and waiting for input that never arrives."* **FALSE.** Phase 0 verified there is **no text search on meals or dishes anywhere in the codebase**; PRD §9.6's `ILIKE` MVP was **never implemented** (list endpoints carry ownership/archive filters and alpha/date/cook-time sorts only; the mobile tabs have **no search box**). ⚠️ **This was written into canon as established fact and became part of the cost basis on which 3f-2 was confirmed.**
- **⛔ THE DECLINE (Hans, August 4).** *"there's not much point in building something that someone can tag if the tags aren't usable"*, then the decisive challenge — **what is the purpose of tags over the preference-aligned attributes of a meal or dish?** Tested against existing typed and computed fields, **most of the proposed 12-chip vocabulary was redundant or contradictory**: *Quick night* duplicates `estimatedTimeMinutes` and can contradict it; *Hearty*/*Light* duplicate computed macros; *Crowd pleaser* duplicates `servingsDefault`. Only ~4–5 (*spicy*, *kid-friendly*, *meal-prep*, *one-pan*, *budget*) carried signal not already held somewhere better. ⚠️ **THE GENERAL LESSON: a second, unvalidated, user-typed channel for something the system already computes is a divergence generator.**
- **Reach also undercut it:** chips lived only in the two builders, i.e. manually-created content, while **1,182 of 1,458 meals are `batch_generated`** and tagged automatically. **A builder-only surface reaches the thinnest slice of a library.**
- **Superseded by D-WS9-109** — re-aim at typed attributes generation actually reads.
- **Redlines owed at WS9 close:** PRD **§10.5.4** Tags chip spec (declined, not deferred) · PRD **§10.6.1** Meal Detail tags row · PRD **§9.6 (LOCKED)** and **§9.3.3**, which describe a tags-inclusive search that **does not exist**.

### D-WS9-102 — What the swap sheet should RETURN, and Ask-Kiwi as a first-class alternate path (not a workaround)
- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[SWAP-SHEET]` `[AI]` `[CATALOG]` `[UX]` `[3F-4]` · **Status:** 🟡 **RULED IN SHAPE, mechanism unverified.** **Owner:** Block 3f-4 · **Source:** Hans, August 2, 2026, device-testing 3f-1, alongside BUG-058
- **RULING 1 — Ask Kiwi belongs in BOTH swap modes.** Hans, verbatim: *"in the Swap for Similar and Swap for Different, the Tell Kiwi functionality available in Add Meal should be present. So, if a user goes to the Find Similar and they don't see what they want they can do a Tell Kiwi like they would if they had composted their meal and used Add Meal. **This makes it an alternate path instead of an available workaround.**"*
  - ⚠️ **The framing is the ruling.** Today a user who dislikes every swap result must **back out, compost the meal, and re-add** to reach Ask Kiwi — ⚠️ **the workaround requires COMPOSTING a meal the user has not decided to discard**, and a dead end escapable only by destroying something is a bad dead end.
  - **This is the concrete product justification for D-WS9-018's Ask-Kiwi escape hatch**, which 3d deferred to 3f (*"the real Ask-Kiwi escape hatch belongs to Block 3f — one creator, two entry points"*). ⚠️ **Hans arrived at this independently of the spec** — a strong signal the deferred scope is correctly aimed.
  - **Build note:** the Ask-Kiwi screen is standalone with its own routing and header, **single one-shot**, not the 3–5-candidate contract the sheet needs; mounting it requires extraction into a prop-driven container **and** a contract widening. **The reuse precedent is the Add-Meals sheet**, which already renders the Ask-Kiwi card Hans describes.
- **RULING 2 (in shape) — the similarity corpus should span user meals AND the catalog.** Hans: *"If it's searching the user's meals it should probably do user and catalog meals."* ⚠️ **VERIFY THE CURRENT CORPUS BEFORE CHANGING IT.** A user-scoped search against a small library **fully explains BUG-058's thin, repetitive result set** with no similarity-logic defect at all — which would make corpus the dominant cause and prompt-tuning a wasted fix. **Measure first (§27: in-chat numbers are beliefs).** The catalog holds **1,124 `batch_generated` meals**; if not already in the corpus, adding it is likely the highest-leverage change to swap quality.
- **⚠️ RULING 3 — the similarity axis is PREPARATION AND EATING EXPERIENCE, not primary ingredient.** From Hans's Chicken-Parmesan calibration: *chicken piccata, spaghetti and meatballs, chicken fingers, baked chicken cutlets* are similar; *whole roast chicken* and *BBQ anything* are not. ⚠️ **The set CROSSES the protein boundary and EXCLUDES same-protein items**, so the operative axis is *breaded / saucy / Italian-American / weeknight-plated*, **not** *contains chicken*. ⚠️ **A fix that tightens ingredient matching moves in the wrong direction and will make results worse.**
  - **Do not assume an AI prompt is the lever.** Establish first whether Find Similar is an AI call, an embedding query, a keyword search, or a tag/cuisine filter. If it **is** a prompt, §7 applies in full: `aiPrompts.ts` is the single source of truth, version bumps are **diff-driven not hand-written**, and **cache-prefix boundaries are load-bearing.**
- **Cross-ref:** BUG-058 · D-WS9-018 · D-WS9-005 (import-to-slot append-vs-replace) · roadmap row 7 if duplicates prove to be in the data.

### D-WS9-105 — The system stores units as free text and does not understand most of them
- **Status:** 🔴 OPEN — **scope ruling needed. Chat's read is that this is a BLOCK, not a patch.** **Owner:** unassigned — needs Hans's sequencing call.
- **Origin:** Hans saved **"1 Pinch Salt"** during 3f-2 device testing and asked whether the system understands a pinch. **It does not.** Verbatim: *"lots of online recipes have pinches of this and that, so we should support it."*
- **VERIFIED (CC Phase 0 — read from code or queried from the DB):**
  - **`unit` is FREE TEXT** — plain text input, no autocomplete or enum, in **both** builders; Zod `z.string().min(1).max(40)`; Prisma a plain String. **There is no canonical unit list anywhere in the system.**
  - **Conversion exists but is PARTIAL** — a normalizer plus volume→cups, weight→grams, count units, and weight↔volume via grams where density is known. ⚠️ **`pinch` is in none of these sets — an opaque passthrough.**
  - ⚠️ **GROCERY CONSOLIDATION IS WHERE THIS BITES.** The merger buckets by `(canonical, unit)` and merges only measured↔measured and known count sub-units; **unconvertible groups stay separate rows.** So **1 pinch salt + 1 tsp salt → two grocery lines, deterministically**, after which an AI re-sweep may or may not fold them **with no pinch→tsp ratio to work from.** ⚠️ **Multi-meal grocery items are a stated product selling point, not an edge case — this is the case that matters.**
  - **Scale-at-render is quantity-only:** 1 pinch at 2× becomes "2 pinch" (the count-noun pluralizer covers clove/head but not pinch, and only on grocery render).
- ⚠️ **THE CATALOG'S UNIT VOCABULARY IS INCONSISTENT AND DIRTY — 37 distinct values.** Alias duplication at scale: `teaspoon` 10,410 / `tsp` 15 · `tablespoon` 7,165 / `tbsp` 50 · `pound` 1,481 / `lb` 40 · `ounce` 1,922 / `oz` 26 · `cup`/`cups` · `clove`/`cloves` · `can`/`cans`. **The normalizer aliases the common ones, so the aliases are survivable. The dirty values are NOT — they are BUG-059.**
- **What a resolution must cover:** a canonical unit set · normalization on write · small-measure handling (pinch, dash, to-taste) · consolidation coverage for the new units · whether free-text entry is preserved or constrained.
- ⚠️ **Scoping caution:** constraining `unit` to an enum is a **breaking change against 37 existing distinct values across thousands of catalog rows.** Any resolution needs a migration plan for the existing corpus, not just a forward-looking rule.
- **Cross-ref:** **BUG-059** (the dirty values — data defect, distinct from this feature gap) · **D-WS9-106** · roadmap row 7.

### D-WS9-106 — "Salt, to taste" is not representable: quantity is a required positive number
- **Status:** 🔴 OPEN — **schema gap. Needs a nullable-quantity migration; deliberately deferred out of 3f-2.** **Owner:** unassigned — pairs with D-WS9-105.
- **VERIFIED (CC Phase 0):** the shared server ingredient schema requires `quantity: z.number().positive().max(10000)` for **both** meal and dish saves, and the column is a **required Float**. **There is no null quantity anywhere in the model.**
- **Consequence today:** a blank quantity is allowed in both builders and **silently becomes `1` at save**, so *"salt, to taste"* is stored and consolidated as **"1 unit salt."** ⚠️ **It reaches the grocery list as a real quantity of a real thing.**
- **Ruled in 3f-2 (Hans, August 3, 2026):** blank stays allowed and keeps defaulting to `1`, because true no-quantity **cannot** be honored without the migration and blocking save on blank would break a legitimate use case. ⚠️ **Accepted-for-now behavior, NOT a resolution — the entry stays open.**
- **What the fix requires:** nullable `quantity` (and any parallel model), the Zod boundary relaxed to match, **and every consumer audited** — quantity formatting, scale-at-render (multiplying null), the grocery `(canonical, unit)` bucketing, macro calculation. ⚠️ **The consumer audit is the real cost, not the migration:** a nullable column with unaudited consumers converts a silent-wrong-value bug into a crash class.
- **Related but distinct:** 3f-2 follow-up 3 made non-blank garbage and ≤ 0 **block save with an inline error** in both builders. **Blank was deliberately excluded.** ⚠️ **PRD §10.5.6's required-field list does not name quantity validity at all** → WS9-close redline.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-105 · BUG-059 · PRD §10.5.6.

### D-WS9-107 — The `tags` column is doing double duty as a search index, and the chips ruling makes that a problem
- **Status:** ✅ **RESOLVED August 4, 2026 by Phase 0 measurement — then moot when the chips feature itself was DECLINED (D-WS9-101).** Findings retained: load-bearing for D-WS9-109 and BUG-058. **Owner: closed. Block 3f-2b was commissioned, audited, and shelved without a build.**
- **Hans's ruling that created this, August 3, 2026 (superseded D-WS9-101's open-tag design):** classification metadata via a **CLOSED chip set** in the builders — *"we don't want users to have to scroll up and down a whole preference screen if they're adding a meal or dish. they can 'tag' it, but it would write to the metadata in the right spot so filters work cleanly if we want to offer filtering on meals in the future."* ⚠️ **And separately: social/sharing tags, if they ever exist, are a DIFFERENT field** — *"I don't want to moderate meal classification tags."*
- **The problem it exposed:** the catalog's meal-tag values are almost entirely **chip-shaped machine metadata** (`medium`, `easy`, `american`, `cajun/creole`), because `buildTags` is literally `{cuisine.toLowerCase(), difficulty}` — **the system vocabulary living inside what Hans ruled is the user-facing column.**
- ✅ **PHASE 0 FINDINGS — VERIFIED from schema and code. The standing reference on `tags`.**
  - **Both models already have `tags String[] @default([])`. No migration was ever required**, and the server already accepts and persists tags on POST and PATCH for both: **zero server work would have been needed.** ⚠️ **`kiwi_codebase_map.md` omitted Dish's `tags` column and was WRONG** — corrected in the same batch.
  - ⚠️ **THE DISH-SIDE COLLISION WITH D-WS7-050 NEVER FIRED.** The chip vocabulary is a **descriptor set**, not cuisine/difficulty — PRD §10.5.4 lists Cuisine, Difficulty and Prep/Cook time as **separate header controls** and Tags as a distinct fourth section. **Decisive evidence: the dish corpus contains ZERO cuisine and ZERO difficulty values** (19 distinct, all descriptors), because `Dish` has no cuisine column and `buildTags` is meal-only.
  - ⚠️ **THE "SEARCH-INDEX HACK" HYPOTHESIS IS FALSIFIED** — flagged UNVERIFIED and wrong: **no text search on meals or dishes exists.**
  - **`buildTags` emits exactly `{cuisine.toLowerCase(), difficulty}`** — ⚠️ **the prior audit's "plus model output" was WRONG for the batch path.** Corpus descriptors come from the AI builder/reformat path.
  - ⚠️ **THREE LIVE NON-SEARCH CONSUMERS READ `tags`** — the real blast radius, and it survives the decline: **(1) Find-Similar's AI input** — **BUG-058 is open and unfixed; changing tag semantics changes an unfixed bug's inputs**; **(2) the plan-gen shortlist**; **(3) the home "Tried & True" rail label**, which renders `tags[0]` — for a batch meal, the lowercased cuisine.
  - **Corpus (re-measured, not trusted from the prior audit):** meals **103 distinct**, 1233/1458 = **84.6%** (batch_generated 100%); head is machine noise — `medium` 617, `easy` 565, `american` 348, plus ~60 near-duplicate cuisine slugs. Dishes **19 distinct**, 52/3452 = **1.5%**, all descriptors. Validation caps tags at 10, each 1–40 chars.
  - ⚠️ **THE ROOT DUPLICATION IS STILL LIVE AND UNADDRESSED:** `buildTags` stamps cuisine and difficulty into `tags` **even though both are real columns on `Meal`**. Stopping that at source is ~8 lines but touches BUG-058's input and the plan-gen shortlist. **Not done, not scoped, deliberately left alone.**
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-101 (declined) · **D-WS9-109 (the re-aim)** · D-WS7-050 · BUG-058 · PRD §10.5.4, §9.3.3, §9.6.

### D-WS9-108 — Kiwi-assist is EITHER/OR by ruling: hand-enter, or let Kiwi generate. Not both, not merged.
- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[DISH-BUILDER]` `[AI-ASSIST]` `[UX]` `[3F]` · **Status:** ✅ **RULED August 4, 2026 — NOT A DEFECT. Current behavior is correct. NO CODE CHANGE.** Owner: closed. ⚠️ **Logged specifically so a future chat does not re-chase it.**
- **What was raised:** the Kiwi-assist toggles hide as soon as content exists, so a user who types "chicken thighs" and wants Kiwi to build the rest around it has lost the option. Chat-Claude framed it as possibly wrong for ingredients and right for steps.
- **HANS'S RULING, verbatim:** *"users can EITHER enter their own ingredients and/or steps, or they can have Kiwi generate their ingredients and/or steps. they're two separate actions in the app, and I think the flow is fine."* His reasoning: an assist that must merge into partially-entered content — without overwriting, without duplicating, without knowing how complete the entry is — is a hard problem with little payoff.
- **VERIFIED implementation:** the ingredients assist and the steps assist gate on **two independent `.some()` derivations, so the "and/or" in the ruling is satisfied** (hand-enter ingredients, still have Kiwi generate steps). **Derived, not latched** — recomputed each render, so clearing a field restores the toggle. Both directions checked.
- ⚠️ **meal-builder has NO per-field assist toggles at all, and this is correct, not a gap.** Ingredients and steps live at the dish level; its assist is a different model. **See D-WS6-031(c) — the PRD parity requirement there rests on a superseded premise.**
- ⚠️ **Canon note:** the remediation and screen-plan docs say *"both Kiwi-assist toggles hide when content already exists."* **"Both" means the two toggles in dish-builder, not one per builder.** That wording misled a downstream handoff into assuming meal-builder had them. Accurate as written; ambiguous in isolation.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS6-031(b)(c) · D-WS9-104 (dormant premium seam on the same rows).

### D-WS9-109 — Re-aim: typed attributes that generation READS, instead of user tags nothing consumes
- **Tags:** `[GENERATION]` `[PREFERENCES]` `[SCHEMA]` `[PRODUCT]` · **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — direction ruled August 4, 2026; scope not yet defined.** **Owner:** post-WS9, plan-generation/catalog track. **NOT a WS9 restyle item.**
- **Source:** Hans, after shelving 3f-2b: *"there's not much point in building something that someone can tag if the tags aren't usable"*, then the decisive one — **what is the purpose of tags over the preference-aligned attributes of a meal or dish?**
- ⚠️ **THE FINDING THAT KILLED THE TAGS FEATURE AND CREATED THIS ONE:** most of the proposed chip vocabulary duplicated fields the system **already holds as typed or computed data**, and a user-typed value can **contradict** the computed one — *Quick night* vs `estimatedTimeMinutes`; *Hearty*/*Light* vs computed macros; *Crowd pleaser* vs `servingsDefault`; dietary chips vs `Meal.allergens` + wizard prefs (**safety-adjacent — see D-WS9-077/-078**).
- **THE REAL GAPS — attributes with genuine signal and no home today** (**each still needs verification against the live preference schema before anything is built**): **spice tolerance** · **kid-friendliness** · **cleanup burden** (one-pan / sheet-pan — ⚠️ possibly *derivable* from step data) · **batch-cooking / meal-prep intent** · **cost** (⚠️ **no cost data exists on meals at all**).
- **THE DIRECTION:** add these as **typed preference and meal/dish fields that plan generation actually reads**, rather than a second free-form user channel. Serves Hans's original goal (*"write to the metadata in the right spot so filters work cleanly"*) **without** creating a divergence generator, and it **puts the consumer before the input** — the inverse of 3f-2b, which would have shipped input with no consumer.
- ⚠️ **THE SEQUENCING RULE THIS ARC EARNED:** 3f-2b was fully audited and ready to build before anyone asked what would consume its output. **Ask what reads a field before building what writes it.**
- **Open questions:** which gaps generation can actually use · whether cleanup burden is derived rather than stored · whether these are user preferences, meal attributes, or both · whether the catalog's 1,182 batch meals can be back-stamped or coverage starts at zero · ⚠️ **whether any of this interacts with `buildTags`' still-live cuisine/difficulty duplication.**
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-101 (declined — this supersedes it) · D-WS9-107 · D-WS9-077/-078 · BUG-058 · PRD §10.5.4 / §9.4.

### D-WS9-111 — A newly ADDED meal lands at the bottom of the plan list, and Hans wants it visible — but "put it at the top" collides with a LOCKED server-canonical ordering rule
- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[PLAN-REVIEW]` `[POLISH]` `[PRD-COLLISION]` `[PREMISE-VERIFIED]` · **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — needs Hans's ruling. Do NOT build "move it to the top" as stated.** **Owner:** **3g** or a late-WS9 polish pass — **not 3f-4**, which owns the swap sheet while this is the *append* path.
- **Source:** Hans, 3f-3 device test: *"when a meal is added (not changed or swapped), it should be at the top of the meals list, not the bottom."* ⚠️ **The add-vs-swap distinction maps exactly onto the append-vs-replace split 3f-3 built:** a **replace** preserves the day assignment so the row stays put; an **append** carries **no day**, so it sorts to the bottom.
- ⚠️ **THE COLLISION — PRD §8 pins this twice, and one pin is LOCKED and server-canonical:** *"Meals with no day assigned appear in a separate **Unscheduled** section at the **bottom** of the meals list"*; and **`[REDLINE LOCKED May 27, 2026 — WS7-4-D c15]`** *Item ordering (server-canonical)*: **(1)** assigned items first, `assignedDayOfWeek` Sun→Sat · **(2)** unscheduled last, **pinned to the bottom** · **(3)** tiebreaker `positionIndex ASC` (implemented in a shared sort helper, Sun=0..Sat=6, **unscheduled=7**). ⚠️ **The stated rationale is that mobile, the future web app, and every analytics consumer see the SAME canonical order.** Breaking it for one screen's convenience defeats the reason it exists.
- **FOUR READINGS, VERY DIFFERENT COSTS — and the last is probably what he actually wants:**
  1. **Float added meals to the top of the whole list.** ⛔ **Rejected on sight** — the one thing the LOCKED rule exists to prevent.
  2. **Top of the *unscheduled cluster*.** Cheap and spec-compatible (the tiebreaker is already `positionIndex ASC`). ⚠️ **But it does not solve the complaint:** with five scheduled meals the new one is still sixth, still below the fold.
  3. **Assign a day at add time.** Puts it in the scheduled block, but the picker does not ask for a day and the PRD explicitly holds *"days can be unassigned"* is valid. **A product change, not polish.**
  4. ⚠️ **THE COMPLAINT MAY NOT BE ABOUT ORDER AT ALL — it may be about CONFIRMATION.** You add a meal and nothing visibly happens, because the row appears somewhere you are not looking. **Scroll-to-and-highlight, or a toast naming the meal, would satisfy that with ZERO change to the LOCKED ordering.** ⚠️ **An app-level toast provider already exists above the navigator** — §27.2 reuse candidate, no new infrastructure.
- ⚠️ **PREMISE VERIFIED BEFORE SURFACING (§27, and the 3d precedent that earned the rule).** In 3d, chat-Claude put a product decision to Hans resting on an unverified technical premise and **he spent a ruling on a problem that did not exist.** The ordering rule here was read from the PRD and confirmed LOCKED **before** this entry was written. **Still unverified: whether the Add Meals picker sets `positionIndex` at all**, and whether the complaint is order or confirmation — **that second one only Hans can answer.**
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-005 · D-WS7-213 (wizard day-assignment ordering — perishables early; **any auto-day-assignment reading must not fight it**) · PRD §8 `[LOCKED]`.

### D-WS9-114 — Pricing ruled ($9.99 / $99.99, no feature tiers) + post-trial state direction
- **Tags:** `[BUSINESS]` `[MONETIZATION]` `[STRIPE]` `[FEATUREGATES]` · **Status:** ✅ RULED (pricing + no-tiers) / 🟡 **DIRECTION ONLY (post-trial state)** — locks at Stripe commissioning, roadmap row 9.
- **Source:** Documentation-reconciliation session, August 5, 2026. **Amends D-WS9-020's open sub-decisions and supersedes `kiwi_business_plan.md` §3's $69.99 assumption.**
- **✅ RULED — pricing: $9.99/month · $99.99/year.** ~17% off, essentially two months free — the category-standard framing; $69.99 was the aggressive end.
- ⚠️ **The trade-off was surfaced and the ruling survived it.** A shallower annual discount pulls fewer users to annual, and annual is what fixes the LTV problem (monthly-SKU LTV ~$42 at 6-month retention, below the $50 CAC trigger). **Sensitivity at ruling time: even if the mix degrades 60/40 → 75/25 monthly/annual, blended net ARPU is ~$8.14/mo, still above the $7.08 modeled at $69.99.** Net ARPU at the assumed 60/40 rises to **~$7.93**; annual LTV ~$59 → ~$85 prepaid. ⚠️ **Business plan §5's scenario table still uses $7.08 and understates revenue ~12% — left deliberately un-recomputed; refresh from real beta mix, not another assumption.**
- **✅ RULED — no feature tiers.** Hans: *"nothing gated and it's either premium or not."* ⚠️ **This unblocks D-WS9-104**, which was explicitly waiting on it. Per-feature "Premium" pills were the wrong SHAPE under a time-based trial, which is why they were removed rather than relabeled — **and under a no-tiers model there are no in-app premium indicators to design at all.** The dormant `premiumLabel` seam stays dormant.
- **🟡 DIRECTION — post-trial state (Hans, verbatim August 5, 2026):** *"read only after. 'your trial ended, but you have an active plan, so you can keep going and using cook and prep mode without being blocked.'"*
  - **Read-only =** view everything already created + **email old lists**. ⚠️ **No AI calls of any kind** — no plan generation, no step or ingredient generation, no meal/dish building, no imports, no Kiwi supplements. **Hans's hard line: a user must not keep building and generating on his dime.**
  - **The carve-out is paid for deliberately.** Hans: cook and prep cost money, and he is spending it because *"if someone is loving the app and sees value because we gave them a few more days without blocking their dinner tonight that's good."* ⚠️ **The trial always ends mid-loop** — active plan, half-checked list, prep started. **Hard-locking there is the worst conversion moment available**; plain read-only barely helps, since an uncheckable grocery list is functionally dead.
  - ⚠️ **COST PREMISE TO VERIFY BEFORE LOCKING.** Hans budgeted cook **and** prep as expensive. **Canon says the cooking sequencer stopped being an AI call** — BUG-018's fix made it deterministic (`usedAI=false`, ~290ms, `LLMCallLog` delta 0), per PRD §13.5.4/§13.5.5. **Prep narration remains a real AI call** (~$0.22/user-week pre-amortization). **If that holds, exposure is prep-only — cheaper than budgeted. CANON-SAYS, NOT VERIFIED: one grep at Stripe commissioning.**
  - **Weighting:** matters most under a **no-card** trial; card-upfront auto-converts, so post-trial state only reaches active cancellers. **Card-upfront vs no-card remains OPEN** (D-WS9-020 sub-decision 1), as do checkout rails and the abuse guard.
- **Business-ops state confirmed same session:** entity via **Stripe Atlas** ✅ · **DUNS** ✅ · **Apple Developer** ✅ · **Google Play Developer** ✅ · **bank account** ❌ · **Apple/Google small-business enrollment** ❌. ⚠️ **The 15%-vs-30% delta is ~$1,900/month at the 1,300-subscriber scenario** — tracked in `kiwi_go_live_todos.md`.

### D-WS9-115 — §A amended: counters leave §1, authority is `max(heading-grep, pointer line)`, VOID stubs encoded
- **Tags:** `[PROCESS]` `[CANON]` `[IDHYGIENE]` · **Status:** ✅ RULED (Hans, August 5, 2026), executed same day.
- **Source:** Defects in D-WS9-113's own implementation, surfaced by a fresh chat's §30 gate. **Recorded here rather than by rewriting that entry (append-only).**
- ⚠️ **DEFECT 1 — THE DECOY `§1`.** §A named *"`kiwi_remediation_progress.md` §1"* as the single source of position, but **two different things answered to "§1":** the unnumbered current-position block at the top, and a literal `## 1. State at a glance` further down that was **stale by an entire workstream** (pre-renumber workstream names, *"WS7-5d NEXT"*, HEAD `80ab5b2`, a next-D-WS7 counter **139 IDs behind**; the H1 read *"(WS6 in progress)"* and `## 0` pointed at a file that **does not exist**). ⚠️ **A fresh chat obeying §A literally would have taken a June snapshot as current.** **Resolved: `## 1` emptied (anchor kept, content deleted per §A's own delete-don't-update rule), H1 fixed, `## 0` rewritten.**
- ⚠️ **THE GENERAL LESSON — bigger than the fix. CONCENTRATING AUTHORITY IN ONE NAMED LOCATION IS ONLY SAFE IF NOTHING ELSE ANSWERS TO THAT NAME.** §A produced this failure the same day it was written, and neither the authoring nor the reviewing chat caught it — both read the block they expected. **Before declaring any doc or section canonical, grep for competing claimants to the name.**
- ⚠️ **DEFECT 2 — THE COUNTER WENT STALE WITHIN HOURS.** D-WS9-113 and -114 were minted with the deferred log's pointer advanced atomically (correct, §6), but **`§1`'s counter line was never advanced** — in the very document §A had just made authoritative for counters. **The §30 gate caught it; a fresh chat reported it would otherwise have minted a collision on its first ID.**
- **THE RULING.** ⚠️ **Counters leave the current-position block entirely.** They live in each log beside the entries they count, because **§6 requires minting and pointer-move to be one atomic step and atomicity across two files is not achievable.**
- ⚠️ **BUT "DELETE THE POINTER, TRUST HEADING-GREP" WAS REJECTED.** The two mechanisms are blind to **different, non-overlapping** failures:

| Mechanism | Catches | Blind to |
|---|---|---|
| Heading-grep | Pointer stale — **this entry's Defect 2** | ID consumed, entry never written |
| Pointer line | Consumed-but-unwritten — **the D-WS7-215 incident** | Pointer never advanced |

- **Authority is therefore `max(heading-grep, pointer line)`.** Measured: **D-WS7 has 194 entries across 001–216 with 22 gaps** (`66, 68, 76, 84, 86–96, 99, 137–139, 143, 165, 173`); **`143` and `165` were consumed in code with no entry ever written.** **D-WS9 (114 entries), D-WS6 (74) and BUG (60) have ZERO gaps.**
- ⚠️ **THE THIRD MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTED AND IS NOW ENCODED.** `D-WS9-088` is a deliberate **VOID stub** converting a would-be gap into a visible heading — **why D-WS9 has zero gaps and D-WS7 has 22.** **Ruled: any ID handed into a CC prompt that comes back without an entry gets a VOID stub at block close.** ⚠️ **The 22 D-WS7 gaps are NOT backfilled** — next is 217, above every gap, and nobody mints backward.
- **ALSO LOGGED THIS SESSION:**
  - ⚠️ **`D-WS7-126` HAS TWO DIFFERENT ENTRIES UNDER ONE ID** — 449 ID-shaped headings, only **448 unique**: a B4 delete-parity decision and a soft-delete reconcile-suppression decision marked RESOLVED. ⚠️ **`sort -u` hides this from every counter check in the working agreements. Not merged and not renumbered** — IDs are referenced from code, commits and CC prompts.
  - ⚠️ **A GUARD CITATION WAS CALLED FABRICATED. ✅ CORRECTED AUGUST 6, 2026 — THE GUARD IS REAL.** It was declared fabricated because its cited symbol and path had zero matches. ✅ **Code says otherwise (3f-4 Phase 1, VERIFIED):** the guard is in `app/meal-builder.tsx`, tagged **BUG-002 / D-WS7-169**, reading almost exactly as circulated — *"Do NOT restore a `setServingsDefault(sourceMeal.effectiveServings)` line."* **`setServingsDefault` has EIGHT real matches** there. **The only wrong parts of the original citation were the ID (D-WS7-169, not -171) and the file/line.** ⚠️ **`kiwi_ws9_screen_plan.md` still carries the wrong ID — it needs the ID CORRECTED, not the line deleted.**
  - ⚠️ **AND `lib/meal-builder-state.ts` EXISTS.** A 3f-4 Phase 0 agent reported it absent; a Phase 1 prompt repeated that absence *as a correction to canon*; **both were wrong.** Two files exist — the screen and a pure-helpers module, where the update-input builder **does** omit `servingsDefault`, deliberately. **Canon was right; the correction was wrong; the correction to the correction was also wrong.**
  - ⚠️ **THREE LAYERS, EACH WRONG DIFFERENTLY — THE MOST TRANSFERABLE THING HERE.** (1) A handoff carried a citation with a wrong ID and path. (2) A doc-only chat, finding no match for the *path*, declared the guard fabricated — **inferring non-existence of a thing from non-existence of its citation.** (3) A code-reading agent searched the wrong root and reported the file absent, making (2) look confirmed. ⚠️ **"I could not find it" is not "it does not exist," and a doc-only search cannot establish either. ONLY CODE ESTABLISHES EXISTENCE (§8.1).**
  - ⚠️ **THREE TIMES IN TWO DAYS, TWO CORRECT NUMBERS LOOKED LIKE A CONTRADICTION BECAUSE NOBODY STATED THE DENOMINATOR.** `453` (all `^### ` headings) and `449` (ID-shaped only) were **both right**; the six-heading difference is five copies of *"Items currently anticipated to be picked up here from earlier WS"* plus one *"WS6 own deferrals"*. **§24.3 now states both denominators.**
