### D-WS9-225 — 🔵 Pack yield is DATA, not a garlic-only constant: the subUnit ladder exists for 1 of 1,569 rows, and 31 count-sold foods are uncomputable for the same reason garlic cloves was

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[GROCERY]` `[CATALOG]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 7, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — measured, unbuilt; the CSV block (D-WS9-226) supplies the data, this is the mechanism** · **Cross-ref:** 🔴 **BUG-215** · **BUG-188 / BUG-213** · D-WS9-220 · D-WS9-218 (🟠 contested — this is NOT the `fromUnit` column) · D-WS9-222 · D-WS9-189.
- **Measured (read-only audit, September 7):** `INGREDIENT_CONVERSIONS` carries exactly ONE `subUnit` entry (garlic: head → 10 cloves), so **1 of 1,569 catalog rows resolves a measured need to a count-pack through a ladder.** Meanwhile **31 rows sell by a count unit against a measured default unit** — green cabbage (head/cup), red cabbage, fresh basil leaves (bunch/cup), fresh chives (bunch/tbsp), broccolini, fresh pineapple, lemon zest… — and every one is uncomputable in the same way `garlic cloves` was in BUG-215. **This is BUG-188's bunch-sold-herb problem generalised past herbs**, and BUG-188's own analysis already named the discriminator: yield per pack.
- **The ruling this asks for (chat-Claude's proposal, licence to refuse):** *yield per pack* becomes a per-ingredient DATA field read by the same ladder code that serves garlic today — `packYield {unit, perPack}` — populated from `pack_yields.csv` (Hans's evening pass) and required at intake for any ingredient whose pack unit and default unit differ in dimension. **The garlic constant becomes the first row of that table, not a special case.** ⚠️ **Not D-WS9-218's column**: that proposed a basis unit on the *relation*; this puts the yield on the *ingredient*, where the pack lives, and the component pool keeps reading relations as it does now.
- ⚠️ **Do not build the ladder generalisation before BUG-215's survivor fix** — a ladder that lives on the ingredient is only as good as the fold's choice of ingredient.
- ✅ **HANS'S FIGURES, RULED September 7, 2026, and they are the data this entry was asking for.** A supermarket herb bunch is **~1 oz** — that one number resolves 17 of the low-confidence rows. A bunch yields **2 cups of leaves uncut, 1 cup chopped**, and *"1 cup cilantro"* with no cut named means **leaves and stems as bought, which the user cuts per the recipe.** Celery **8 stalks/bunch** · pineapple **4 cups of chunks** (⚠️ **NOT USDA's 905 g, which is the whole fruit including skin and core — the shipped gate would have taken it**) · watermelon: a recipe's *pound* means **flesh, ~6 lb of a ~10 lb melon** · American cheese **¾ oz supermarket single, not the 1 oz deli slice** · chicken halves: the 4 lb pack is **one bird, two halves, ~2 lb each**.
- 🔴 **AND ONE ANSWER THAT IS NOT A FIGURE AT ALL, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL FINDING.** Asked for a grams-per-bunch for `fennel fronds`, Hans ruled the row out of existence: *"I don't think there's a need to put fronds on a list. tops are part of the bulb and come with it."* **A part that arrives free with its parent must never generate its own purchase line — and the mechanism for that already exists and is not a pack figure: a `component` relation with `coHarvestable = true`, exactly as lemon zest rides along with the lemon.** ⚠️ **So a `pack_dimension_straddle` is TWO different defects wearing one label: a missing yield figure, or a missing co-harvest relation. Ask which before pricing anything.** **Sweep the 31 straddlers for the second kind before authoring figures for them** — herb stems, zests, tops, trimmings and fronds are all candidates.

### D-WS9-226 — 🔵 Ingredient INTAKE: a new row must arrive computable or flagged — never with an AI pack sized to one plan's need and written back catalog-wide

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[GROCERY]` `[CATALOG]` `[SCHEMA]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 7, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — Phase 0 DONE and the product decision RULED (b) September 7; ready to commission after the grocery P1 block** · **Cross-ref:** 🔴 **BUG-124** (the writer) · **D-WS9-225** · D-WS9-222 · D-WS9-224 · BUG-188 · D-WS9-214 (precedent, see refutation) · D-WS9-181.
- **Hans's question, verbatim (September 6):** *"if we get a new ingredient from a wizard or import meal, will it get picked up and processed appropriately by the current rules?"* **Measured answer: NO.** One runtime creation point (`ingredientResolve`), reached from manual meal/dish save + PATCH, recipe import, the wizard and store-fill (Tell Kiwi does not reach it); **nothing at runtime writes `ingredient_relations`, nothing outside the seed writes `ingredient_aliases`** — two search shapes each, gitignore-blind, raw SQL checked. A new row gets: name · keyword-inferred category · the first mention's unit · a pack only if one of 58 static names hits · fire-and-forget USDA nutrition · **no `conversionRef`, no relations, no aliases, ever.** Catalog today: 1,078 null packs (68.7%), 236 `conversionRef` (15%), 1 `subUnit`.
- 🔴 **THE PRECEDENT REFUTED:** the handoff proposed copying D-WS9-214's *"deterministic baseline + AI pass at creation, unioned."* **There is no ingredient-level allergen path** — `Ingredient` has no allergen column; allergens are stamped on `Meal` by a pure function over names. The SHAPE (deterministic first, AI second, unioned, flagged) still applies; the CODE cannot be copied.
- **The design (chat-Claude's calls, delegated; Hans may object):** (1) **`Ingredient.createdAt` / `updatedAt`** — absent today, so intake cannot be measured at all; cheapest first fix. (2) **`Ingredient.packSource`** enum `static | csv | ai_gapfill | user` + **`packReviewedAt`** — `reviewedByHuman` exists only on `IngredientRelation`; the BUG-096 review lives in a CSV, not the catalog. (3) **The gap-fill stops receiving the asking plan's need** — it asks for the smallest common retail pack of the food, not a pack for `requestedQuantity`; the result persists with `packSource = ai_gapfill` so it is visible, reviewable and exportable, never mistaken for a fact. (4) **An idempotent CSV load script** for `pack_sizes.csv`, `pack_yields.csv`, `subsumes_direction.csv`, `unit_conversions.csv`, keyed on the stable ids in column 1, writing `packSource = csv`. (5) **A standing export of `packSource = ai_gapfill` rows** so the next evening pass is a list, not a hunt.
- ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 7, 2026): (b).** When a brand-new ingredient has no reviewed pack, the shopper sees the retail-shaped AI proposal, persisted as `packSource = ai_gapfill` **with the asking plan's need removed from the prompt** (option (a), the need-only staple-style line, was the alternative). **AND — Hans's addition, verbatim: *"it should try and also in the future send me an email to review if needed."*** So the standing export of `ai_gapfill` rows (design item 5) is not a file Hans goes looking for: **when unreviewed `ai_gapfill` rows exist, he gets an email listing them** — mechanism to be chosen in the build (a scheduled task that reads the export, or the api-server sending via Resend once row 3a lands); either way the trigger is *rows exist*, not a calendar.
- ⚠️ **Sequencing:** BUG-214 + BUG-215 + BUG-216 first (the P1 block); then this block, whose CSV load can be built before the CSVs are filled and run when they are. **Every write in this block runs on a Neon branch first** (D-WS9-181's mechanism, per the September 7 acceleration review).
- 🔴 **MEASURED September 7, 2026 — THE RECURRING-ITEM POPULATION IS THE WORST-SERVED IN THE CATALOG, AND A `pack_class` FILTER WOULD HAVE MISSED ALL OF IT.** Of the 9 recurring rows on one live list: **2 packs came from the static default table; 7 are Haiku gap-fills; and 4 of those 7 carry a NULL `ingredientId`, so there is nowhere to write the answer back and they are re-asked on EVERY generation, forever** (`coffee`, `pet treats`, `paper towels`, `toilet paper`). ⚠️ **Meanwhile `pack_class` scores the recurring set 0 null and 0 need-shaped — it looks clean, because the classification is keyed on CATALOG ROWS and four of these lines have no catalog row at all.**
- ✅ **SO THE CSV PASS GROUPS RECURRING ITEMS BY PACK PROVENANCE, NOT BY `pack_class`** — static / catalog / `ai_gapfill` / no-row-at-all. **That is also the argument for `packSource` being a column rather than a derived guess:** the thing that identifies a bad pack is where it came from, and today that is only recoverable by re-deriving three separate lookups per row.
- 🔴 **AND THE INTAKE PROBLEM IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL — IT FIRED DURING THE VERIFICATION ITSELF.** Hans built one meal through the mode-A parser and it minted **`onion` and `diced onion` as separate catalog rows with separate fold keys**, putting **four onion rows** on one list (`White onion`, `Yellow onion`, `onion`, `diced onion`). ⚠️ **`diced onion` is a PREP MODIFIER that became a catalog row.** The same meal left three ground-beef rows. **This is the intake path manufacturing exactly the duplicate-name population D-WS9-189 has spent the arc folding away — one meal, six new rows of it.** ⚠️ **Any intake fix that does not normalise prep modifiers out of the ingredient name will keep feeding the fold work it should never have been given.**
- ⚠️ **Two catalog-drift instances found in passing, both BUG-124's shape:** `limes` resolves to catalog `lime` whose pack reads `"2 limes"` but the row renders `"1 lime"`; and catalog `bananas` holds `"1 banana"` while the curated static default for it says `"1 bunch"` — **a catalog row that has drifted away from the table it was seeded from.**

✅ **`unit_conversions.csv` REVIEW CLOSED — HANS RULED ALL FOUR OPEN ROWS, September 8, 2026.** ⚠️ **The review surface was **51 rows**, not the 55 canon had been carrying — "51 low + 4 refusals" double-counted, because all four refusals ARE low-confidence rows.** Chat-Claude read all 51; 47 cleared, including the two highest-reach (chipotle in adobo ×19 live rows at 12 g, bay leaves ×10 at 0.2 g).
- ✅ **`whole chicken halves` = 907 g each — the lane's assumption was RIGHT.** Hans: *"2 halves per 4 lbs of chicken halves. If I need 4 halves, I need 8 lbs."* **The row is confirmed, not corrected** — worth recording because the lane explicitly flagged it as a coin-flip that would have been a clean 2× error the other way.
- ✅ **`hoagie rolls` = 57 g → **106 g** (Hans: *"106, medium"*).** 🔴 **THE LANE'S PREMISE WAS WRONG, NOT JUST ITS NUMBER: it wrote *"USDA carries no record for hoagie rolls"* and reached for SR Legacy's "Rolls, hard (includes kaiser), 3½″ dia" = 57 g. USDA FNDDS food code 51157000 "Roll, submarine, hoagie, white" DOES exist and carries three per-roll weights — 73 g small (5½″), 106 g medium (8″), 153 g large (11½″).** ⚠️ **VERIFIED VIA A USDA MIRROR (nutritionvalue.org), NOT A DIRECT FDC READ — the loading block confirms the food code before writing the value.** 🔵 **THE TRANSFERABLE PART: a "no USDA record" negative from ONE database view is a §27.3 single-grep negative. SR Legacy and FNDDS are different corpora; the ladder pass searched one and concluded the food was absent.**
- ✅ **`fennel fronds` — KEEP 7 tbsp per bunch, and fix the REAL problem with a component edge, not a number (Hans).** His constraint, verbatim: *"I don't want to have a fennel bulb for shaved fennel and a fennel bulb for the fronds on the same grocery list."* 🔵 **That is exactly what the D-WS9-189 A3 component pool already does for garlic (2 heads → 17 cloves, LIVE): fronds are a COMPONENT of the bulb, so a frond need is satisfied from the bulb already on the list and no second bulb appears.** ⚠️ **MEASURED September 8: `fennel fronds` has ZERO relations and ZERO aliases, so nothing connects it to a bulb today, and no row in the 260-row CSV references fennel at all.** 🔴 **UNVERIFIED AND IT GATES THE FIX: whether a `fennel bulb` catalog row EXISTS is not answerable from this CSV (it is a 260-row subset of ~1,569). One catalog query settles it — if there is no bulb row, the edge has nothing to attach to.** ✅ **7 tbsp/bunch stays as the fallback for a recipe that needs fronds with no bulb on the list. Blast radius is 1 live row, so this is cheap either way.**
- ✅ **THE FOUR REFUSALS ARE PERMANENTLY BLANK, NOT A GAP TO FILL — Hans ruled the rows out of mass consolidation entirely.** Verbatim: *"applewood chips are wood, toothpicks/skewers are also wood (and skewers could be metal)… we don't need to consolidate those rows."* 🔴 **WRITE THAT DOWN EXPLICITLY, BECAUSE AN EMPTY CELL LOOKS LIKE UNFINISHED WORK: a future pass must not try to invent grams for these four. The blanks ARE the answer.**
- ✅ **AND HANS NAMED THE PRODUCT REASON THEY SHOULD STAY VISIBLE AS THEIR OWN LINES:** *"I saw a recipe that told me to buy skewers, which was great to see - they're like an uncommon not staple thing that people often have, but should confirm before they sign up to make kebabs."* 🔵 **So the requirement is the opposite of consolidation: surface them as countable, checkable rows. Their packs already support it — `1 box (100 count)`, `1 package (8-12 count)` — which is why the gram conversion was never needed.**
- ⚠️ **NO NEW SECTION IS REQUIRED. PRD §12.4's `Household` section already exists for "cleaners, paper goods, pet supplies, etc." and is where these belong.** 🔴 **They are NOT there today — see BUG-232, which this review turned from a one-row cosmetic into a measured class.**

### D-WS9-227 — 🔵 A shopper can change how MUCH, never WHAT — the grocery row exposes quantity and a cosmetic label, and nothing else

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[GROCERY]` `[UX]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 7, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — measured and named; the product decision is Hans's and is NOT yet made** · **Cross-ref:** **BUG-226** (the case that surfaced it) · **BUG-124** · D-WS9-222 · D-WS9-226 · BUG-225.
- **Hans, verbatim (device pass, September 7):** *"grocery list items are not editable easily (it either checks it as measured or edits the quantity needed and units). it doesn't allow a user to change what's being purchased."*
- ✅ **HIS READING IS CORRECT, AND THE CONSTRAINT IS IN THE SCHEMA AND THE ROUTE CONTRACT, NOT JUST THE UI.** Measured from code, September 7: the item PATCH accepts **eight** fields — `isChecked`, `quantity`, `unit`, `stapleOptedIn`, `storeSection`, `displayName`, `userResolvedTo`, `acknowledgeAmbiguity` — **the client sends five of them**, and every mutation funnels through `AppContext` (no screen calls the API layer directly).
- **What a shopper CAN do:** tick and untick · edit quantity and unit · opt a staple in for the week · resolve or acknowledge an ambiguity · add an extra row · remove a row · undo the removal · mark the shop complete.
- 🔴 **WHAT NOBODY CAN DO, AND THE THREE REASONS ARE DIFFERENT:** ① **the ingredient identity** — `ingredientId` is settable on ADD and absent from the update schema, so once a row exists the ingredient it points at is fixed and **no route repoints it**; ② **the pack** — `purchaseUnit` / `purchaseQuantity` / `purchaseDisplay` are in **no input schema anywhere**, and the schema comment states the rule: **the pack is DERIVED and reconcile regenerates it, the need is AUTHORED** — so it is deliberately non-user-authored and an edit would be overwritten; ③ **swapping one product for another** — the nearest affordance is the Clarify sheet, and it writes `userResolvedTo`, **a display string**. ⚠️ **You can relabel what the row SAYS. You cannot re-point what it IS** — `ingredientId`, the pack and the conversion basis all stay put.
- ⚠️ **TWO FIELDS THE SERVER ACCEPTS AND NO CLIENT EVER SENDS: `displayName` (read path only, zero write sites) and `storeSection` (sent on ADD, never on UPDATE — so a generated row cannot be moved between aisles).** **That is latent surface, not a feature: either wire it deliberately or drop it from the schema.**
- 🔴 **THE QUESTION FOR HANS, AND IT IS A PRODUCT CALL, NOT A BUG:** when the list says something a shopper knows is wrong — `1 quart` of milk, a pack that is not what they buy — **what should they be able to do about it in the moment?** The options are genuinely different in cost and in blast radius: **(a)** nothing, and the fix is always the catalog (today's behaviour; requires D-WS9-226's review loop to be trustworthy); **(b)** a per-list override that changes this row only and never touches the catalog; **(c)** a correction that writes back to the catalog for that user; **(d)** a correction that proposes a catalog change for review — the same shape as `ai_gapfill`, but sourced from a human who is standing in the aisle.
- ⚠️ **DO NOT BUILD ANY OF THEM YET.** (c) and (d) both re-open BUG-124's exact hazard — a value derived from one person's situation persisted as a product fact — and (b) collides with the reconcile pass that regenerates the pack. **The ruling must come before the build, and D-WS9-226's intake work should land first so the catalog side is trustworthy.**

### D-WS9-228 — 🔵 A recurring staple's default names the GRADE the recipes assume — ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 7, 2026)**

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[GROCERY]` `[CATALOG]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 7, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Status:** ✅ **RULED — the axis is settled; the per-food application is NOT** · **Cross-ref:** **BUG-225** (the eggs instance) · **BUG-226** (the milk instance, still open) · D-WS9-226 · D-WS9-221 · D-WS9-223.
- **Hans, verbatim:** *"I always buy (at least almost always) and mostly only see Grade A Large eggs and some Grade A Extra Large eggs. Maybe I'm incorrect, but I feel like Large Eggs is what people buy... I think that means the recurring eggs should default to 1 dozen large eggs. am I thinking that through correctly? is there sales data to support the idea that large eggs is what everyone gets?"*
- ✅ **THE RULING: when a food is sold in GRADED SIZES and the recipe corpus assumes one grade, the recurring staple's default names THAT GRADE, in the pack size it is normally sold in.** Eggs: **`1 dozen Large`.**
- 🔴 **THE JUSTIFICATION IS RECIPE CONVENTION, NOT MARKET SHARE — AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS.** Chat-Claude searched for the sales-share statistic Hans asked for and **did not find one**: USDA's shell-egg reports carry prices and movement by size band but publish no retail share, and the consumer sources are explainer articles. ⚠️ **NO SHARE FIGURE IS RECORDED ANYWHERE IN CANON AND NONE MAY BE CITED LATER AS IF IT WERE MEASURED.** ✅ **The ruling does not need one.** The American recipe convention is that an unqualified *"2 eggs"* means **2 large eggs** — so Large is the size the app's own recipe math already assumes, and a shopper who buys Large is never wrong against a Kiwi recipe. **That argument is stronger than a share figure would have been, because it ties the default to something the product controls rather than to consumer behaviour it does not.**
- ⚠️ **THE TEST FOR APPLYING IT ELSEWHERE — and it is deliberately narrow.** A food qualifies only if **(i)** it is sold in named grades or sizes AND **(ii)** the recipe corpus has a default grade it assumes silently. **Eggs pass. Most foods do NOT** — an onion is not graded, and *"1 lb of chicken"* names a weight, not a grade. ⚠️ **Do not turn this into a licence to pick a "standard" size for every ungraded food; that is D-WS9-221's job (smallest normal size that retires the demand) and it answers a different question.**
- 🔴 **IT IS AN ALIAS-PRECEDENCE CHANGE, NOT A FOLD, AND THE `distinct` EDGE STANDS.** Measured September 7: `egg` (`179e8716`) and `Large eggs` (`ff985025`) are separate catalog rows joined by a deliberate high-confidence **`distinct`** edge, and the recurring preference string `egg` lands on the generic row because **a canonical name always beats an alias**. ⚠️ **This ruling changes only WHICH ROW THE RECURRING STRING RESOLVES TO. It does NOT authorise deleting the `distinct` edge, folding the two rows, or a subsumes pass on graded foods** — D-WS9-223's discriminator (*does the distinction change the dish?*) is untouched by it.
- ⚠️ **AND IT DOES NOT CLOSE BUG-225.** Even with the recurring row resolved to Large, two adjacent lines can still both open *"1 dozen"* for unrelated reasons. **The unrelatable-pack render is still the defect of record.**
- ⚠️ **UNBUILT. NOT COMMISSIONED.** The ruling is recorded so the CSV pass and the intake work (D-WS9-226) can apply it to the recurring group; **no block has been written for it, and the alias-precedence code has not been read.** Whoever commissions it reads `ingredientResolve`'s precedence first and reports before editing.

### D-WS9-229 — 🔵 The grocery-generate limiter's BUDGET is reasoned, not priced — and it will hit Hans's own device passes before it ever hits an attacker — ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 7, 2026)**

- **Tags:** `[WS9A]` `[COST]` `[UX]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 7, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9A · **Status:** ✅ **RULED September 7 — all three questions answered; the BUDGET ships as committed, the ESCAPE HATCH and the MESSAGE are UNBUILT** · **Cross-ref:** **BUG-222** (the limiter) · BUG-223 · D-WS9-181 · D-WS9-226.
- **What shipped, at CC's own declaration that it is a reasoned number and not a priced one:** `POST /api/plans/:id/generate-grocery-list` gets **capacity 4, refill 4 per 300 s, keyed on `userId`.** Placed against the existing ladder: `mutationLimiter` 60/min (cheap writes) · assist/recalc/prepWeek 12/min (mid-tier AI) · `wizardLimiter` 8/min (the tightest existing AI tier). **Half the wizard's burst, refilling 5× slower, because canon calls this the most expensive request the server serves.**
- 🔴 **CC COULD NOT PRICE A SINGLE GENERATE AND SAID SO.** Pricing needs a live AI call or an `LLMCallLog` read; **both were barred in the block.** ⚠️ **So the number is calibrated by RELATIVE POSITION IN A LADDER, not by dollars — and the ladder itself has never been priced either.** **Do not describe this budget as cost-based.**
- 🔴 **THE NEAR-TERM CONSEQUENCE IS NOT AN ATTACKER, IT IS HANS. A device pass that regenerates repeatedly gets 429 after four, then one per 75 seconds** — and a 429 on his screen mid-test reads as a defect, not as a limiter working. ⚠️ **This is the §27 pattern exactly: if the product owner misreads it, a beta user will.** **Nobody should run a grocery device pass without knowing this.**
- **The decision, and it is three questions, not one:**
  1. **Is 4 burst / 4-per-5-min the right BETA budget** for a friends-and-family group, or is it tuned for a public URL that does not exist yet?
  2. **Should there be a dev/test escape** — an env-gated non-firing bucket, the same DI seam the suites already use — so device passes and local work are not throttled? ⚠️ **An escape hatch that can be set in production is worse than no limiter; if this is built, it must be impossible to enable on a deployed instance.**
  3. **What is the USER-FACING behaviour at the limit?** Today it is a bare 429 from a route the app calls during a generating overlay. **A limiter with no message is a hang.**
- ⚠️ **THE REAL FIX IS THE ONE THIS ONE STANDS IN FOR, AND BUG-222 SAYS SO: there is no per-user AI SPEND CEILING anywhere in the server**, and `GET /api/wizard/limits` reports a cap it does not enforce. **A rate limiter bounds requests per minute; it does not bound money.** ✅ **Ship the limiter now — it is strictly better than nothing — but do not let it close the spend question.**
- ✅ **ONE PART NEEDS NO RULING AND SHOULD NOT BE REOPENED: the key is `userId`, not `ip`, deliberately.** Under BUG-223 an IP key collapses behind Cloud Run's front end, **which on this route would let one user's regenerate exhaust everyone's.** A per-user key is immune whatever `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS` becomes.
- ✅ **HANS'S RULING, September 7, 2026 — ALL THREE, YES.**
  1. ✅ **The budget stands: 4 burst, 4 per 300 s, per user, for beta.** No change to `fa1859c`.
  2. ✅ **BUILD THE DEV ESCAPE HATCH**, env-gated, using the DI seam the suites already use. 🔴 **AND THE CONSTRAINT IS PART OF THE RULING, NOT A CAVEAT: it must be IMPOSSIBLE to enable on a deployed instance.** An escape hatch a production env var can flip is worse than no limiter at all.
  3. ✅ **AND THE MESSAGE IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING, BECAUSE HANS REFRAMED THE WHOLE THING.**
- 🔴 **THE DURABLE INSIGHT: A RATE-LIMIT MESSAGE SHOULD DIAGNOSE THE PRODUCT, NOT SCOLD THE USER.** Hans's copy, verbatim: *"Kiwi seems to be missing the mark, please refine your preferences or use the 'Tell Kiwi' option with more details about what you'd like to eat."* And his statement of intent, verbatim: *"Basically 'hey, if you're messing around and using tokens for fun, please stop. and if this really isn't getting you what you want, try something else'."*
- ✅ **WHY THAT IS BETTER THAN A LIMIT NOTICE, AND THE REASONING GENERALISES TO EVERY LIMIT IN THE APP: someone regenerating five times in ten minutes is telling you the plan is wrong, not that they love clicking.** A message that says *"slow down"* answers the server's problem; **a message that says *"this isn't working for you — here is the path that will"* answers the USER'S problem and reduces the load as a side effect.** ⚠️ **The `Tell Kiwi` pointer is the load-bearing half — it names the cheaper, better route instead of leaving a dead end.**
- 🔴 **CHAT-CLAUDE SAID "WITHOUT THE MESSAGE THE LIMITER IS A SILENT HANG." THAT IS REFUTED BY THE DEVICE, September 7, 2026.** Hans drained the bucket (~5 presses) and the app showed **"something went wrong, please try again in a moment."** ⚠️ **The client has a generic error path and it caught the 429.** ✅ **So item 3 is a COPY improvement on a working error state, not a rescue from a spinner — a smaller and less urgent job than this entry claimed.** ⚠️ **§27's rule again: a UI claim asserted from a route contract, without opening the client's error path.**
- 🔵 **AND HANS'S SECOND PASS AT THE COPY, WRITTEN AFTER SEEING IT FIRE, DIFFERS FROM HIS FIRST — WHICH IS INFORMATION, NOT INDECISION.** Verbatim: *"Kiwi is having trouble with your grocery list and needs a rest. Please wait a few minutes and try again."* **The first version diagnoses the USER'S SITUATION (the plan is missing the mark — try Tell Kiwi); the second states the SYSTEM'S STATE and the recovery (wait, then retry).**
- ✅ **THEY ARE NOT COMPETING DRAFTS — THEY ANSWER THE TWO DIFFERENT QUESTIONS A PERSON HAS AT THAT MOMENT, IN ORDER: "is it broken and what do I do now?" then "why does it keep happening?"** ⚠️ **A message that only diagnoses gives no recovery; a message that only says wait leaves them regenerating again in five minutes.** 🔵 **WORKING SHAPE, PENDING HANS'S CONFIRM: the recovery first, the diagnosis second** — *"Kiwi needs a short rest — please try again in a few minutes. If the plans aren't hitting the mark, refining your preferences or using Tell Kiwi will get you there faster than regenerating."*
- ⚠️ **Do not ship the limiter to a beta user without item 3** — the current copy is truthful but says nothing about the cause or the cure.
- ⚠️ **UNBUILT: items 2 and 3 are ruled and NOT commissioned.** ✅ **Item 1 is already in `fa1859c`.** **The limiter itself is live in the tree, so item 3 is now the highest-priority piece of this entry — a device pass can produce the silent-hang state today.**
- ⚠️ **STILL OPEN AND NOT ANSWERED BY THIS RULING: the per-user AI SPEND CEILING (BUG-222's product half).** A rate limiter bounds requests per minute; **it does not bound money.**

### D-WS9-230 — 🔵 NO BACKFILLS. Fixes are FORWARD-ONLY, and Hans's existing data is disposable — ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 7, 2026)**

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[WS9A]` `[SCOPE]` `[PROCESS]` · **Date:** September 7, 2026 · **Owner:** every block from here · **Status:** ✅ **RULED — binding on commissioning** · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-186** (which first split forward fixes from historical backfills) · D-WS9-203 · D-WS9-184 · D-WS7-219 · BUG-231 · BUG-232 · BUG-096.
- **Hans, verbatim:** *"on any fixes, there is NO NEED to backfill or fix data. I can test on new plans for everything. and it's all my data and no one else is in there, so bad data is fine for me to ignore."*
- ✅ **THE RULING: a fix ships when NEW data comes out right. Existing plans, lists, meals and imports are NOT repaired, NOT migrated and NOT audited for residue.** **Verification is "generate a fresh plan and look", never "re-run the corpus."**
- 🔴 **THIS IS A LARGE, PERMANENT SCOPE REDUCTION AND IT SHOULD BE APPLIED AGGRESSIVELY.** This project has repeatedly built a fix and then built a second thing to repair what the bug already wrote — review sheets, dry-run/apply merge scripts, residue-rate gates, 53-list re-measurements. ⚠️ **A large share of that was serving a corpus of ONE developer's throwaway test plans.** ✅ **Pre-launch, with no other users, the corpus has no value worth an engineering hour.**
- 🔴 **THE CARVE-OUT, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL — DO NOT READ THIS RULING AS "NEVER WRITE DATA AGAIN."** Two different things are called "data" here:
  - **USER-SCOPED data — plans, grocery lists, meals, imported recipes. THIS is what the ruling releases.** It belongs to Hans, no one else has any, and he throws it away by making a new plan.
  - 🔴 **THE SHARED INGREDIENT CATALOG (1,569 rows), its relations, aliases and packs, is NOT user-scoped and is NOT covered.** **Every future user inherits it on day one.** ⚠️ **D-WS9-226's CSV load, the pack-size work and the relationship program are PRODUCT DATA and remain in scope exactly as ruled.** **A chat that cancels the CSV load citing this entry has misread it.**
- ⚠️ **THE TEST, when it is unclear which side something falls on: WOULD A NEW USER SIGNING UP TOMORROW INHERIT THIS ROW?** If yes it is catalog and it gets fixed. If no it is Hans's scratch and it gets ignored.
- ✅ **IMMEDIATE CONSEQUENCES, already applied:** **BUG-231** (`onion` / `diced onion`) needs the INTAKE fix only — **the four onion rows on Hans's current lists are not to be cleaned up.** **BUG-232** (`Celery Seed` in Produce) is a catalog-side classification and **stays in scope, because a new user inherits it.**
- ⚠️ **IT ALSO CHANGES WHAT A DEVICE SCRIPT ASKS FOR: "generate a NEW plan and check" replaces "open your existing list and confirm the old rows changed."** Several past scripts asked the second question and got confusing answers for exactly this reason.
- 🔵 **AND ONE THING IT DOES NOT LICENSE: it is not permission to ship a fix unverified.** **Forward-only means the ACCEPTANCE TEST runs on new data, not that there is no acceptance test.**

**✅ AMENDMENT — September 14, 2026: THE RULING EXTENDS FROM DATA TO THE SCHEDULE. A BROKEN APP FOR A FEW DAYS IS AN ACCEPTABLE COST OF A FASTER ROUTE.**

- **Hans, verbatim:** *"this is a meal planning app, so I'm not like actively using it. I just test there and have done some weekly meal plans and grocery lists to kick the tires… chats often forget that breaking something temporarily is ok for now because this is development mode until we actually go on an app store… if that impacts our build approach to be more efficient in the delivery of what's on the roadmap it's ok for the app to be unusable for a couple days at a time if necessary."*
- 🔴 **WHAT IS NEW: the original ruling released HIS DATA. This releases THE SEQUENCE.** The entry above already said his plans are disposable; chats kept honouring a second, unwritten constraint — *keep the app working at every commit* — and paid for it in lane splits, feature flags and extra round trips. **That constraint is lifted until the App Store submission.**
- ✅ **WHAT IT LICENSES, named so a chat can act on it without re-asking:** a rewrite may REPLACE a flow rather than run beside it (no dual-path scaffolding, no feature flag, no compatibility shim built only to keep the old path alive) · a lane may land in a knowingly broken intermediate state and be fixed by the next lane · a sequence may be split by WHAT IS EFFICIENT TO BUILD rather than by what keeps the app usable — **the D-WS9-239 1a/1b/1c split was partly the second, and a comparable split in future should be justified by build cost or measurement, not by user-visible inertness** · device testing belongs at the END of a sequence, not between every step · **a schema change may drop or reshape a column carrying only user-scoped rows without a migration path for them.**
- 🔴 **WHAT IT DOES NOT TOUCH, AND THE LINE IS NOT "USER-VISIBLE" — IT IS REVERSIBLE vs EXPENSIVE-TO-UNDO.** There are no users on either surface, so "don't break the app" was never the real boundary. What still binds: **the SHARED INGREDIENT CATALOG and the 1,872-meal catalog** (the carve-out above — every future user inherits those rows, and a wrong write costs a repair pass, which is the thing this entry exists to prevent) · **anything that cannot be taken back**: the Play Store application id, a published store build, a live sending domain, a deleted column whose content is catalog · **the audit gate (§3) and acceptance (the clause directly above)** — speed comes from sequencing, never from skipping the check that catches the wrong build.
- ⚠️ **SO A MEASUREMENT GATE IS NOT THE THING BEING RELAXED.** D-WS9-239's fresh-20 gate protects the **catalog**, not Hans's comfort: 1c writes tags onto shared meals. **Read a gate's purpose before citing this amendment at it.**
- 🔴 **REFINED BY HANS THE SAME DAY, AND IT IS THE HALF A CHAT WILL GET WRONG IF IT READS ONLY THE LICENCE ABOVE.** Verbatim: *"the big thing, and where I should be inserted into a defined run, is if we're building something that benefits from a build checkpoint or validation partway through to reduce variables if it's broken when I get to testing."* ✅ **THE DISTINCTION, STATED ONCE: a checkpoint that exists to keep the APP USABLE is dropped. A checkpoint that exists to ISOLATE A VARIABLE before Hans tests is KEPT — and named explicitly in the sequence, with what it proves.** ⚠️ **Going faster is not the same as handing him a finished pile he has to bisect.** A stop before an irreversible or expensive step (a catalog write, a spend, a store submission) is the same class and stays for the same reason.
- ✅ **AND ON THE CATALOG, HANS, VERBATIM: *"it's less the $17, and more making sure we're doing the right thing."*** **The carve-out above is not a budget rule and must not be argued down with a cost figure.**
- ✅ **CC MAY NOW RUN `prisma:seed` ITSELF (Hans, September 14).** The reseed was the main thing stopping a lane mid-flight for a round trip through his terminal — 1b cost three. ⚠️ **Disclosed when he ruled it and still true: the seed also upserts the 12 recipe rows and the ingredient rows, so it touches CATALOG — idempotent, deterministic from a file in the repo, and it has run many times, but it is a catalog write and it is the one place this permission brushes the carve-out.** **Migrations are unchanged — `prisma migrate deploy` stays DENIED to CC and Hans runs them (§2).**
- ✅ **AND IT RETIRES A CLASS OF PARAGRAPH FROM CHAT MESSAGES AND CANON ALIKE:** *"note that plans generated between X and Y may read wrong"*. **Hans does not need to be warned about his own scratch data.** State the live-DB fact once if a chat must not misread it, never as a caution to him.

### D-WS9-231 — 🔵 `kiwi://` custom-scheme links do not survive email, and every link the app mints is one — ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 7, 2026): https fallback page now, universal links later — and they are the SAME URL**

- **Tags:** `[WS9A]` `[AUTH]` `[MOBILE]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 7, 2026 · **Owner:** the auth+email block · **Status:** ✅ **RULED September 7 — option 2 (https + web fallback), with option 1 as the later upgrade on the same URLs** · **Cross-ref:** **BUG-235** (the client that would consume it) · **BUG-224** · BUG-233 · D-WS7-022.
- **CC, auth+email Phase 0, flagged unprompted:** both mail-bearing flows mint **`kiwi://…`** URLs — `kiwi://reset-password?token=…` and `kiwi://verify-email?token=…` — **and neither has ever been through a real mail client, because neither has ever been sent.**
- 🔴 **A CUSTOM SCHEME IS THE ONE LINK SHAPE EMAIL IS WORST AT.** Many clients decline to linkify a non-`http(s)` scheme, some strip it, and **if the app is not installed the link is simply inert — no store page, no web fallback, nothing.** ⚠️ **The user experience of a failure here is a link that visibly does nothing, on the one email whose entire job is to rescue a locked-out account.**
- ⚠️ **THE EXISTING EVIDENCE PROVES THE WRONG THING AND MUST NOT BE MISREAD: `kiwi://verify-email` works — from a device, where something already resolved the scheme.** **That says the ROUTER is wired. It says nothing about whether Gmail will render the link.**
- **The decision, and there are three real options:**
  1. **`https://` universal / app links** — the app opens if installed, the web page loads if not. 🔴 **Costs a live domain and a hosted `apple-app-site-association` (plus the Android asset-links file), so it is gated on the same DNS session as everything else — and it is the only option that degrades gracefully.**
  2. **`https://` link to a plain web fallback page that then hands off to the app** — cheaper, one page, works everywhere, one extra hop for the user.
  3. **Keep `kiwi://`** — free, and accepts that some recipients get a dead link. ⚠️ **Defensible for a friends-and-family beta where Hans can talk someone through it; indefensible at launch.**
- 🔴 **IT GATES BUG-235's BUILD RATHER THAN FOLLOWING IT.** The deep-link target screen, the token hand-off and the fallback behaviour all differ by option. **Building the client first and choosing after means building it twice.**
- ⚠️ **AND IT COMPOSES WITH THE `PUBLIC_APP_URL` GAP: options 1 and 2 both need an https host the server can build links from, and no such variable exists** (see BUG-228's env contract).
- ✅ **HANS RULED OPTION 2, September 7, 2026** — *"fallback page is fine"* — and asked the right follow-up: **why not build universal links now?**
- 🔴 **THE ANSWER IS THAT UNIVERSAL LINKS ARE NOT A DIFFERENT LINK, THEY ARE THE SAME URL PLUS THREE THINGS THAT DO NOT EXIST YET.** The email carries `https://<host>/reset-password?token=…` in BOTH options. **The upgrade is hosting two association files and shipping a build that claims the domain — the email, the route, the token and the server change NOT AT ALL.** ✅ **So option 2 is not a detour that gets thrown away; it is the foundation, and the migration is additive.**
- **The three missing prerequisites, none of which is code:** ⓐ **a live https host serving `/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` and `assetlinks.json`** — Cloud Run is not deployed; ⓑ **an Apple Developer account and the Associated Domains entitlement** — Hans's Apple Small Business Program setup is still an open personal action, **and this does NOT work in Expo Go; it needs a development build**; ⓒ **an Android build signed with the certificate fingerprint named in `assetlinks.json`.** ⚠️ **Building universal links today means blocking the beta on the Apple account and the dev build — the exact standing hazard canon already flags around Expo Go.**
- 🔴 **AND THE FALLBACK PAGE IS MORE THAN A FALLBACK FOR THIS PARTICULAR FLOW, WHICH RAISES ITS VALUE AND ITS SCOPE.** ⚠️ **Password reset is the flow MOST LIKELY to be opened on a laptop** — someone locked out of the app checks email on a desktop. **A page that only says "open the Kiwi app" strands exactly the person the feature exists for.** ✅ **The reset must be COMPLETABLE IN THE BROWSER: enter the new password, POST to the API, done.**
- 🔴 **CONSEQUENCE FOR BUG-235's ESTIMATE, AND IT IS NEW SURFACE: Kiwi has NO deployed web surface today.** A browser-completable reset is a small static page plus a call to `/auth/password-reset/confirm` — **modest, but it is not a React Native screen and it is not in anyone's current scope.** ⚠️ **It also needs somewhere to live (the same host as the association files), so it lands with the deploy work rather than the mobile work.**
- 🔵 **THE ORDER THAT FALLS OUT: the WEB page is the PRIMARY reset surface and the app deep-link is the ENHANCEMENT — the reverse of how the flow was originally imagined.** ⚠️ **Do not build the React Native reset-confirm screen first.**
- ⚠️ **`PUBLIC_APP_URL` is now load-bearing rather than tidy** — the server must build these links from a real https host, and no such variable exists (BUG-228).
- ✅ **SERVER SIDE BUILT September 8, 2026 — `c38a596` (LOCAL, NOT PUSHED, NOT DEVICE-TESTED).** Both flows now mint `https://<PUBLIC_APP_URL>/reset-password?token=…` and `/verify-email?token=…` — the shape options 1 and 2 share — **and the whole decision is isolated in one function, `buildAppLink`, so reverting to option 3 would be a one-function edit; nothing else in the commit depends on the ruling.** ⚠️ **CC built it while REFUSING the prompt's "Hans ruled D-WS9-231" premise — correctly, because the mirror copy it could see (banner 01:32Z) still read OPEN: the ruling reached canon after that sync, and the manifest claimed a sync that had not landed on disk. The mirror is re-synced September 8; the code needed no change.** `PUBLIC_APP_URL` exists now (BUG-228 closed) and `.env` must carry it whenever the key is set.
- 🔴 **SCOPE CORRECTION — THE PAGE SERVES BOTH ROUTES, NOT JUST RESET.** The reasoning above is about reset only. **The email-change verification link is https now too, so the email-change client that BUG-235 calls complete is reachable from its email ONLY through this page's hand-off.** For `/verify-email` a hand-off to `kiwi://verify-email?token=…` (or an in-browser POST to the verify route) is enough; `/reset-password` must be completable in the browser, as ruled. ⚠️ **DEPLOY GATE: no deployed instance carries `RESEND_API_KEY` until this page exists — a link that 404s is worse than no email. Harmless on the laptop, where the only recipients are Hans's own test accounts.**

### D-WS9-232 — 🔵 `stoveType` and the dead-preference-field audit: remove what nothing reads — and check the schema DEFAULT before removing anything

- **Tags:** `[PRODUCT]` `[ONBOARDING]` `[SCHEMA]` `[AUDIT]` · **Date:** September 8, 2026 · **Owner:** the WS9 redesign / onboarding pass · **Status:** 🔵 **OPEN — Hans's intent is stated; the audit has not been run** · **Cross-ref:** PRD §3.5 · **D-WS7-190** (`wantsLeftovers` — the precedent that makes this dangerous) · D-WS9-207.
- **Hans, September 8, 2026:** user preferences carry a **stove type** (electric / gas / induction); he does not believe it does much of anything and wants it out of the layout **to reduce onboarding friction** — *"it's worth confirming there are no extra fields that don't really do anything when we do that."* **The audit is the larger half of the ask.**
- **What canon establishes and what it does not.** PRD §3.5 specs `stoveType` as an enum (gas / induction / electric / unknown) inside the OPTIONAL, expandable Cooking-equipment section of onboarding step 3 — alongside `equipment[]`, `kidCount`, `kidAgeRanges[]`, `pickyEaterCount`, `pickyAvoidances[]`, `spiceTolerance`, `healthGoals[]`, `budgetLevel`, all carried under one `[SCHEMA]` note. ⚠️ **That proves it was SPECCED, not that anything READS it (§8.1: only code establishes existence, and the PRD's characteristic failure is OVER-REPORTING what exists).**
- **The audit is one read-only sweep with TWO columns per field, and the second is the one that matters: is it WRITTEN** (does the screen set it, does `PUT /me/preferences` accept it) **and is it READ** (does any prompt body, filter, sort, or display consume it). **Written-and-never-read is the removal candidate. Read-only-by-a-prompt-body is NOT dead, and removing it silently changes generation.**
- 🔴 **REMOVING THE CONTROL IS NOT SUFFICIENT, AND THIS PROJECT HAS ALREADY PAID FOR THAT LESSON ONCE.** `wantsLeftovers` (D-WS7-190) was pulled from onboarding, the Preferences screen and both wizard screens — **but its schema default was `@default(true)`, so a UI-less field would have silently turned leftover-inflation ON for every new user**, the exact opposite of pulling the feature. It needed its own migration to flip the default. ✅ **THE RULE THIS ENTRY CARRIES: every removal in this sweep checks the SCHEMA DEFAULT and every consumer, not just the screen.**
- ⚠️ **AND THE CONSUMER THAT HIDES FROM A SYMBOL GREP IS THE PROMPT BODY.** Some prompt bodies are `{{…Input}}` with the real instructions in compiled TS (§7's footgun), so a field can be load-bearing inside a prompt string while a grep for its name returns nothing useful. **Sweep `aiPrompts.ts` and the compiled prompt surfaces, not only the TypeScript that names the field** — and per §27.3, no negative from a single grep shape.
- **OPEN, for Hans once the audit reports:** whether "nothing reads it" means **drop the column** or **keep the column and drop only the onboarding control.** 🔵 **Keeping a written-but-unread column is the cheaper reversal if equipment data is ever wanted for recipe filtering — which is what the PRD said it was for** (*"so we don't suggest recipes you can't make"*). **Friction is removed either way; only the schema decision differs.**

### D-WS9-233 — 🔵 Macro targets: the build is post-launch, but the REDESIGN decision is now — and "per meal" is not what canon deferred

- **Tags:** `[PRODUCT]` `[ROADMAP]` `[WS9]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 8, 2026 · **Owner:** definition track now; build post-launch · **Status:** ✅ **RULED September 8, 2026 (Hans) — PER-DINNER-SERVING targets, displayed as "daily averages" with an explicit asterisk. The scope fork is closed; LOE can now be sized** · **Cross-ref:** PRD §11.4 / §11.5 / §11.6 / §11.13 · PRD §3.5 (`dailyCalorieTarget`) · **PRD §11.7** (the half that already exists).
- **Hans, September 8, 2026:** users should be able to **set macro targets for their meals**; *"this could come after launch, but I want to understand the LOE and make sure this is incorporated into the redesign effort."*
- **This re-opens an explicit MVP exclusion, and canon is unusually firm about it.** PRD §11.5 locks *"No macro target tracking at MVP… no comparison to a target, no progress indicators, no 'X / Y' framing"*; §11.6 was REMOVED in favour of §11.13's roadmap row; and §3.5's `dailyCalorieTarget` onboarding capture was deferred in the same breath. **Re-opening is Hans's call to make — this entry records that it IS a re-opening, so nobody later reads §11.5 as still binding.**
- ✅ **HALF OF IT ALREADY SHIPS, AND THAT CHANGES THE ESTIMATE.** PRD §11.7 (LOCKED) already has the wizard weighting generation by macro INTENT — high-protein > 25 g/serving, low-carb < 30 g/serving, healthy < 600 cal/serving, **with the thresholds admin-configurable as prompt config.** **So "generate toward a macro shape" exists. What is missing is a user-set NUMBER, its storage, and the X-of-Y display.**
- 🔴 **THE URGENT HALF IS NOT THE BUILD — IT IS THE LAYOUT, AND THAT IS WHY THIS CANNOT SIMPLY WAIT.** Macros render on **six** surfaces (§11.4: Plan Review daily averages · plan result cards · Meal Detail · Dish Detail · Cook Now results · My Meals rows). **Target framing turns `620 cal` into `620 / 700 cal` plus a progress affordance — a materially wider element in rows that are already tight.** ⚠️ **A redesign that sizes those slots to the bare number either forecloses the feature or buys a second pass over all six surfaces.**
- **So the ask splits, and only one half is post-launch:**
  - ⓐ **NOW — design track, no code:** the WS9 restyle **reserves room** for target framing on the macro surfaces and picks the treatment once (inline `X / Y` · a ring · a bar), so the slot exists even while it renders a bare value.
  - ⓑ **POST-LAUNCH — build:** capture (onboarding + Preferences), storage, the comparison display, and whether the wizard generates **against a numeric target** rather than a soft intent.
- 🔴 **LOE IS DELIBERATELY NOT ESTIMATED HERE, AND MUST NOT BE GUESSED — THERE IS A SCOPE FORK UPSTREAM OF IT.** Hans said targets **"for their meals."** ⚠️ **PER-MEAL is NOT what §11.13's roadmap row describes — that row is DAILY calorie/macro targets and daily consumption-vs-goal.** **Per-meal and per-day are different features:** per-day compares against Plan Review's existing daily averages (which are already computed and displayed); per-meal needs a target that means something on a single Meal Detail row, and it interacts badly with the fact that **per-serving macros are constant while servings change** (§11.3). **Rule per-meal vs per-day BEFORE anyone sizes this.** ⚠️ **Second fork, same rule: display-only, or does it steer generation? §11.7 says a soft intent already steers it; a hard number is a different prompt contract and a different failure mode when no plan satisfies it.**

✅ **RULED — HANS, September 8, 2026. BOTH FORKS ANSWERED IN ONE MOVE.**
- **The target is PER DINNER SERVING, and it STEERS GENERATION.** Hans, verbatim: *"users can say '600 calories, 25 grams protein, 3 grams fat, 16 grams carbs' for their target and it will suggest meals that meet (or approximately meet) those goals for 1 serving at dinner."* ⚠️ **"Approximately" is his word and it is load-bearing — this is a weighting, not a filter. A hard constraint that returns no plan is the failure mode to avoid (§11.7's existing soft-preference behaviour is the correct precedent).**
- **The DISPLAY stays "daily averages" — with an explicit asterisk that Kiwi plans DINNERS ONLY.** Hans: *"a person truly using this for macros for each day wouldn't really be able to use Kiwi in the current state… users can add breakfast and lunch meals to get full daily macros, but we're not planning all the meals for them."* ✅ **This is honest and it costs nothing today: a plan containing only dinners has a daily average that IS the dinner value, so the asterisk describes reality rather than papering over it.**
- 🔴 **AND THAT COINCIDENCE IS THE TRAP TO WRITE DOWN NOW, BECAUSE IT EXPIRES.** Today *daily average* and *per-dinner value* are the same number. **The moment breakfast and lunch land, "daily average" silently changes meaning and any comparison built against it would be measuring a full day against a dinner-sized target.** ✅ **THE FIX IS CHEAP IF DONE AT BUILD TIME: store the target WITH ITS SCOPE (`per_dinner_serving`), never as a bare number.** A future daily target is then a second scope, not a reinterpretation of the first.
- **Breakfast and lunch are POST-GO-LIVE and are a SEPARATE PRODUCT DECISION, not just later scope.** Hans: *"Breakfast and Lunch menus are after go-live, we have the defaults available now… I would say that's a separate subscription and strategy."* ⚠️ **Record it as a business-model marker, not only a roadmap row — full-day planning is being positioned as a different tier, which changes what "macro targets" is allowed to promise at launch.**
- 🔵 **THE TIMING DRIVER IS NEW AND IT PULLS AGAINST "POST-LAUNCH":** Hans wants to catch the **holiday / New Year meal-prep search wave** — people searching, trying and adopting meal prep in late December and January. ⚠️ **That is a market-timing argument for landing this AT or NEAR launch rather than after it, and it sits in tension with his own earlier *"this could come after launch."* Not resolved here — it belongs in the roadmap conversation he has already asked for.**
- ✅ **LOE IS NOW SIZEABLE, AND THE MECHANISM MOSTLY EXISTS.** §11.7 already weights generation by macro intent (protein > 25 g, carbs < 30 g, < 600 cal per serving) with **admin-configurable thresholds**. **This feature is the user-set numeric version of that same lever** — capture + storage + a prompt-contract change, plus the asterisked display. **It is not net-new machinery, which is the single most useful thing to know before estimating.**
- ⚠️ **ONE OPEN QUESTION HIS OWN EXAMPLE EXPOSES, AND IT IS A REAL PRODUCT DECISION: the four numbers need not agree.** 25 g protein + 3 g fat + 16 g carbs ≈ **191 kcal**, not the 600 stated. **The example was off-the-cuff and is NOT a spec — do not encode those figures.** **But it demonstrates the question: when a user's macro grams do not reconcile with their calorie number, does Kiwi validate, warn, derive calories from the macros, or weight all four independently and ignore the mismatch?** **Rule it before build; it decides whether the capture screen argues with the user.**

### D-WS9-234 — 🔵 The cooking "Playlist" — a FOURTH concept, and it RENAMES what D-WS7-202 has been calling a favorite

- **Tags:** `[PRODUCT]` `[SCHEMA]` `[WS7-11]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 8, 2026 · **Owner:** **WS7-11 — Favorites, Saves, Ratings** (roadmap row 6a) · **Status:** 🔵 **OPEN — Hans has stated the concept; it is not yet ruled into WS7-11's model** · **Cross-ref:** 🔴 **D-WS7-202 (the entry this AMENDS)** · D-WS7-203 · D-WS7-204 · D-WS7-111 · D-WS7-139 (fork-on-acquire) · PRD §13.10.4 · BUG-018.
- **Hans, September 8, 2026, in his own frame:** meatballs and a lasagna he loves are **favorites**, and he would rate them **5 stars** — *"other users may not favorite those meals and some people could think the meals are less than 5 stars and that's fine."* A chicken piccata is **a favorite, probably a 4-star meal, and a recurring meal they cook** — *"it's on our 'playlist' of meals we cook regularly because we know them, they taste good, meet our dietary needs/goals, and everyone eats them."* **He wants Favorites, Ratings, then "add to my cooking playlist" as an attribute tag — and the wizard to incorporate it, "or even shuffle ONLY the user's playlist meals when it generates plans and suggestions."**
- 🔴 **THIS IS A RENAME AS MUCH AS AN ADDITION, AND A BLOCK BUILT FROM D-WS7-202 AS WRITTEN WOULD GET IT WRONG.** That entry defines **three** concepts — **Saved** (the heart; acquisition, not a rating) · **Rated** (stars; retrospective quality) · **Favorite** (*"this is a staple; put it in front of me when I'm planning"* — forward-looking intent). **Its verbatim Hans quote from July is the SAME chicken-piccata argument:** *"this is a 4 star meal, but it's easy and my kids love it, save it as a favorite if I want to add to a plan because it's a staple meal."* ⚠️ **JULY'S "FAVORITE" IS SEPTEMBER'S "PLAYLIST."** Hans has now split that one concept in two and moved the name: **Favorite = plain affection ("I love this")** · **Playlist = the staple / planning signal.** **Four concepts, not three — and the word "favorite" now means the lighter one.**
- ✅ **AND IT ANSWERS D-WS7-202's OWN BLOCKING QUESTION, WHICH IS WHY THIS ENTRY UNBLOCKS RATHER THAN COMPLICATES.** That entry forbids commissioning WS7-11 until *"what do favorites actually DO?"* is ruled, because *"a favorite toggle that visibly does nothing is worse than no toggle."* 🔵 **The answer falls out of Hans's model: the PLAYLIST is the one that does something — it feeds the wizard. The FAVORITE can then be the light one (a My Meals filter/sort), because it is no longer carrying the planning job it was never a good fit for.**
- 🔵 **THE WIZARD ASK IS THE NEW SCOPE, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THE "BIAS" D-WS7-202 CONTEMPLATED.** That entry's candidate was *"wizard bias — weight generation toward favorites, a prompt-contract change."* **Hans is asking for that OR a stricter mode: shuffle from the playlist ONLY.** ⚠️ **These are different builds. A weight is a prompt-contract change. "Only these meals" is closer to a constrained selection over the user's own library than to a generation prompt** — and it has a failure the bias does not: **a playlist of three meals cannot fill a week.** **Rule which one, and rule what happens when the playlist is too small (top up from the catalog? refuse? shorten the plan?), before commissioning.**
- ⚠️ **KEEP DECLARED SEPARATE FROM OBSERVED — the trap this entry exists to flag.** *"Meals we cook regularly"* is exactly what `timesCooked` / `lastUsedAt` would measure **if anything ever wrote to them** — they are dead columns, DB-probed **0/337** (D-WS7-111, adopted by D-WS7-204). 🔴 **The playlist is a user's DECLARED intent, not a derived frequency. Do not auto-populate it from cook counts, and do not let the cook-tracking work absorb it** — a meal you cook weekly out of obligation is not on the playlist, and a seasonal favourite is.
- ⚠️ **D-WS7-202's HAZARDS CARRY TO THE PLAYLIST FLAG UNCHANGED:** **fork-on-calibrate** — never write a personal playlist flag to a `userId: null` catalog row; **reuse D-WS7-139's fork-on-acquire, do not reinvent it** · the **migration WS7-11 already needs** (rating + favorite + cook-tracking, now + the playlist attribute — still likely one) · and the PRD §13.10.2 `[SCHEMA]` note that was **already redlined once for forgetting the stars** — ⚠️ **it now also omits the playlist. Redline it in the same pass, or it will be wrong a second time in the same way.**
- **Sequencing unchanged:** WS7-11 sits **AFTER** the WS9 restyle (net-new UI, built once in the new design system). ✅ **This entry is DEFINITION-track work and can run now, alongside WS9A execution — it produces rulings, not code.**
- ✅ **HANS, September 10, 2026 — THE PLAYLIST IN HIS WORDS, AND IT IS THE PRODUCT'S STANCE ON REPEAT COOKING:** *"Most importantly, I want to introduce the concept of a meal Playlist. Users can save meals to a playlist (either by importing or selecting a Kiwi Cookbook meal), and marking the meal as a playlist meal. Then, they can create plans from the playlist if they want. or generate a plan and include playlist meals. the idea is a lot of home cooks repeat the same meals because they're easy, they work, and they taste good. I don't want Kiwi to get in the way of that."*
  - **It adds three things this entry did not have:** the two ways IN (import a meal, or pick a Kiwi Cookbook meal — the latter is fork-on-acquire, above); **plans built FROM the playlist** (the "shuffle ONLY" mode); and **generation that INCLUDES playlist meals** (the bias mode). **Both modes are wanted — the either/or above is answered "both"; what remains open is the too-small-playlist behaviour.**
  - 🔴 **"Don't get in the way" has two concrete consequences for machinery that already exists — chat-Claude's reading of this quote plus D-WS9-039, to confirm when the playlist is spec'd:** (1) **the fatigue nudge (D-WS9-073) must not push against a playlist meal** — a declared staple is the opposite of "Kiwi really loves suggesting those dang fajitas"; (2) **BUG-249's no-repeat-across-suggested-plans rule exempts playlist meals the USER chose to include**, exactly as it exempts meals named in TellKiwi — **but playlist meals Kiwi picks on its own are fillers, and still vary across the three plans.** ⚠️ **And a user-chosen playlist meal over the cook-time cap is included with its honest time (BUG-245's ruling), not filtered out by the shelf predicate.**
  - ⚠️ **SEQUENCING HAS MOVED BY HANS'S STATEMENT: the playlist is part of the plan-building redesign he places after "the last few P1 bugs and grocery stuff" (D-WS9-237) — not only WS7-11 after the restyle.** The roadmap update is owed; the mockup session precedes the build.
- ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 15, 2026, mockup round 2 — recorded on D-WS9-237 with the rest of the flow): the Playlist is a BOTTOM-NAV TAB where users manage the meals they cook the most, and its per-plan use is a DIAL on the Kitchen Wizard — Playlist meals: None · Some · Mostly · All (default unselected).** **That dial answers the "both modes" question above: All = build the plan from the playlist only; Some / Mostly = the bias mode.** The per-plan include toggle drawn in mockup round 1 is gone — the dial replaced it. ⚠️ **Still open: the too-small-playlist behaviour when the dial says All or Mostly, and the intake sheet (drawn as Hans described it, not ruled).**
- ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 16, 2026, mockup round 5):** **"Plan a week from these" → the Pick screen filtered to the user's playlist meals only — no Kiwi suggestions, the same "Build my week", one active plan.** **"Add meals" → the existing Create Meal screen's six options, plus the bulk intake (now D-WS9-244).** **Copy: "your go-to favorites", not "the meals you actually cook"** — Hans: *"came off like the rest of the kiwi meals aren't great."* **A user with NO playlist meals cannot set the wizard's Playlist dial; they see instead:** *"No playlist? No problem. If you want your own personal go-to favorites included in your plans, click here to get started"* (his words; the link opens the Playlist tab). Still open: the too-small-playlist behaviour when the dial says All or Mostly.
- ✅ **BUILT — Block 2b, September 16, 2026 (`36482cf` the tab and screen · `c812f3d` the two ways in · `f31b149` "Plan a week from these"), AUDITED PASS; device-unproven.** The fifth tab exists with Hans's copy (*"your go-to favorites"*, the rotation line), membership is DECLARED only (no cook counts, no "last cooked" — BUG-275 stays dead as ruled), "Add meals" is today's Create Meal screen with a `toPlaylist=1` thread through all six ways in plus a Meal Detail toggle, and "Plan a week from these" is the Pick screen with `source: "playlist"` — no Kiwi suggestions, no "Get more options", the same "Build my week". **Still open and now sharper: the too-small-playlist behaviour when the dial says All or Mostly** (the server neutralises a dial to `none` at zero meals, but a 3-meal playlist against a 5-day plan on `all` is unruled — the Pick path just shows 3; the generate path is BUG-281's territory), and **BUG-283** (membership is not determinable client-side).
- 🔵 **NOT DESIGNED — Hans, September 10: *"the multi-select list screen hasn't been designed. Same with the playlist."*** **His intake idea, verbatim, for the spec — not ruled:** *"I was thinking of an easy 'tell kiwi' type of import with like 10 rows and a cached call or version of the call to anthropic. so a user like me could add a line 'grilled chicken breasts, near east rice pilaf, roasted broccoli. and grilled chicken thigh tacos with pico and saucy black beans and chicken picatta with arugula salad etc. etc. etc.' and have it create meals for me in my playlist. but there's a lot there, and we can save it for the spec work before build."* ⚠️ **For the spec, not now:** it is TellKiwi's shape turned toward the library — a named-meal parse (the directed path already extracts `explicitMeals`), a Kiwi Cookbook match before any generation (catalog hit = no AI cost, per the arc's ~18× store-bound saving), live generation only for the misses, and every result marked as a playlist meal.

### D-WS9-235 — `estimatedTimeMinutes` is DERIVED from steps at save time, with the scheduler's parallelism, and ACTIVE time is captured beside it — ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 10, 2026)**

- **Raised:** September 9–10, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Tags:** meal-generation · data-integrity · prompt-contract · **Source:** BUG-245's Phase 0 · **Cross-ref:** 🔴 **BUG-245** · **BUG-069** · **D-WS9-122** · D-WS9-128 · D-WS9-230 · BUG-246.
- **Hans, September 9, verbatim, which is the direction:** *"the time to cook should be estimated or calculated at the meal level… we have meals, dishes, ingredients, and STEPS in the catalog, so the data should be there."*
- 🔴 **WHY THIS IS A RULING AND NOT A PROMPT TWEAK.** BUG-245's Phase 0 found the generator being INSTRUCTED to write a false number: `wizard.candidate.expand v5` says *"Author estimatedTimeMinutes from the actual recipe, then keep it under the cap… No exceptions,"* with a worked example licensing the exclusion of unattended time. **Writing 30 for a 58-minute bake is the COMPLIANT answer.** ✅ **A prompt fix closes THAT leak. It does not close the CLASS: any prompt that authors a scalar independently of the steps can drift from them, and BUG-069 → D-WS9-122 → BUG-245 is three instances of exactly that in six weeks.**
- ✅ **THE STRUCTURAL FIX: the meal-level time is COMPUTED from the steps at save time and the generator never writes it.** Then no prompt can lie into it, a time cap must be met by SELECTING meals whose steps fit rather than by writing the cap, and the whole class becomes impossible rather than patched.
- ⚠️ **NOT TRIVIALLY `Σ steps`.** D-WS9-128 measured the step sum overcounting parallel work at a 1.84 median ratio (p90 2.69). **But the data to do better exists: `parallelGroup` is 0 of 25,564 steps, so a dish's own steps are strictly sequential — the honest floor is the LONGEST DISH's serial sum, and the scheduler already knows which cross-dish steps overlap.** **The formula is a design question inside this ruling, not a blocker to it.**
- 🔴 **AND A PRODUCT QUESTION FALLS OUT THAT ONLY HANS CAN ANSWER: WHEN THE CAP CANNOT BE MET, WHAT DOES THE APP DO?** Today it fabricates. **Once the number is honest, a 30-minute cap against a catalog where 40–75% of meals overshoot their own claims will refuse a lot.** Options are not exclusive: tell the user and offer to relax · relax silently to the nearest fit · treat the cap as "aim for" rather than "never exceed." **Unruled.**
- ⚠️ **SEQUENCING WITH BUG-245's PROMPT FIX: complementary, not alternatives.** The prompt fix's SELECTION half — "if the recipe cannot fit the cap, pick a different recipe" — is needed either way. **Its DEFINITION half becomes moot if this is ruled "derive."** Rule this first; it decides the shape of that block.
- 🔵 **BACKFILL:** Hans is open (September 9) and D-WS9-230's carve-out already covers catalog meals. **A derived formula, once ruled, IS the backfill — run it once over the pool, then it runs on every save.**
- ✅ **RULED September 10, 2026 — Hans, verbatim, because each clause changed the block:** *"on the structural piece, yes, but to refine that a bit more: the steps need the parallelism baked in to them. bake one thing for 20 minutes and sautee another for 10 minutes can be done in about 20 minutes. we did a lot of work on this and what counts as parallel or not, so the rules are there. I would also say if this requires a backfill or process to get at the data we should do the cached prompt thing and have it run overnight like when the catalog was created. almost more importantly, is if we're going to all this trouble - and we are - we should get active time and cook time. filtering the wizard on active time and whatnot is NOT MVP and can be deferred to the roadmap."*
  1. 🔴 **THE FORMULA IS THE SCHEDULER'S.** `cookingScheduler.ts` (BUG-018 B2) already decides what overlaps: **unattended = `{preheat, rest, hold}` OR `cook && !isTimingSensitive`.** The derived **TOTAL** is that timeline's end for the meal's dishes; the derived **ACTIVE** is its attended minutes. **Neither `Σ steps` nor a new parallelism model is acceptable — the "formula is a design question" line above is CLOSED by this ruling.** Hans's example is the acceptance test: a 20-minute bake beside a 10-minute sauté derives to about 20, not 30.
  2. ✅ **TWO FIELDS.** `estimatedTimeMinutes` keeps D-WS9-122's meaning (total wall-clock); a new active-time field is captured beside it on every derivation. **Filtering or steering the wizard on active time is NOT MVP → D-WS9-236.** ✅ **Display RULED the same night — Hans: *"capture for sure. displayed would be great if it's not much more work."* Capture is unconditional; display (meal card + meal detail) goes into Phase 1 if the design pass sizes it small, otherwise it queues.**
  3. ✅ **THE DATA PATH IS PRE-AUTHORISED.** If the derivation's inputs are missing or untrustworthy at scale, the remedy is **an overnight cached-prompt tagging pass over the catalog** on the Block 3.8 pattern (`25db784`) — not a forward-only fix. D-WS9-230's carve-out covers it.
- ✅ **THE PRODUCT QUESTION IS RULED TOO — verbatim:** *"if we can't meet their needs, we should be honest about it. the wizard generation falls back to AI, so I would imagine it would figure something out to suggest (right or wrong), so I don't know if we really need an error page or anything."* 🔴 **The cap constrains SELECTION; the number shown is the derived, honest one; there is NO error page, NO refusal state and NO relax-the-cap dialog.** A cap the pool cannot meet surfaces a meal with a true number over the cap, and that is the product telling the truth. ✅ **Hans's own pool-side remedy is scheduled: a catalog supplement targeted at 30-minute meals before launch, during UAT (`kiwi_go_live_todos.md`).**
- 🔴 **COMMISSIONED September 10: a READ-ONLY design pass in the server lane (`kiwi_cc_prompt_LANE_A_time_from_steps.md`) — what the scheduler returns today, the state of the step inputs by `sourceType`, every meal-writing path and what the wizard card shows before steps exist, the prompt's residual shape, and whether the overnight pass is needed. Phase 1 is written from its report; BUG-245 carries the build status.**
- ✅ **THE DESIGN PASS ANSWERED THE SAME NIGHT (server lane; full detail on BUG-245):** the scheduler already returns the total (`scheduleCookingSequence → totalEstimatedMinutes`); ACTIVE needs one export-only change inside the module that owns the predicate; the step inputs are FINE (`isTimingSensitive` true on 16.4%, `estimatedMinutes` on 100%) so **the overnight tagging pass is NOT needed and Hans's pre-authorisation stays banked**; every persistence path has steps at write time and only the candidate CARD does not; `mealMaterialize` defaults a missing number to **30**. 🔴 **And the under-claim is SYSTEMIC, not constraint-driven: 93.8% of 1,555 meals, p50 +20 minutes, capped and uncapped alike — only 19 meals honestly fit a 30-minute cap (163 at 45, 567 at 60).** ⚠️ **"The constraint dominates", relayed into this entry from eight rows, is withdrawn; the ruling stands because it ruled the structure, not the cause.**
- 🔴 **ONE CORRECTION TO THIS ENTRY'S OWN SEQUENCING NOTE: D-WS9-122's definition is moot for the PERSISTED value only. ### D-WS9-236 — Filtering or steering the wizard on ACTIVE (hands-on) time — 🔵 NOT MVP, roadmap

- **Raised:** September 10, 2026 · **Owner:** roadmap (post-MVP) · **Tags:** `[PRODUCT]` `[ROADMAP]` `[WS9]` · **Source:** Hans's D-WS9-235 ruling · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-235** · BUG-245 · D-WS9-122 · D-WS7-166 (the cook-time cap) · PRD §17.5.1.
- **Hans, verbatim:** *"filtering the wizard on active time and whatnot is NOT MVP and can be deferred to the roadmap."*
- ✅ **WHAT IS IN MVP: the active-time NUMBER is derived and stored on every meal (D-WS9-235 item 2), so this feature starts with its data already populated.** **What is deferred: any wizard control, preference field, prompt instruction or catalog filter keyed on active time** — e.g. *"under 20 minutes of hands-on time"* as a cap distinct from D-WS7-166's total-time cap, or steering weeknights toward low-active meals.
- ⚠️ **When it is picked up, it is a PREFERENCE-CONTRACT change (a second cap beside `maxCookTimeMinutes`) plus a selection-filter change, and it inherits D-WS9-235's rule that a cap constrains SELECTION and never the number.** The obvious product shape is the D-WS7-166 control with a second row; do not design it now.
- ✅ **Display IS ruled (September 10, Hans): capture unconditionally; show it on meal cards / meal detail if it is not much more work — sized in D-WS9-235's Phase 1. This entry defers only FILTERING/steering.**
- 🔵 **THE DATA, MEASURED September 11 (server lane, read-only; public, non-archived dinners with a derived time, n = 1,189) — recorded for when this is picked up, NOT a reopening of the ruling:** total ≤ 30 / 35 / 40 / 45 / 50 / 60 → **6** / 15 / 51 / 115 / 197 / 435 · active ≤ 15 / 20 / 25 / 30 → 1 / 14 / 74 / **177**. **A 30-minute cap on total time is a six-dinner shelf; the same cap on hands-on time would be 177.** Until this is picked up, thin short-cap shelves are met by live composition under BUG-245's selection rule and by Hans's planned 30-minute catalog supplement.
- 🔵 **HANS, September 11 (midday), after seeing honest draft times of 43 and 55 on a 30-minute plan — product input, verbatim, NOT yet a ruling that moves this out of the roadmap:** *"I'm ok with how it's working right now. the times are honest. and if we display the prep time, and especially if we give a prep time max with a flexible total time that's perfect."* **That is this entry's feature described from the user's side — a hands-on ceiling with a loose total.** The display half is already BUG-245's mobile half. **Whether the hands-on CAP is pulled into MVP was put to Hans (September 11).**
- ✅ **HANS ANSWERED, September 11 afternoon — verbatim, and it REFINES this entry rather than reopening it:** *"for hands-on, I feel like that's almost more important than total time. a 45 minute meal where I'm active the whole time is a pain on a busy night (think of a risotto with constant stirring and steps), but a 45 minute meal where I put things on a sheetpan and multi-task or watch my kids while it bakes is fine if I need an easy night of cooking. I'm thinking the labels may need an adjustment more than we need to engineer options. a true 30 minute ceiling sounds appealing, but if a meal is 8 minutes of prep and 37 minutes total to cook, I don't think a home chef would complain. the edge to consider with prep/active being low is a slow cooker meal - if the chef needs dinner on the table and it's 8 minutes of prep, but 4 hours of cooking, that's not a great weeknight option"* **What that settles:** (1) **no new cap option now** — *labels, not options*: every place a time shows carries BOTH numbers, total and hands-on, plainly labelled (BUG-245's mobile half, building September 11: `38 min · 10 min hands-on`); (2) **the MVP cap stays on total time**, and an honest few-minute miss is fine (BUG-245); (3) **the roadmap item is reframed:** not "a second cap on active time" but **a weeknight-suitability read that needs BOTH bounds — low hands-on AND a bounded total** (a slow-cooker dinner fails on total; a risotto fails on hands-on). Design it as one control, not two rows, when it is picked up. **Still post-MVP.**
