### D-WS9-238 — When the eligible shelf is thin, does the shelf guard relax and let Kiwi invent? — ✅ RULED by Hans, September 14, 2026: CATALOG FIRST, AI FALLBACK

- **Raised:** September 12, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 / plan-gen · **Tags:** `[PLAN-GEN]` `[PROMPT]` `[COST]` `[PRODUCT]` · **Status:** 🔵 **OPEN — a decision, not a defect** · **Source:** Hans, challenging chat-Claude's BUG-255 (b) ruling · **Cross-ref:** 🔴 **BUG-255** (where the measurement and the withdrawal live) · **D-WS9-073** (the shelf guard's own entry) · D-WS9-037 (coverage degrades on actual coverage, not a flag) · D-WS7-166 (the cap as a shelf predicate) · `kiwi_plan_generation_arc_scope.md` §3 · `kiwi_go_live_todos.md` (the supplement row this decision may retire).
- **Hans, verbatim:** *"if it can't find a catalog option for a slot it should make up a recipe and meal or meals as needed. I caught this because you created a list of 70 meals in under 30 minutes no problem."*
- ✅ **RULED by Hans, September 14, 2026, verbatim:** *"worth measuring to be sure it's not crazy, but if a meal doesn't exist it should be generated from the wizard. the process should try to pull from the catalog (which is built to reduce the every time cost of creating many meals), and then fall back to AI to create meals if none match the user's criteria."*
- 🔴 **WHAT THIS SETTLES, AND IT REFRAMES THE GUARD RATHER THAN TUNING IT: the catalog is a COST OPTIMISATION, not the boundary of what Kiwi can offer.** The shelf guard’s job is therefore **not** "protect a thin shelf by repeating meals" — it is **"decide when to stop searching the catalog and start generating."** A slot with no catalog match is a GENERATION, not a repeat. **D-WS9-073’s guard was written for a 1,214-meal catalog and read as a scarcity rule; under this ruling scarcity is not a reason to repeat, it is a trigger to invent.**
- ⚠️ **THE ONE MEASUREMENT HANS ATTACHED ("worth measuring to be sure it’s not crazy") — owed before the build, not before the ruling: the PER-GENERATION COST of an invention-heavy plan.** If most slots miss the catalog, a week’s plan becomes N generations instead of N lookups, on the most latency-sensitive path in the product and against the spend guard’s per-user cap. **Measure: cost and wall-clock for a plan where 0 / half / all slots miss, and the per-user-cap headroom that leaves.** ✅ **The ruling does not depend on the answer — the answer sizes the guard’s threshold and tells us whether a cap is reachable in normal use.**
- ⚠️ **Chat-Claude’s note, recorded as a read and not a ruling:** the 30-minute shelf is now **12** meals (D-WS9-239’s catalog pass, measured from the DB). **On a 30-minute cap this ruling is what makes the promise deliverable at all** — 12 catalog dinners cannot fill repeated weeks, so generation is the mechanism, not the exception.
- ✅ **THE PREMISE IS CORRECT AND ALREADY BUILT.** Live gap-fill is the arc's design (§3): the shelf is a pool the AI composes from, invention fills what it cannot cover, and the fallback triggers on measured coverage rather than a flag. **Two of four dinners in the September 11 round were live-composed.** The capability is not the constraint.
- 🔴 **THE CONSTRAINT IS ONE SENTENCE OF PROMPT.** D-WS9-073's shelf guard — *"never abandoning the shelf"* — was written to protect Block 4b-1's reach gain against a 1,214-dinner shelf. At a 30-minute cap the eligible shelf is **six**, and the guard keeps pointing the model back at six meals the rotation nudge has already exhausted. **Guard and nudge conflict precisely when the cap is tight.**
- **The three shapes, none built, none ruled:**
  - **(a) THRESHOLD RELAX** — when the eligible shelf is below N (N unmeasured; six is clearly below it, 116 at a 45-minute cap probably is not), the guard softens to *prefer* the shelf rather than *never abandon* it. **Smallest change; one prompt edit per body; the cost moves per generation and is unbounded.**
  - **(b) CATALOG SUPPLEMENT** — author 30-minute dinners into the catalog until the shelf is deep, and change no rule. **One-time cost; the 95-row target list exists; it fixes the 30-minute case only and every future tight constraint re-opens it.**
  - **(c) BOTH** — supplement the common caps, relax below a floor for the long tail.
- 💰 **PRICE THE DECISION BEFORE RULING IT, and do not use the arc's headline numbers as if they were this measurement.** Block 4b-3 measured store-backed **$0.0458** / three plans against live **~$0.27** / one plan (**~18×**), but neither was a thin-shelf 30-minute generation. ⚠️ **Owed: the real per-generation cost and latency of a 30-minute plan built mostly by invention** — a read-only measurement, and (a) should not be chosen without it. Latency matters as much as money: live slots run `expand` + `finalize`, which is where the 20s-per-call cost lives, and the whole latency block exists because generation speed is a product property.
- ⚠️ **Quality is the third axis and it is unmeasured.** Catalog dinners went through the D-WS9-040 quality gate and an editorial pass; an invented 30-minute dinner has had neither, and **BUG-245's whole history is invented meals writing dishonest times.** Invention gets cheaper to trust *after* the expand v9 ceiling and BUG-256's scheduler fix land — so this decision is also **sequenced behind them**, not independent of them.
- 🔵 **OPEN QUESTIONS:** what N is · whether the relax is a prompt clause or a server-side signal passed into the payload (the payload already knows the shelf size) · whether `'most'` behaves differently from `'all'` · whether relaxing re-opens BUG-249 (repeats within one generation) by giving the model more freedom.

- ✅ **THE COST MEASUREMENT OWED BEFORE THIS BUILD — taken from `LLMCallLog` (30 days, successful calls) by the redesign arc's Phase 0, September 16, read-only:** an invented wizard meal ≈ expand (v6–v8: $0.027–0.036, 12–18 s) + finalize_steps (v7: $0.035, ~19 s) ≈ **$0.06–0.075 and ~30–40 s serial** (fan-out is parallel across meals), plus the candidate generate ($0.03–0.05, ~20 s, titles only). The store-fill generator: **$0.048 / meal, ~34 s, 99% cache-read.** So in the redesign flow (D-WS9-237: "Get more options" on a ≤10 shelf = up to 2 AI rounds of 3–5) **one round ≈ $0.20–0.35 and ~40 s wall.** ⚠️ **What this does NOT measure:** a whole invention-heavy PLAN at 0 / half / all slots missing the catalog (the original ask) — the redesign replaces that shape for the meals path, so the per-meal figure is the one the build needs. **The spend guard (D-WS9-241 D) is the per-user backstop.**

### D-WS9-239 — Intra-dish overlap: the step generator records where an overlap starts AND ends (`parallelGroup`), the scheduler honours it, existing meals get a tagging pass — ✅ RULED (a), September 12, 2026

- **Raised:** September 12, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 / plan-gen + scheduler · **Tags:** `[COOK-TIME]` `[PROMPT]` `[SCHEDULER]` `[DATA]` `[PRODUCT]` · **Status:** ✅ **RULED (a) by Hans, September 12, 2026 — IN SCOPE, sequenced as the server block right after WS9A lands and BEFORE the UAT 30-minute catalog supplement; the catalog tagging pass is a separable step whose per-meal cost is measured on 20 meals first. UNBUILT.** · **Source:** CC's read-only intra-dish measurement (BUG-256, second amendment) · **Cross-ref:** 🔴 **BUG-256** (the numbers) · **D-WS9-235** (the ruled derivation this extends — steps within a dish are SERIAL today; the scheduler's cross-dish parallelism is what "the scheduler's parallelism" has meant) · **BUG-253** (Ask-Kiwi imports are one-dish meals — the population this helps most) · **D-WS9-238** (the other half of the thin-shelf problem) · **BUG-018** (finish-alignment, kept) · D-WS6-034 (`parallelGroup`'s type drift, the field's own history) · `kiwi_go_live_todos.md` (the 30-minute catalog supplement).
- **What the measurement established (2,344 meal-schedules, September 12):** the recipes ARE written with intra-dish overlap in mind — *"While the potatoes bake, make the marinara"* — and D-WS9-235's serial-within-dish rule charges every such minute to the meal. **Removing the serialisation honestly is worth ~12 minutes mean over the catalog and takes the 30-minute shelf from 6 dinners to 17–20, the 45-minute shelf from 116 to ~250, the 60-minute shelf from 443 to ~680 — the largest lever on the "30-minute meals" promise measured to date, three times the catalog supplement's likely effect and ten times BUG-256's ordering fix.** ⚠️ **But only the START of an overlap is recoverable from text (195 steps, ~1 min mean, one shelf meal); the END — which later step needs the unattended step finished — is recorded nowhere, and without it every automatic rule either drains the potatoes before the boil ends or makes the griddle wait for the onions.** The missing bit is exactly what `parallelGroup` (exists on `RecipeInstructionStep`; set on 0 of 26,409 rows) was for.
- **The shape, none built:** **(1) generator contract** — the step-generation prompt (`finalize_steps` and its siblings) emits, on every step that may run inside an earlier unattended step of its own dish, a `parallelGroup` token naming that unattended step, and the SAME token on the unattended step; every untagged step after the group waits for the unattended step's finish. Prompt-playbook loop; one bump per body. **(2) scheduler** — honour the tag (the TEXT rule for tagged steps, the window-close for untagged ones); finish-alignment and attended-serial unchanged; re-derive on save as today. **(3) tagging pass** over existing catalog dinners — the cached-prompt overnight pattern that D-WS9-235 pre-authorised *"if the step data needs it"* (it does), then a re-derivation of every stored time. **(4) sequencing:** (1)+(2) BEFORE the UAT 30-minute catalog supplement, so the 95 new dinners are generated with the contract and never need the pass; (3) is separable and can follow.
- 💰 **Costs owed before ruling, not guessed:** the per-meal cost of the tagging pass at the cached-prompt rate (measure on 20 meals, then multiply) · whether the generator can be TRUSTED to place the window end (hand-check 20 tagged dishes against the timelines, the way the regex was checked) · the re-derivation's effect on saved plans is NIL by D-WS9-230 (forward-only; catalog meals are shared data and ARE re-derived).
- ⚠️ **What this does NOT reopen:** D-WS9-235's ruling that time is derived from steps with the scheduler's parallelism — this EXTENDS the scheduler's parallelism to inside a dish using data the generator supplies; it is not Σ-steps and not a second model. Active time is unaffected (0 of 2,344 changed). BUG-018's invariant is kept. **BUG-256's ordering fix (ALT-B) is NOT authorised by this entry; it is revisited only inside this build, where the two interact.**
- ✅ **RULED (a), Hans, September 12, 2026.** His framing of the kitchen, verbatim, which the design must honour: *"I think it's related to logic that you can't reliably chop stuff for 10 minutes while you're sautéing an onion. I don't want the kitchen to feel rushed, but things do need to run in parallel. doing the prep/chop stuff first makes cooking so much easier, and you can sautee two things at once if your food is ready to put in the pan, but that's a hard set of rules to create."* **Three of those four are already the rules and stay: (1) attended never overlaps attended — no chopping during a sauté (BUG-018 / D-WS7-164, single cook); (2) attended work MAY run inside an UNATTENDED window (a low caramelise, a bake, a simmer, a rest) — cross-dish today, and THIS entry extends it to inside a dish, only where the recipe's own steps declare the window; (3) prep-first is the recipe author's ordering and is not changed by this.** 🔴 **The fourth — two attended sautés at once when the food is ready — is DECLINED as scope: it is the "hard set of rules" Hans named, it would weaken the single-cook rule that keeps the number honest, and the intra-dish lever alone carries ~12 min mean without it. Do not re-propose it as part of this build.** ⚠️ **"Not rushed" is a design constraint on the build, not a slogan: the scheduler infers NO overlap — it honours only what the generator declares (start AND end), and a step that is not tagged waits, exactly as today. The derived number stays the honest one.** Remaining open, for the build's Phase 0 (not for Hans): the catalog pass's measured cost · the 20-dish hand-check of the generator's window placement · whether the card needs a label beyond D-WS9-236's hands-on time.

(2) The step-writing instructions exist in TWO places: `wizard.candidate.finalize_steps` (seed body) and the store harness's compiled `cachedSystemPrefix` (`store.finalize_steps`'s seed body is just `{{finalizeInput}}`; a reseed changes nothing there — a code deploy does). §10 replace-don't-layer applies across both; Phase 0 diffs them.   - **(1) THE LEVER WAS OVERSTATED IN THIS ENTRY, AND THE OVERSTATEMENT IS CHAT-CLAUDE'S.** The *"~12 minutes mean"* above is the **UPPER BOUND** (every attended step overlapping) from the September 12 measurement; the text-recoverable lever in that same measurement was **1.22 min mean**. Real model-placed tags give **7.55 min mean (Sonnet, all tags) / 4.95 min mean on the dishes whose tags survive a hand-check**; p50 is 0 on the trusted set — most dishes have nothing to overlap. **On the 20-meal sample, zero meals cross the 30-minute line under any tag set; 1–2 cross 45.** The *"30-minute shelf from 6 to 17–20"* projection does not survive: intra-dish overlap is an honesty correction of a few minutes on meals with real windows, not the shelf lever. **The 95-dinner UAT supplement is the shelf lever; this entry's sequencing ahead of it was justified by a number that was the ceiling, not the expectation.**
  - **(2) THE GENERATOR CANNOT YET BE TRUSTED TO PLACE THE END — the question this Phase 0 existed to answer, answered NO for both models tested.** Hand-check of 41 dishes: Sonnet tagged 16, **5 wrong-window (31%)**; Haiku tagged 23, **14 wrong-window (61%)**, plus 2 missed. The recurring shape is a rider that CONSUMES the window's product: *"thread the marinated shrimp"* riding the marinade rest; the ribs' 150-minute bake riding the oven preheat (starts cold, 15 min deleted); the fettuccine riding the water it cooks in (8 min deleted); a 500°F pizza preheat riding a roast in the same oven. **Every error is in the direction "not rushed" forbids — the number gets LOWER than true.** Chat-Claude's premise that bad tags can only make the number more conservative was **refuted**: true for structurally invalid tags, false for semantically wrong ones. **Haiku is out. Sonnet is usable only behind a re-measured error rate.** One structural rule catches 9 of the 19 wrong tags with zero false positives: **a `rest`/`hold` step never rides the `cook` immediately before it** (it is waiting on that cook by definition).
  - **(3) THE SCHEDULER DESIGN HOLDS; THE PERSISTENCE SURFACE IS WIDER THAN THE ENTRY SAID.** `parallelGroup` is not "write-rejected" in general — only the `/me/meals` canonical save returns 400; **every AI step schema strips it silently**, and so do the step-preserving re-save (`readPreservableSteps`), the meal fork (`STEP_COPY_FIELDS`) and every read projection feeding the scheduler — the day tags exist, a Dish Builder edit or a fork would silently drop them and the number would jump back up. `mealTiming.dishTotals` sums serially, so under tags a dish could stamp longer than its meal. **Design additions from the replay (160 tagged schedules, 0 early finishes, 0 attended overlaps, 0 order violations):** a token's group must be CONTIGUOUS (a token re-appearing after its group closed is invalid); the first step carrying a token must be the unattended window; **the meal total can get LONGER under a valid tag (1 of 160 — a list-scheduling anomaly, 79 → 82) — the guard is to schedule with tags honoured and ignored and emit the shorter, deterministic and cheap**; finish-aligned unattended riders change no total and break the intra-dish order pin — start-aligned it is. Tagging-pass economics: **Sonnet ≈ $0.017/meal → ≈ $20 for the catalog, ~2 h; no cache benefit at this prompt size** (the prefix is under the cache floor). The two step-writing instruction copies (wizard finalize body · store harness prefix) have DIVERGED around a byte-identical step-rules core — Phase 1 edits both in lockstep.

### D-WS9-237 — The meal-selection plan flow: the wizard returns MEALS the user multi-selects, and suggested plans stay — ✅ SCREENS RULED by Hans, September 15, 2026 (mockup round 2); build NOT commissioned

- **Raised:** September 10, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 → the plan-building redesign (sequencing per Hans below; `kiwi_roadmap.md` does not reflect it yet) · **Tags:** `[PRODUCT]` `[PLAN-GEN]` `[ROADMAP]` · **Status:** 🔵 **DIRECTION RECORDED — this entry owns only the flow and its sequencing; every piece below has its own owner entry** · **Source:** Hans, device-pass notes on BUG-249, and his correction the same evening · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-120** (Cookbook scope) · **D-WS9-234** (Playlist) · **D-WS9-200** (the hand-off) · **D-WS9-191** (the chooser redesign) · D-WS7-207 · BUG-249 · D-WS7-166 · roadmap row 7 Phase D · PRD §9.5.
- **Hans, first mention, verbatim:** *"there is an upcoming redesign of the meal plan generation coming where users will select meals for their plan vs. having suggested plans. The suggested plans option will still be available, so that's valuable work to fix."*
- **Hans, the same evening, verbatim — the flow and the sequencing:** *"it's coming up in the roadmap/sequence one we get the last few P1 bugs and grocery stuff put to bed. This is where a user can use the wizard to get a list of meals that they multi-select for a plan. similarly, users will be able to search and filter and sort the Kiwi Cookbook (maybe try that term?) to find meals they can add to a plan."* · on screens: *"We should plan on some HTML or whatever mockups to talk through the screens in detail, but the specs are well defined and available in canon."*
- 🔴 **CORRECTION, and the lesson is §27.3's: this entry's first draft said "IT WAS NOT IN CANON" after three searches — FALSE. The searches used "select meals" / "redesign" vocabulary; canon files this under "Kiwi Cookbook" and "Playlist."** Where the pieces live:
  - **Browse/search/sort/filter the Kiwi Cookbook and add to a plan** → **D-WS9-120** (search bar, attribute sort/filter, a Cookbook chip on Add Meal · Swap for Different · Recipes → Meals) + `kiwi_cookbook_spec.md` §6 / roadmap row 7 **Phase D** (browse · sort · view · save-creates-copy · add-to-plan).
  - **"Users select meals from a list to build their plan"** → Hans, quoted in **D-WS9-200**: *"when we go to a model where users select meals from a list to build their plan, ultimately the user will choose and they control the selection of combinations that result in more or less waste."*
  - **The Playlist** (save meals, build plans from them, include them in generation) → **D-WS9-234**.
  - **Favorites surfacing in the plan-builder / add-meal-to-plan screens** → **D-WS7-207**.
  - **The three-candidate chooser that stays** → **D-WS9-191** (pared-back draft-review cards).
- ✅ **CONFIRMED BY HANS, September 10: the wizard's multi-select list screen is NOT designed, and neither is the Playlist (D-WS9-234). The mockup session designs both before any build.**
- ✅ **What it settles now: suggested plans are NOT retired, so fixing them (BUG-249, D-WS7-166's shelf predicate) is not throwaway work.** ✅ **And D-WS7-166's shelf — the capped, filtered, fatigue-aware catalog query — is the natural pool for the wizard's meal list and for Cookbook filters, so build it as shared, not wizard-private.**
- ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 15, 2026 — mockup round 1 → round 2; the design canvas "Kiwi Meal Selection" holds the boards). Four rulings, one open list:**
  1. **Home has TWO entries: "Use my preferences" → the Kitchen Wizard, and "Tell Kiwi" — its label left of the free-text input, otherwise unchanged.** 🔴 **SURPRISE ME IS RETIRED.** Verbatim: *"surprise me goes away. we shouldn't plan on trying to put 5 meals together in a single plan and be right. it's not realistic or probable."* (The 3c §7.6 zero-typing path goes with it.)
  2. **The entry decision lives ON the Kitchen Wizard screen, not on Home.** At the top: **"Build my plan", terracotta, DISABLED until the user picks a path** — in Hans's words *"Create plan by selecting meals"* or *"Select plan, have kiwi put in the meals"* (labels are open copy). **Path A → the meal-select screen (3). Path B → today's three-plan chooser (D-WS9-191), unchanged.** Under the choice, two dials, each **None · Some · Mostly · All**: **Playlist meals** (default unselected) and **Discovery meals** (default None — today's `discoveryMealsPerWeek` Off / 1 / 2 becomes a share of the plan; the concept is `kiwi_cookbook_spec.md` §4.2's, outside preferred cuisines and recent history). **Everything below the dials — plan length, household, the Adjust-saved-prefs disclosure, notes — stays exactly as built.** The goal, verbatim: *"simplify the entry decision: tell me what you want, or kiwi will suggest things."*
  3. **The meal-select screen: Kiwi returns ~15 matching meals for the request (cap it — *"we should cap it so it's usable"*), the user selects — FEWER OR MORE than the plan length is allowed — and "Build my week" compiles EXACTLY those into ONE ACTIVE plan.** Verbatim: *"no different combinations, just one plan the user created based off meals kiwi suggested. no draft, no save, just create an active meal plan for the user with the meals in the plan."* 🔴 **So "beside, replacing, or feeding the chooser" is answered NONE OF THE THREE — the picks ARE the plan, and the chooser serves path B only.** **Cookbook search / sort / filter is NOT in this flow** — that is the separate Cookbook screen, post-go-live (D-WS9-120). No source row and no filter row on the meal-select screen.
  4. **Playlist is a BOTTOM-NAV TAB** (fifth tab; D-WS9-234 carries the model). Verbatim: *"users manage the meals they cook the most. Cooking fatigue is a big factor in why people fall off cooking… I want to head off user attrition."*
- 🔵 **OPEN after round 2 — chat-Claude's proposals on the canvas, Hans to rule:** the path-card copy (drawn *"I'll pick the meals"* / *"Kiwi picks the meals"*, with one-line sublines) · whether an unselected Playlist dial ALSO holds the button, or means "Kiwi's call" (drawn: only the path gates it) · **All on one dial forces None on the other** (they share one plan) · the thin shelf — when a 30-minute cap yields 6 meals, widen the cap or let Kiwi invent up to ~15 (D-WS9-238 says catalog first, AI fallback; drawn: no invention, the honest count) · tab order (drawn Home · Plans · Recipes · Playlist · Groceries). ⚠️ **FOR THE BUILD SPEC, NOT A DESIGN QUESTION: "create an active plan directly" bypasses the wizard-draft lifecycle** (D-WS9-072 / BUG-047: generation clears, nothing else does; drafts are `isWizardDraft`) — **path A must say which rows it writes and that it never leaves a draft behind.** The roadmap update placing this arc after the P1s and grocery work is still owed.
- ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 15, 2026, evening — his read of round 2; round 3 is on the canvas). Five more, and one PRINCIPLE that outranks them:**
  1. 🔴 **THE PRINCIPLE — "good every time, which makes it great."** Verbatim: *"The book 'The Effortless Experience' talks about customer service, but the concept of 'wowing' a customer rarely actually works, and is more prone to pissing people off. we want this to be good every time, which makes it great."* **Kiwi does not guess that a user might like something random.** The target is the goulash case — *"my family tested some plans and made a goulash, which we had never had before, and it stood out as a pretty easy meal we would try again."* Apply this to every suggestion surface, not only the dial below.
  2. **DISCOVERY MEALS ARE RE-DEFINED: meals NEW TO THE USER that still match their preferences — not meals outside their cuisines.** 🔴 **This retires `kiwi_cookbook_spec.md` §4.2's generation rule (*"N meals outside preferred cuisines AND outside recent history"*) and its "wild card" helper copy; redline that section at close.** Playlist meals = meals from the user's playlist. **Both dials default UNSET, and unset on both means today's behaviour — straight preferences** (this supersedes round 2's "Discovery default None").
  3. **The path cards must read as Kiwi curating, not the user hunting.** *"I'll pick the meals"* was rejected: *"makes me think I have to go pick meals that I want. not that Kiwi is going to curate a list based on my preferences."* Drawn in round 3: section *"What should Kiwi suggest?"* → **"Meals to choose from"** / **"Complete plans"** (proposed copy, not ruled).
  4. **The meal card carries everything the decision needs: name · description · times (active AND total) · macros · tags.** Verbatim: *"this is all the user will have to decide what they want, so they need all the information consolidated and consumable here."* **And a "Get more options" button in line with the cards at the bottom of the list — fetches 3–5 meals at a time, up to 4 times.**
  5. **The thin shelf: NO per-filter widen links** (*"hard to scale"*). Below a threshold the user gets "Get more options" once or twice, then a message — Hans's words: *"your preferences and restrictions don't have a lot of options, refine your preferences, or use Tell Kiwi."* The 30-minute case itself is handled by the supplement meals (D-WS9-240 item 6). 🔵 **Chat-Claude's read, licence to refuse: "Get more options" is where D-WS9-238's catalog-first / AI-fallback lives — catalog first, invention only when the shelf is empty, never past the tap cap.** The threshold N is unruled.

### D-WS9-245 — The two wizard dials (Playlist · Discovery), how they are STORED and how a level becomes a count — ✅ RULED by chat-Claude under delegation, September 16, 2026; 🔴 rule (3) OVERRULED by Hans the same day (the Playlist dial gets a STORED default too); server half BUILT and its migration APPLIED; the playlist column + the client half = Block 2

- **Raised:** September 16, 2026, by the redesign arc's Phase 0 (Q2.2) · **Owner:** the redesign arc, Block 1 (server) + Block 2 (client) · **Tags:** `[SCHEMA]` `[AI-PROMPT]` `[PLAN-GEN]` `[PREFERENCES]` · **Status:** ✅ **RULED — technical/architecture call made under Hans's standing delegation; a migration Hans runs** · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-237** (the dials as ruled: None · Some · Mostly · All, both unset by default, unset = today's behaviour; Discovery = new-to-the-user within preferences) · **D-WS9-234** (the Playlist dial) · D-WS7-035 (per-run overrides never write back) · `kiwi_cookbook_spec.md` §4.2 (the field this replaces) · D-WS9-230 (the September 14 amendment licensing a user-scoped column reshape with no row migration path).
- **What Phase 0 established (read-only):** `UserPreferences.discoveryMealsPerWeek` is `Int NOT NULL @default(0)`, pinned to 0..2 by three Zod `.max(2)`s (`me.ts` PATCH allow-list, `schemas/wizard.ts`, `schemas/tellKiwi.ts`) and seven tests; written by onboarding step 2 and the Preferences screen; carried per-run by `perRunPayload.ts` (override ?? stored, default 0); **read by exactly two seed prompt bodies** (`WIZARD_SET_PREFERENCES_GENERATE_BODY`, `WIZARD_DIRECTED_GENERATE_BODY`), where it is already defined as *"outside the preferred cuisines OR a preferred-cuisine dish deliberately unfamiliar versus recentRotation"* — i.e. the prompt is half-way to Hans's new meaning already. **A stored "unset" is impossible on that column; a per-run unset already is (`.optional()` = omit). No compiled prefix reads it.**
- ✅ **THE RULING:** **(1) one vocabulary, stored and per-run:** the stored preference becomes an enum **`DiscoveryLevel { none, some, mostly, all }`** with `@default(none)`, replacing the Int — **one migration, mapping existing rows 0 → none, 1 → some, 2 → mostly** (a user-scoped column; the September 14 amendment applies; Hans runs it). The Preferences screen and onboarding step 2 show the same four chips as the wizard dial. **(2) Per-run semantics are D-WS7-035's:** the dial sends a value only when the user sets it; omitted = the stored preference applies — which is exactly *"unset = today's behaviour"*. **(3) Playlist is PER-RUN ONLY** — no stored default, no column; omitted = none; and the dial is not offered to a user with zero playlist meals (D-WS9-234). **(4) A level becomes a COUNT on the server, from the plan length, before the prompt sees it** — the prompts keep receiving integers as today: `none` = 0 · `some` = ceil(days × 0.3) · `mostly` = ceil(days × 0.7) · `all` = days (for a 5-day plan: 0 / 2 / 4 / 5); **the fractions are a first setting, not a ruling — tune with data.** **(5) All on one dial forces None on the other** (they share one plan), enforced server-side, mirrored in the UI. **(6) The two prompt bodies are re-worded to Hans's meaning** — *new to this user, still inside their preferences; never a random or outside-cuisine pick* — which is a `prisma:seed` and two version bumps; the *"outside the preferred cuisines"* clause is DELETED, not layered (§10).

Reseed owed for the two re-worded generate bodies.**

### D-WS9-243 — The store-bought shortcut has NO DATA SLOT: `Dish.substitutions` runs scratch→bought only, so a component that is bought BY DEFAULT cannot carry its from-scratch alternative — the generator either stores the long path as the default or inverts the path labels

- **Raised:** September 15, 2026, by the substitution lane's first-10 gate (it STOPPED at 4 of 10 ≤ 30 and reported the cause rather than continuing) · **Owner:** the catalog generators (`storeFillPrompts.ts`, the store-fill volatile input) for the fix; WS9B for the grid half · **Tags:** `[CATALOG]` `[AI-PROMPT]` `[SCHEMA-SHAPE]` · **Status:** 🔴 **OPEN — ruling Hans's. It BLOCKS the rerun of the remaining 85 supplement meals (D-WS9-240 item 6) and nothing else.** · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-242** (the effort-class grid, whose defaults this distorts) · **D-WS9-240 item 6** (the 95) · **D-WS9-066** (the dual-path model: scratch is the default, bought is the option) · **BUG-270** (stored time = base + DEFAULT path) · **BUG-121** (both paths render; unbuilt, which is why nothing user-visible is broken today).
- 🔴 **THE MECHANISM, measured on 10 regenerated meals.** The wire sentence told the generator to build the default path around the bought product and treat the from-scratch version as *"the optional bought→scratch alternative."* **There is no bought→scratch direction:** `Dish.substitutions` entries go scratch→bought, and BUG-270 stores base + the SCRATCH path as the meal's time. So the model expressed the alternative as a swappable component and the stored default then carried whichever side it had labelled `scratch`, two ways:
  - **The long version lands in `scratch`, so the STORED time is the long one.** KM-004 Turkey Club: *"Roast a 1½ lb turkey breast 50–60 min"* tagged `turkey/scratch`, deli turkey tagged `bought` — **derived 94 on the default, 26 on the bought path.** KM-008 Broiled Salmon: stovetop rice 22 min `scratch`, pouch rice `bought` — 29 / 19. **The 30-minute premise loses on the number that gets stored.**
  - 🔴 **The labels INVERT, which is the worse half because the number looks right.** KM-005 / KM-006 / KM-010: canned tuna and canned soup, boxed mac, and rotisserie chicken tagged `scratch`; *"cook 1½ lb albacore in simmering water"*, *"elbow macaroni"* and *"raw boneless chicken breasts"* tagged `bought`, with `substitutions.product` set to the RAW INGREDIENT. Today's derived time is right; **under D-WS9-242's grid a level-3 user (*"buy it"*) would be handed the raw-chicken path.** ⚠️ **Nothing reads path labels yet (BUG-121 unbuilt), so this is latent, not live — but it is catalog data, and it is exactly what the grid will read the day it ships.**
- 📊 **The 10, derived through the shipped scheduler** (`parallelGroupDerive.ts` + `selectDefaultPathSteps`, `ADJACENCY_MAX_MINUTES = 5`), stored default / bought path: **BLT 23/23 · Smash Burgers 31/27 · Smash Burger Tacos 33/31 · Turkey Club 94/26 · Tuna Melts 29/38 · Hot Dogs + Boxed Mac 32/32 · Sheet-Pan Sausage 42/42 · Broiled Salmon 29/19 · Chicken Caesar Wraps 26/20 · Buffalo Quesadillas 38/52.** **4 of 10 ≤ 30 (23, 29, 29, 26) → the gate's STOP.** Shortcut honoured on the default path by reading: **15 of 23 products; 6 of 10 meals fully.** Misses are all the same shape — bagged slaw against a default that shreds half a cabbage, pouch rice against a 22-minute stovetop rice, bottled Caesar against a whisked dressing.
- 🔴 **THE CAUSE IS CHAT-CLAUDE'S, NAMED SO IT IS NOT REWRITTEN: the wire sentence invented a direction the schema does not have.** `componentRegistry` was existence-checked in that lane's Phase 0; **the `substitutions` direction was not, and the sentence was written against an imagined symmetric model.** §27.6 item 4 / item 9 — an instruction that names something which does not exist. ⚠️ **Do not re-issue any wording that asks for a bought→scratch alternative until this entry is ruled.**
- 🔵 **THE THREE SHAPES, for Hans to pick from:** **(a)** leave the wire as is and let the STORED default become f(effort class) once D-WS9-242's grid ships — defers the problem into the grid build and leaves 95 meals wrong in the meantime · **(b)** add a bought→scratch direction to the schema and the wire — the general fix, a real schema-shape change, and it reopens what BUG-270 means by *"the default path"* · **(c)** **drop the alternative clause entirely and author the shortcut as a PLAIN BASE INGREDIENT with no `substitutions` entry at all.**
- ✅ **CHAT-CLAUDE RECOMMENDS (c), with an explicit licence to refuse — the reasoning, and the evidence it rests on:** **these 95 meals are DEFINED by their shortcut.** A *"BLT with bakery bread and chips from the bag"* is not a from-scratch dish carrying an option; the bought item IS the recipe, and there is no from-scratch intent to preserve. ✅ **It is also the pattern the existing 1,124-meal shelf already uses** — D-WS9-242's own Phase F measured 167 dishes starting from bought tortillas, 527 from bought stock and 12 from store pizza dough, all as **plain ingredients, not as substitutions**. So (c) makes the 95 look like the rest of the catalog rather than inventing a shape for them. **It needs no schema change, no grid dependency, and no second ruling.** ⚠️ **Its honest costs, both accepted: the 95 carry no bought paths and are therefore inert to the effort-class grid (correct — a meal whose ingredients are already bought has nothing to classify); and the store generate prefix needs a SHORTCUT MODE branch, because *"author this product as a plain ingredient"* is the opposite of what the prefix tells every other catalog run.**
- ⚠️ **What this does NOT block:** the effort-class stamp (landed, `b3ae94d`), the prefix parity and vocabulary work (landed), and the redesign arc. **Only the 85 wait.**
- ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 15, 2026, morning): OPTION (c), REFINED — THE SHORTCUT PRODUCT IS AUTHORED AS A PLAIN BASE INGREDIENT AND NO FROM-SCRATCH ALTERNATIVE IS AUTHORED FOR IT.** Hans, verbatim: *"we don't need a 'why to go from taco kit to making the spice mix.' and no one is going to bake turkey breasts to slice them for a sandwich. and no one is going to bake bread for a BLT."* ⚠️ **AND THE SCOPE FENCE, VERBATIM, BECAUSE IT IS THE KIND OF IDEA THAT COMES BACK: *"there's an argument that the day after thanksgiving could be a good day for turkey clubs, or a quick bread maker loaf would improve a BLT, but we're 100% not chasing that for this piece."* DO NOT REOPEN THE SEASONAL / BREAD-MACHINE VARIANTS IN THIS LANE OR THE NEXT ONE.**
- ✅ **THE DELEGATED HALF, CHAT-CLAUDE'S CALL: NEVER AUTHOR IT — not "author it and hide it."** Hans offered both (*"we can delete the manual cook option, or just leave it and never expose it unless a user clicks"*). **Never authoring is strictly cheaper in four places: an unexposed scratch path is still catalog data that the D-WS9-242 grid, the grocery list (D-WS9-067), Prep & Cook (D-WS9-068) and BUG-121's renderer each have to decide what to do with; BUG-121 would need a new never-expose flag, which is new state carrying no user value; it is the shape the existing 1,124-meal shelf already uses for bought staples (plain ingredients, not substitutions); and an authored scratch path is exactly what puts a 94-minute turkey club back into the stored default.** ⚠️ **Nothing is deleted — the 95 are regenerated from scratch, so this is "do not write it", not a data cleanup.**
- 🔵 **THE RULE AS IT REACHES THE PROMPT — a SHORTCUT-MODE BRANCH in the store generate prefix, and it is a branch rather than a new sentence because it inverts the prefix's standing instruction:** when a `shortcut_used` product is on the wire for a target, **that product is a base ingredient of the dish; author no `substitutions` entry for it and no from-scratch steps to replace it.** **Components NOT named by `shortcut_used` are unchanged** — the normal model still applies (scratch is the default path, the bought product is the option), which is why the taco-packet case Hans raised keeps both paths and is untouched by this ruling. ✅ **Mechanical acceptance criterion, checkable without judgment: across the regenerated 95, the number of `substitutions` entries whose product matches that meal's `shortcut_used` must be ZERO.**
- 🔵 **THE LEFTOVER, RECORDED AND NOT COMMISSIONED — it belongs to D-WS9-242's grid build, not here: the shelf stores ONE time per meal, and once the grid ships the default is PER USER.** A level-2 or level-3 user sees a shelf number derived from the scratch path on every component where the bought path is materially faster — **Phase F measured 180 components saving ≥ 20 minutes**, so this is not hypothetical. **The 95 do not need it** (under this ruling their default IS the fast path), which is why it is recorded rather than solved. **Shapes when it is picked up: store both times, or derive at query time — CC has already shown both are cheap to compute.**
- ✅ **BUILT AND AUDITED PASS — `d359ba3` (LOCAL, September 15). THE RULING HELD ON ITS OWN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION: 0 of 27 `substitutions` entries across the 95 names a shortcut product, checked mechanically AND read by eye.** The prefix gained a distinct `# Shortcut mode` section placed after `# Store-bought substitutions` as its explicit override (the shape chat-Claude proposed and CC adopted), and `b3ae94d`'s bought→scratch paragraph was DELETED, not qualified. Suite 2226 = 2224 + 2 skip; break red, restore sha1-identical (CC disclosed that the prefix's token-count doc comment was edited after the sha1 pair and before the commit — the pair still proves what it tested). Generate prefix 4,931 → 5,150 tokens; finalize unchanged. **$4.22 for 95 meals, $0.0444/meal, 0 API failures.**
- 🟢 **THE FIX IS VISIBLE IN THE ONE NUMBER THAT DIAGNOSED THE DEFECT: the Turkey Club went 94 → 22 derived minutes.** First-10 gate passed at **6 of 10 ≤ 30** (was 4 of 10). **Full distribution of the 95: ≤30 21 · 31–45 51 · >45 23**, against the last honest run's **8 / 38 / 49** — the ≤30 shelf nearly tripled and the >45 tail halved. ⚠️ **These are FRESH generations, so meal-by-meal comparison against the old run is not like-for-like; the distribution is.** ✅ **The public shelf excluding `km30-` is UNCHANGED at 16 / 228 / 631 (n=1,201), which is the guard that the run touched nothing it should not have.** Including them: 37 / 300 / 723.
- 🔵 **ONE BEHAVIOUR THE RULING DID NOT ASK FOR, AND IT IS HANS'S CALL — shortcut mode suppressed substitutions on components it does not name, not just on the ones it does.** Total `substitutions` across the 95 is **27, with 70 of 95 meals carrying none**; the pre-ruling 10-meal run carried **17 entries on 10 meals** (1.7/meal → 0.28/meal, a ~6× drop). **The ruling says unnamed components keep both paths — *"a taco spice packet keeps both paths"* — so this is over-reach, not compliance.** ✅ **Chat-Claude's read, licence to refuse: LEAVE IT.** These 95 exist to be fast; suppressing marginal swaps on a meal built from bought products is consistent with its purpose, the 27 that survived are the sensible ones (seasoning packets, bottled vinaigrettes, pre-grated cheese, a broth carton), and restoring them costs another ~$4 regeneration for a gain nobody has asked for. **If Hans wants them back it is a nudge in `# Shortcut mode`'s last paragraph, not a data fix.**
- ⚠️ **WHAT THE RERUN DID NOT FIX, stated so it is not mistaken for done: 23 of the 95 still derive >45 minutes** on a target list whose whole premise is a 30-minute dinner. **The three LONG reads in the 13-meal hand-check are all window/rider losses of the D-WS9-239 class, none a shortcut-rule failure** — so the remaining tail is the scheduler contract, not this ruling. 🔵 **Cheap follow-on nobody has run: the target CSV carries an `est_total_min` column that has never been compared against derived minutes. That comparison would say whether the 23 are generation misses or whether the target list itself was optimistic — $0, one query.**

### D-WS9-242 — What a store-bought path IS, and which path is the DEFAULT: bought paths must be real products that replace the component, and staples a home cook buys (dough, pasta, ravioli, fries) may be the NORMAL recipe rather than the shortcut — 🟡 OPEN, measurement instructed (BUG-270 Phase F), ruling Hans's

- **Raised:** September 15, 2026, by Hans, reading BUG-270's Phase C report · **Owner:** WS9B (row 3c, the store-bought toggle) for the ruling; the catalog generators (`storeFillPrompts.ts`, the wizard finalize prefix) for the fix · **Status:** ✅ **RULED September 15, 2026 (Hans): default path = level × effort class (assembly / cooking / craft), class stamped by a $0 derivation, same vocabulary in prompt, data and preference labels; measured first (Phase F, below). 🟡 UNBUILT — rides as ONE lane with the store-prefix parity fix and the 95 rerun; placement on the Preferences screen unless Hans objects** · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-066** (the dual-path model this refines — *"the user sees the full from-scratch recipe and may decide, per dish, to take the shortcut"*) · D-WS9-067 / D-WS9-068 (grocery and prep follow the selection) · **BUG-121** (both paths render everywhere; P1, unbuilt) · **BUG-270** (whose Phase C surfaced the two examples) · D-WS9-148 (the toggle surface) · D-WS9-240 item 6 (the 30-minute supplement, whose premise is the shortcut).
- **Hans, verbatim, on the Patty Melt bought path (*"warm pre-sliced onions"* standing in for a 38-minute caramelize):** *"I don't like that suggestion - it saves maybe like 2 minutes. buying pre-carmelized onions would save time if the product exists (it probably does)."* **And on the default:** *"I'm ok that we have something like that, where it's totally from scratch, but I want to make sure we have normal home meals and start with store-bought pizza dough, store-bought ravioli, store bought steak fries, etc. At least that has to be happening with pizza dough and ravioli. and pasta.. right?"* **And confirming the consumer side:** *"the sequencer needs an update to hide the store-bought or the full cook steps based on what the user chooses on the meal. and obviously same with the grocery list"* — that half is already ruled (D-WS9-066/067/068) and unbuilt (BUG-121); this entry is the two halves that were NOT ruled.
- 🔴 **THE TWO QUESTIONS, stated so the measurement answers them:** **(1) QUALITY BAR — a `bought` path must name a product that EXISTS and REPLACES the component.** Pre-sliced onions do not replace caramelized onions; jarred marinara does replace a simmered sauce. Canon has no such bar today: the generator built a bought path for every `Dish.substitutions` entry (D-WS9-066 measured 34/34) and nothing judged the product. **(2) WHICH PATH IS THE DEFAULT for staple components.** D-WS9-066 makes from-scratch the default everywhere. For pizza dough, fresh pasta / ravioli / gnocchi, tortillas, stock, fries and pastry, **the normal home recipe STARTS from the bought item — it is an ingredient, not a shortcut — and making it from flour is the optional upgrade.** A from-scratch default on those dishes makes a 35-minute weeknight pizza read as a 2½-hour project, drops it off every shelf, and hides the normal version behind a toggle nobody knows exists. ⚠️ **Hans is explicitly fine with SOME fully-from-scratch dishes existing (Detroit Pizza’s class); the requirement is that the NORMAL version exists and is what the catalog offers by default.**
- 🔵 **WHAT PHASE F MEASURES (read-only):** F.1 — how many public dishes’ default path MAKES a staple a home cook buys, per class, with and without a bought alternative, default-vs-bought minutes, 10 opened by eye for the detector’s false-positive rate · F.2 — for every component with a bought path, **minutes actually saved** (Σ default-path − Σ bought-path), its distribution, the count saving ≤ 5 minutes, a seeded random 25 read for "does this product exist and replace the component," and the count of the `pre-sliced | pre-cut | pre-chopped | diced` class · F.3 — the store prompt’s own words on what a bought path is and what qualifies a component. ⚠️ **A word-list is the DETECTOR for F.1, never the fix (BUG-266).**
- ✅ **WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE, said now so nobody waits on it:** **BUG-270’s re-stamp is correct under any answer here** — it stores base + DEFAULT path; if the default flips for staple components, those dishes re-derive and re-stamp for $0. **And the shortcut premise of the 30-minute supplement (D-WS9-240 item 6, `shortcut_used`) is exactly question (1) applied at generation time — the rerun of the 95 waits on this ruling as well as on the store-prefix parity fix.**
- 🔵 **LIKELY SHAPES OF THE RULING, for Hans to pick from once the numbers exist — not proposals:** (a) keep from-scratch as the universal default and fix only the quality bar; (b) a per-component default — staple components default to `bought`, everything else to `scratch` — expressed in data (`componentRegistry`), not in code, so the toggle still works both ways; (c) staple-from-scratch paths are generated only when the dish is *about* making that staple. **Each changes the generator prompts (a reseed) and the tagger; (b) also touches the catalog defaults (a carve-out write).**
- 🆕 **HANS, September 15, ~00:30Z, while Phase F ran — THE USER-SIDE HALF: defaults and overrides need a PREFERENCE, and the preference must align to a RULE.** Verbatim: *"I think we need to have a user preference on the first page of the signup, or change the preference 'store bought preference' to be a bit more clear and align it to this feature. So, a user could have three options like: 1. I prefer making it myself 2. I can mix, measure, and cut, but I enjoy convenience 3. My default is easy peasy, buy the lemon squeezy … defaults and overrides mean we need a preference, and we need that preference to align to a rule. how can we classify if a user wants to buy the bag of cole slaw mix and a thing of cole slaw dressing, or make one and buy the other? Can we maybe run another catalog update for a 'default' on from scratch or not and users can override if they want?"*
- ✅ **WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so nothing is built twice (§27.2): `UserPreferences.saucePreference` IS this preference** — `store_bought | balanced | homemade`, labels *"Store-bought preferred / Balanced / From scratch preferred"*, default `balanced`; D-WS9-065 (OPEN, unbuilt) already rules its RENAME because the name is wrong and the axis is general. **Hans’s three options map onto its three values one-to-one; what is new is (1) copy that states the RULE in the user’s own terms and (2) the rule itself — today the value is read at wizard generation for substitutions (D-WS9-064) and drives NO default on catalog meals, because the path filter is unbuilt (BUG-121).**
- 🔵 **CANDIDATE RULE (chat-Claude, September 15 — a proposal, licence to refuse; F.2’s numbers test it before anything is built): a component’s DEFAULT path = f(user level, the EFFORT CLASS of its scratch path), and the effort class is DERIVABLE from data already on the rows — no AI pass needed.** Classes: **assembly** (every scratch step is a prep phase — mix, measure, cut, shred: dressings, spice blends, slaw, guacamole, marinades) · **cooking** (the scratch path has a `cook` / `preheat` / `rest` phase: caramelized onions, simmered sauce, stock, beans from dry) · **craft** (the scratch path has a `rest`/rise or a shaping step AND is a staple a home cook buys: dough, fresh pasta, ravioli, tortillas, wrappers, pie crust). Grid: **level 1 "making it myself" → scratch for all three** · **level 2 "mix, measure, cut, but convenience" → scratch for assembly, BOUGHT for cooking and craft — the label literally describes the rule** · **level 3 "buy it" → bought wherever a bought path exists.** Coleslaw under the rule: shredding cabbage and mixing dressing are both *assembly*, so level 2 makes both, level 3 buys both, and *"buy the mix, make the dressing"* is the per-component OVERRIDE D-WS9-066 already provides (this week / forever). ⚠️ **The class can be stored once per component in `componentRegistry` by a $0 derivation pass (D-WS9-066 built that field and kept it separate from `substitutions` for exactly this kind of metadata) — so "another catalog update for a default" is a DERIVATION write, not a generation run; the only AI work is the quality bar in question (1).** ⚠️ **Where a staple has NO bought path (F.1’s from-scratch-only class), no preference can help — that is a generation gap to close on those dishes.**
- ⚠️ **PLACEMENT — chat-Claude’s recommendation, Hans’s call: NOT on the first page of signup.** §9 rules the signup → plan → grocery path as the highest priority and every added step as friction debt; signup today is email, password, phone and two consents (D-WS9-241 A). The preference already lives with the other cooking preferences (onboarding / Preferences), where a three-way choice with a one-line explanation reads naturally and can be changed later. **Renaming + re-labelling it there is D-WS9-065’s open work plus copy; moving it into signup is a new screen decision.**
- 📊 **PHASE F MEASURED (September 15, read-only, $0; 3,047 public dishes / 20,923 steps) — THE NUMBERS THE RULING RESTS ON.** **F.1, does the DEFAULT path make a staple a home cook buys?** Detector = make-verbs over default-path text, ~20% false positives (concentrated in fries — roasted wedges — and stock — manicotti "shells"), 10 opened by eye. **The NORMAL versions are there, overwhelmingly:** tortillas — 167 dishes start from bought, 4 make masa (tamales, sopes) · stock — 527 from bought, 1 from bones (Caldo de Pollo) · fresh pasta / dumplings — 15 from bought, 4 make it (all 4 offer the bought path; Potato Gnocchi 94 → 2) · **pizza dough / bread — 12 start from store dough, 17 make dough, and 16 of those 17 offer bought dough as a path** (Detroit-Style Pizza 125 → 60 · Pepperoni Pizza 74 → 30 · Garlic Naan 46 → 1) · fries — 56 make them, 22 with a bought path, **33 with none — oven fries and wedges, where the potato IS the recipe** · pie / puff pastry — 0 make, 6 from bought. **Dishes making a staple with NO bought path: 35 of 82, 33 of them the oven-fries class; Scallion Pancakes and Caldo de Pollo are the only from-scratch-is-the-point cases.** ✅ **So the default-flip question touches ~40 dishes and needs NO rewrite of any catalog default — the preference rule below handles it.** **F.2, are bought paths real shortcuts?** **1,644 components with a bought path on 1,459 dishes.** Minutes saved (Σ scratch − Σ bought): p10 1 · p50 4 · p90 20 · mean 7.2; **≤ 5 min: 990 (60%)** — mostly seasoning packets, bottled dressings and slaw mix: small time, real convenience, FEWER ITEMS TO BUY, which minutes-saved does not measure · ≤ 0: 123 · ≥ 20: 180. **Seeded random 25 (seed 270) by eye: 21 real products that replace the component · 4 NOT** — two save nothing (an Italian seasoning blend for two dried herbs, twice), one replaces a DIFFERENT component (pre-minced garlic for a roasted-garlic butter), one has no scratch path at all (Thai red curry paste from a jar on both paths). **The pre-cut class Hans named: 33 components (2%)** — fajita pepper blends, stir-fry beef, chicken cutlets, pre-cut squash, pre-chopped kale — **plus the two caramelized-onion cases, whose product text is *"pre-sliced caramelized onions"* / *"caramelized onion jam"*: the COMPONENT MATCHES.** 🔴 **CORRECTION AGAINST CHAT-CLAUDE, recorded so the example is not repeated: chat-Claude told Hans the Patty Melt shortcut was *"pre-sliced onions"* — the Phase C step text, relayed without asking what the PRODUCT was (§27.6 item 5). Hans’s principle stands; that example was the relay’s, not the generator’s.** **F.3, the store prompt’s own rule, quoted:** the finalize prefix defines a component as *"a convenience product the cook can buy INSTEAD of making that part of the dish from scratch"* and a bought path as *"1–3 NEW steps describing what the cook actually does with the store-bought product"*; the generate prefix carries the right TEST verbatim — *"would a good home cook plausibly buy this and still be making THIS dish — and would the substitute actually BE that component?"* — beside a slogan its own examples violate: *"a substitution replaces ASSEMBLY, never COOKING"*, while listing *refrigerated pizza dough*, *store-bought pie crust* and *rotisserie chicken* as legitimate. **`Dish.substitutions` is the ONLY source of bought-path candidates** (generate authors them; finalize tags paths only for dishes carrying them; `storeFill.mergeSteps` strips any tag outside the registry). **Compliance with the prompt’s own test ≈ 85% on the sample.**
- ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 15, ~00:45Z — *"I like your level 1, 2, 3 solution, I think that works well"*): THE DEFAULT PATH OF A COMPONENT = f(the user’s level, the component’s EFFORT CLASS).** Classes **assembly / cooking / craft**, derived from the phase tags already on the scratch-path steps and **stamped once per component into `componentRegistry` by a $0 derivation pass** (not a generation run). Grid: **level 1 (*"I prefer making it myself"*) → scratch for all three · level 2 (*"I can mix, measure, and cut, but I enjoy convenience"*) → scratch for assembly, BOUGHT for cooking and craft · level 3 (*"buy it"*) → bought wherever a bought path exists.** The per-component override (D-WS9-066, this week / forever) sits on top. **The SAME three words replace the "assembly, never cooking" slogan in the generate prefix and label the preference — one vocabulary in the prompt, the data and the UI, which is what "align the preference to a rule" means.** The preference is the existing `saucePreference` (D-WS9-065’s rename lands with this). ⚠️ **F.2 says the phase-derived class must be checked against the random-25 before it is stamped; if it misclassifies, the fallback is a model-authored class (~$10 over 1,644 components).** ⚠️ **The quality bar (question 1) stays a PROMPT rule, enforced by the prompt’s own TEST sentence — the 15% that fail it today are a catalog-quality follow-on, not a schema change.**
- 🔵 **SEQUENCING — Hans, *"can we do that update when we run the other update?"* — YES: this rides as ONE lane with the store-prefix parity fix (1b-ii wording) and the revert-and-rerun of the 95 with `shortcut_used` on the wire (D-WS9-240 item 6): prompt wording (both prefixes; a reseed) → the effort-class derivation stamp → the 95 rerun → hand-check. Not tonight; after the redesign-arc sequencing call.** **Placement stands as recommended unless Hans objects: the Preferences screen, renamed and re-labelled with the three options and a one-line explanation — not the signup form.**
- ✅ **THE DERIVATION STAMP LANDED — `b3ae94d` (LOCAL, September 15), AUDITED PASS. 1,843 components classified and written: assembly 1,311 · cooking 515 · craft 17 · unresolvable 9 (0.49%, now BUG-272).** Population reconciles exactly against Phase F: 1,852 registry entries on 1,655 dishes = public non-km30 1,524 + km30 120 + private-only 208, and **1,524 + 120 = Phase F's 1,644 public bought-path components** — two independent measurements agreeing to the row. **Stored times moved 0** (snapshot over 1,758 meals, taken in the dry run and re-read after the write). Pre-image on disk; `revert_class.ts --apply` restores all 1,651 touched dishes. Re-running the derivation is idempotent (`to write: 0`).
- 🔴 **CC REFUSED THE RULING'S LITERAL CLASS DEFINITIONS THREE WAYS, WITH EVIDENCE, AND THE REFINEMENTS ARE ADOPTED — under the literal mapping the random-25 scored 23/25; refined it scores 25/25.** ⚠️ **These are the durable part; the entry's original prose definitions are superseded by them:** **(1) `rest` ALONE IS NOT COOKING** — all 11 of 11 rest-only components were dressings, tzatziki, olive salad and a buttermilk marinade CHILLING, which are this entry's own assembly examples; a rest still counts toward `craft` (a rise). **(2) ≤ 2 MINUTES OF HEAT IS NOT COOKING** (`HEAT_MIN_MINUTES = 3`) — all 79 of 79 were *stir in the spice blend / the dried herbs / the can of tomatoes / the broth*, tagged `cook` only because they happen in the pot. ⚠️ **Sensitivity, so the knob is visible: components with 1–2 heat-minutes = 82 · ≤ 3 = 106 · ≤ 4 = 135 · ≤ 5 = 171.** **(3) `craft` needs dough-craft TEXT** (knead / rise / proof / roll out / pasta sheets / tortilla press / cut butter into) **or a strict staple name on a path with heat or a rest** — *noodles* (boiling dried pasta), *garlic bread* and *tortilla strips* classify as `cooking`. The 17 craft are 13 dough (pizza ×10, naan, roti ×2), pierogi, gnocchi, dumplings and biscuit dough.
- ⚠️ **AND THE STRUCTURAL NOTE THAT MAKES THOSE REFINEMENTS CHEAP TO GET WRONG LATER: under the ruled grid, the ONLY boundary that changes a default is assembly-vs-not.** Level 1 makes all three classes; levels 2 and 3 both buy `cooking` AND `craft`. **So the cooking/craft split carries vocabulary and future flexibility, not behaviour — and the assembly boundary, which the two refinements move, is the one that decides what a level-2 user is handed.** Both refinements move components INTO assembly, i.e. **a level-2 user MAKES a chilled dressing and MAKES a two-minute spice stir-in** — which is what *"I can mix, measure, and cut"* says literally.
- ✅ **THE PROMPT VOCABULARY LANDED IN THE SAME COMMIT:** the generate prefix's *"a substitution replaces ASSEMBLY, never COOKING"* slogan and its self-contradicting example list are **replaced** (not layered) by the three classes, each with its own examples, plus the product-reality rule — *pre-sliced onions do not replace caramelized onions; a jar of caramelized-onion jam does.* **The TEST sentence is kept verbatim.** Real `count_tokens` on the cached system prefixes: **generate 4,532 → 4,931 · finalize 5,251 → 5,356.** ⚠️ **No reseed is owed for the store side — `storeFillPrompts.ts` is COMPILED TS passed as `cachedSystemPrefix`, and the seed bodies are bare `{{generateInput}}` / `{{finalizeInput}}`; `LLMCallLog.promptVersion` therefore does NOT move with a store prefix change and still reads 1. The cache invalidation is the only mark the edit leaves.** The wizard finalize / expand bodies were NOT touched (they carry no bought-path steps), so no `prisma:seed` is owed at all.
- 🔴 **THE QUALITY BAR (question 1) IS STILL UNENFORCED, WITH FRESH INSTANCES: the TEST sentence did not catch a bought path swapping one BOUGHT item for another** — potato buns → *"brioche burger buns"*, frankfurters → *"all-beef hot dogs"*, both authored September 15 under the new prefix. ⚠️ **AND THE CLAUSE ALREADY EXISTS IN CANON — IT NEVER REACHED THE PROMPT. D-WS9-064 states it verbatim:** *"it is not a substitution if you'd buy it either way — offering Italian sausage for ground beef has no store-bought-vs-scratch axis; that is a recipe variation in the wrong field."* **So the fix is a port, not a drafting exercise: carry that sentence into the store generate prefix beside the TEST sentence.** 🔴 **This is the THIRD time in one night that canon already held the answer and nobody searched it** (the store-prefix parity premise on D-WS9-239; this clause; and D-WS9-064's `substitutions` DIRECTION, which is D-WS9-243's whole cause). **§27.6 item 10's check is one `project_search` and it would have caught all three.** Catalog-quality follow-on, not commissioned.
- 🔵 **COPY DIRECTION FROM HANS (September 15) FOR THE THREE-OPTION PREFERENCE AND THE PER-COMPONENT TOGGLE — the benefit, not the mechanic:** *"buy the taco dinner kit to keep ingredients and measuring simple"* vs *"authentic at home flavors by creating the taco packet in your kitchen."* **Both paths are described by what the user GETS — simplicity on one side, flavor and authenticity on the other — and neither is framed as the lesser choice.** ⚠️ **This is the wording brief for D-WS9-065's rename and relabel and for BUG-121's toggle; it is NOT a new ruling and it does not change the grid.** ✅ **And it names the case this vocabulary must keep working: a spice packet is an ASSEMBLY component, so scratch stays the default and the kit stays the option — D-WS9-243 does not touch it.**

### D-WS9-241 — The auth surface, ruled as one: sign-up consents on the signup wire, a bootstrap that can fail visibly, the password-reset CLIENT, spend-guard copy that survives the client, and web token storage — ✅ RULED (chat-Claude's calls, licence to object), September 13, 2026

- **Raised:** September 13, 2026 (the read-only auth-surface Phase 0, run beside D-WS9-239 Phase 1a; it audited clean and refuted six of chat-Claude's claims — recorded below so nobody re-asserts them) · **Owner:** WS9A polish / auth · **Tags:** `[AUTH]` `[SECURITY]` `[WEB]` `[COPY]` `[GO-LIVE]` · **Status:** ✅ **RULED September 13, 2026 — five rulings A–E below, made as chat-Claude's calls under Hans's standing delegation; Hans objects if he disagrees.** ⚠️ **Nothing here is built. Three lanes carry it (sequence at the end).** · **Cross-ref:** BUG-235 (reset client — P1, beta blocker) · BUG-258 (blank bootstrap) · BUG-261 (consents not sent) · D-WS9-231 (the browser-completable reset page is the PRIMARY reset surface; this entry adds the in-app one) · D-WS7-025 (consent columns) · D-WS7-022 (email infra) · BUG-239 (SessionGate) · BUG-233/234 (single-use reset tokens, epoch).
- **What Phase 0 established, kept only as far as the rulings rest on it:** the server `signupSchema` is non-strict, so the consents and phone the sign-up form already collects are silently STRIPPED, not rejected · `PATCH /me/profile` already accepts phone and both consents (tested) · the bootstrap has three failure paths — `/auth/me` hangs → blank forever; throws → silent bounce to Welcome; `readToken()` rejects → uncaught → blank forever, **and that third path is exactly what the web target hits, because `expo-secure-store` ships a web stub that THROWS at call time** (it is not "missing a web build") · no reset-password client exists at all — no request screen, no confirm screen, no sign-in link, no wrappers · `SessionGate` evicts a logged-out user from every route outside `(auth)/` · the spend guard's server copy is overridden by canned client copy in more places than grocery, and the 502 branch discards it too.
- **Refuted by CC (do not re-assert):** "429/503 show NO copy" — they show generic wrong copy · "prep-week and the builders are fine" — they override copy · "`expo-secure-store` has no web build" — it has a throwing stub · "BUG-235 is just the confirm screen" — it is request + confirm + link · "all five share the auth surface" — the copy defect touches no auth file · a CC citation of D-WS7-144 as a copy-canonicality ruling — that entry is a resolved mapper-duplication, and nothing in canon blocks surfacing server copy.

**✅ A — Sign-up consents and phone go on the SIGNUP wire, server-side, one write.** Extend `POST /auth/signup`'s schema and its `user.create` with `phone` (optional), `marketingConsentEmail`, `marketingConsentSms`; the client sends what the form collects. **Rejected:** a second `PATCH /me/profile` call after signup — two writes, the second can fail silently, and a consent record that may or may not have landed is worse than none. Rules: phone optional · **SMS consent without a phone is refused (400) — a consent that cannot be honoured is not a consent** · the client mirrors the phone rule `PATCH /me/profile` already enforces (the SAME rule, not a second one). `PATCH /me/profile` stays the edit path. BUG-261 closes with this.

**✅ B — The bootstrap gets a deadline and a failure state.** `/auth/me` at bootstrap runs under a 10-second `AbortController`. Outcomes: **401** → the existing cascade (clear token → sign-in, expired message rendered; unchanged) · **timeout, network error, 5xx** → a failure screen, **token KEPT**: heading *Can't reach Kiwi*, body *Check your connection and try again.*, primary *Try again* (re-runs bootstrap), secondary *Sign out* (clears the token, Welcome) · **`readToken()` throws** → caught, treated as NO token → Welcome. **Rejected:** retry-forever with a spinner (the September 12 instance was a stopped api-server; a spinner would have spun all night) · auto-sign-out on a network failure (punishes a subway ride with a lost session). ⚠️ `app/**` is outside the test glob (D-WS9-164): the screen is device-verified; the timeout and the three branches get unit tests at the context/wrapper level. BUG-258 closes with this.

**✅ C — BUG-235 is THREE things and lives under `app/(auth)/`:** a request screen (`forgot-password`: email → `POST /auth/password-reset/request` → the anti-enumeration success copy regardless of outcome), a confirm screen (`reset-password`: opened by `kiwi://reset-password?token=…`, the link the Cloud Run page already emits; new password twice, min 8 / max 100 mirrored from `resetConfirmSchema`; `POST /auth/password-reset/confirm`), and a *Forgot password?* link on sign-in. Wrappers in a NEW `lib/api/passwordReset.ts` — deliberately not `lib/api/auth.ts`, so this lane and the auth-core lane are file-disjoint. Under `(auth)/` because the user is logged out by definition and `SessionGate` would evict the screen anywhere else; the group does not appear in the URL, so the deep link still resolves. **A signed-in user opening the link is redirected home by `(auth)/_layout` — accepted; they change their password from profile.** A 400 from confirm renders ONE invalid state (bad, expired, or already-spent — the server answers the same 400 for all three on purpose, BUG-233) with the page's copy minus "from the app", and a *Request a new link* action. Success → sign-in with an app-level toast (*Password changed. Sign in with your new password.*) — the route does not sign the user in, and it should not. **Rejected:** minting a session on confirm (a client-visible contract change the server comment already declines) · reusing `app/verify-email.tsx`'s root placement (it sits outside `(auth)/`; see the open question at the end).

**✅ D — For the three spend-guard reasons, SERVER COPY WINS EVERYWHERE.** Where the body carries `reason` ∈ {`spend_cap_user`, `spend_cap_global`, `ai_disabled`}, every client surface renders the server's message verbatim and keys on `reason`, not on status. Every other 502/429/503 keeps its local canonical copy — this ruling does not open the copy question generally. Surfaces Phase 0 named, each to be verified at build: `lib/api/grocery.ts` · `lib/api/recipeImport.ts` · `lib/groceryHandoff.ts` · `askKiwiSubmit.ts` · `askKiwiDishSubmit.ts` · `PrepWeekScreen.tsx`. Reason: the guard's copy tells the user WHAT happened (your daily allowance / Kiwi is paused / AI is off) and canned copy turns all three into "something went wrong" — the one message a spend refusal must not send. **No separate BUG entry — this ruling is the tracking record for the copy defect.**

**✅ E — Web token storage is `sessionStorage`, behind a platform branch in `lib/auth.ts`, native path untouched.** The three functions branch on `Platform.OS === "web"`; every web read/write is wrapped so a throwing or empty storage reads as "no token", which with B means Welcome, never a blank screen. Cost accepted: a web user signs in once per browser session. **Rejected:** `localStorage` — a 30-day JWT persisted where any injected script can read it, on an API that is now public, is the wrong default for a "quiet secondary surface" · in-memory only — a sign-in on every reload is too poor even for that surface · an httpOnly cookie — the right long-term answer and a server change (CSRF, cookie routes); **revisit if web becomes primary.** The reset flow on web is the Cloud Run page (D-WS9-231), not the Expo web app, so C's screens are native-first and merely must not break on web. **No separate BUG entry.**

- **Lanes, in order (Hans runs; one code-bearing server lane + one file-disjoint mobile lane at a time, §29.1):** **(1) BUG-235 client lane — NOW, mobile-only, beside D-WS9-239 Phase 1a**: new `app/(auth)/forgot-password.tsx`, new `app/(auth)/reset-password.tsx`, new `lib/api/passwordReset.ts` + its test, one link in `app/(auth)/sign-in.tsx`; touches nothing the 1a lane or the auth-core lane owns. **(2) Auth-core lane — A + B + E, after (1) commits**: `routes/auth.ts` (server), `AuthContext.ts`, `lib/auth.ts`, `app/index.tsx`, `app/(auth)/sign-up.tsx` and their tests; it needs a server slot, so it also waits for 1a to land. **(3) Error-copy lane — D, after (2)**: the six surfaces above, mobile-only. Each lane gets its own device script (§3.1); (1) and (2) each need a real login at item 1.
